vision: "Over the top" means SC2 Tools feels like one calm, trustworthy product rather than a pile of powerful parts. Nothing is broken: CTA labels stay visible, failed requests offer Retry instead of a false "no data", the desktop app never quits or hides failures, and backups really exist. Every number explains itself: each game is set against your own norm and your league, every timestamp moves the replay, every opponent arrives with a deterministic scouting brief, and every chart shows its sample size. Help is one click away and searchable, with an article for every feature, public for visitors and embedded in Settings > Help. Streamers get a studio that sets itself up, survives going live and never leaks the token. Everything is computed from replays with fixed rules and classic statistics (no AI, no model APIs), and server cost stays flat: work moves to the browser, the edge cache and R2.

waves.name: Wave 1 — Professional baseline: nothing broken, help one click away
waves.goal: Fix the global bugs that make the product look broken, give every feature a findable how-to, make every failure recoverable and reportable, make filters honest, restore dead live-scouting widgets, and make sure the database is backed up. All items are self-contained and low risk.

waves.name: Wave 2 — Connected and confident: pairing, desktop-app reliability, first run, data safety
waves.goal: Make the drop-off moments safe: pairing that cannot fail silently, a desktop app that explains itself, never quits and never costs FPS, and a resumable welcome flow. Add one notifications inbox with support replies and what's-new. Make snapshots, deletion and realtime correct and cheap on one server. One coordinated agent release ships with this wave.

waves.name: Wave 3 — Every game explains itself, every opponent is scouted
waves.goal: Make /app/game/[id] the one complete per-game workspace: a shared clock, benchmarks, supply build orders, smooth accurate playback and a deterministic game story. Use the scouting data the backend already computes in the live brief, the dossier and the desktop card. Add the veto planner, mobile opponents, game hygiene and a few analytics that are honest about sample size.

waves.name: Wave 4 — Stream Studio that sets itself up, and a practice loop that works everywhere
waves.goal: Get a streamer from sign-up to a correctly sized, healthy, restylable overlay in minutes, with a Dock that controls the game side, safe token rotation, richer chat and moments, and native Twitch predictions. Make practice one click from any build, sync it across devices and grade it privately. Unify the build editor and surface the dossier analysis the API already computes. Agent release 2 ships here.

waves.name: Wave 5 — Grow, include everyone, scale on one server
waves.goal: Turn every public page into a working acquisition path: return to context after sign-up, real share cards, edge caching, an in-browser landing demo, a shareable /try report and one public player page. Bring accessibility to WCAG AA with CI enforcement, add the missing UI primitives, glossary and find-anything. Cut server work with per-user caching and a local analysis corpus. Ship agent health and sync health so 'my game didn't show up' answers itself.

waves.name: Wave 6 — Bigger features: sessions, goals, notes, sharing, deeper analytics and power tools
waves.goal: Build the large features on top of the foundations: one session definition with session history and reports, goals, league targets, a unified notes system with a review queue, per-game share links, replay studio tools, unit trades, a private practice log and desktop HUD, build library safety, Discord, push notifications and the remaining polish.

items.title: Stop primary CTA labels vanishing on hover and focused pills turning square
items.why: The most-clicked conversion buttons ('Get started', 'Download the agent', 'Try again') go invisible on hover today. The fix is two lines.
items.spec: apps/web/app/globals.css: the unlayered `a{color}` and `a:hover{color}` rules (L215-220) beat `.text-white` on specificity, and `*:focus-visible{border-radius:4px}` is emitted after `.rounded-full`. Move both into `@layer base` with zero-specificity selectors: `:where(a){color:rgb(var(--accent))}`, `:where(a):hover{color:rgb(var(--accent-hover))}`, `:where(*):focus-visible{outline:2px solid rgb(var(--accent));outline-offset:2px}`. Drop the border-radius; outlines already follow the element's radius. No component edits. Audit nav links that relied on the accidental hover recolour (most already set hover:text-*). Tests: a Playwright check in tests/e2e/public-pages.spec.ts that hovers the header 'Get started' at 1280px and asserts the label's contrast against its background is at least 4.5:1. A vitest that compiles globals.css and fails on any unlayered element selector with a pseudo-class.

items.title: App shell fixes: mobile Save bar and safe areas, page titles, lighter bundles, correct PWA manifest
items.why: On phones the Settings Save button sits under the tab bar, iOS standalone puts the header under the notch, tabs share one title, and every section ships every other section's code.
items.spec:
1) Safe insets: AppChrome measures the mobile tab bar with a ResizeObserver and sets `--chrome-bottom` (tab-bar height plus env(safe-area-inset-bottom)) on <html>. SaveBar moves to z-50 and, together with Toast, the ServiceWorkerRegister update prompt and CookieBanner, uses `bottom: calc(var(--chrome-bottom,0px) + .75rem)`. The AppChrome context bar gets `pt-[env(safe-area-inset-top)]`. Do not apply this inside Modal (BuildEditorSaveBar) or on overlay or dock routes.
2) Titles: app/layout.tsx sets `title:{default:SITE_TITLE, template:'%s · SC2 Tools'}`; strip hand-written suffixes (SEO-tuned guide and stream-studio titles use `title.absolute`). Add server layout.tsx metadata for /settings, /coaching and /welcome; useDocumentTitle per Settings tab; generateMetadata for /app/game/[gameId] ('Defeat · PvZ on Alcyone'). Card gets a headingLevel prop.
3) Code splitting: SectionPanel.tsx and app/settings/page.tsx load each section or tab with next/dynamic, using the existing skeletons; Foundation stays eager. Fraunces gets `preload:false`. public/logo.png (2 MB) is replaced in the chrome by logo-64.webp/logo.svg. stream-backgrounds/source moves to apps/web/assets. Add a perf-budget.json check in web-ci.
4) Manifest: `id:'/app'`, `start_url:'/app?source=pwa'`, `orientation:'any'`, theme/background #06090e, and shortcuts for Today, Opponents, Replays and Stream settings. Offline shell and share target are deferred.
Tests: jsdom test that SaveBar uses var(--chrome-bottom); a test that every app/**/page.tsx resolves a non-default title; bundle budget in CI.

items.spec:
Data: apps/web/lib/help/articles/*.ts (one file per category: getting-started, desktop-app, analyzer, game-page, opponents, builds, stream-studio, account-data, troubleshooting). Routes: public /help hub (search, category cards, popular, 'Still stuck? Report a problem') and /help/[slug] via generateStaticParams, with canonical, FAQPage/HowTo JSON-LD and sitemap.ts entries. Keep them out of the middleware isProtected list.

items.title: Bring back live scouting intel: compute favourite opening, predictions, cheese and best answer from real games
items.why: The Fav Opening, Best Answer, Cheese and Scouting widgets and the voice readout are blank for every agent user. They read opponents.openings, which nothing writes (no `opening` producer in the agent's replay_pipeline.py).
items.spec:
API: add opponentTendencies(userId, identity, {myRace, oppRace, map}) to services/overlayLiveAggregations.js. It runs one indexed query on games by userId plus opponent.pulseId/pulseCharacterId, projecting date, map, races, opponent.strategy, result and OPP_INTENT_LABEL_PROJECTION (so check-in corrections count), sorted by date desc, limit 50. On the matchup subset it computes:
- favOpening {name, share, samples, of}
- predictedStrategies via the dossier's recencyWeightedStrategies, so overlay and dossier agree
- cheeseProbability: the recency-weighted share of games whose strategy scores at least 0.4 on the existing cheese classifier
- bestAnswer via _bestAnswerVsStrategy
Wire it into buildFromGame and buildFromOpponentName in place of the openings reads, inside the existing 5-minute enrichment cache. Add samples and window to the payload so widgets can say '3 of last 5'. Keep reading openings only for legacy rows. Stop computing last5GamesScouting in the live path (unused). ScoutingWidget renders opponentPhases as one footer line.
Community aggregateOpponent drops the openings section.
Tests: rows without `opening`, check-in-corrected strategies, a mixed-matchup opponent, cheese thresholds, cache key. CHANGELOG note that these widgets will now appear on stream.

items.title: Nightly off-site database backups to R2, a weekly restore drill, and honest backup copy
items.why: Production runs on free-tier Atlas, which has no backups, and no workflow dumps the database. Meanwhile Settings tells users 'Atlas takes daily continuous backups' (SettingsBackups.tsx:194). One mistake would lose the product.
items.spec:
1) .github/workflows/db-backup.yml: nightly cron at about 09:17 UTC plus workflow_dispatch. Runs mongodump with a read-only Atlas user (--gzip --archive), excluding ephemeral collections (site_presence, platform_webhook_receipts, multichat_engagement_events, jobLocks, browser_ingest_daily, build_intent_live, platform_oauth_states). Uploads to a private R2 bucket sc2tools-db-backups using a write-only token, then writes manifest/latest.json {at, sizeBytes, sha256, durationSec, counts}.
2) scripts/prune-backups.js keeps 7 daily, 4 weekly and 6 monthly.
3) A weekly restore-drill job restores into a mongo:7 service container and runs scripts/verify-restore.js (counts within 1%, sample docs parse, ensureIndexes succeeds). On failure it opens a GitHub issue via gh.
4) scripts/restore-user.js <archive> <userId> for single-user recovery.
5) GET /v1/admin/backups reads the manifest through the existing S3 client (10-minute cache). /admin/health gets a 'Database backups' card: age (green under 26 h, amber under 50 h, red above), size, counts and last drill. A stale backup raises an admin_events alert.
6) Fix SettingsBackups copy and app/legal/privacy to state the real schedule and the 6-month retention.
Tests: prune logic unit tests; verify-restore against a fixture dump.
items.howto: Runbook docs/runbooks/restore-database.md (full restore, single-user restore, token rotation), linked from the /admin/health card. User-facing: corrected text in the help article 'Backups, snapshots and export' (slug backups-and-export) and in the privacy page.

items.title: Desktop app: pairing never quits, codes refresh themselves, and an unlinked PC recovers in one click
items.why: Today the app closes itself after 10 minutes, or when the API is unreachable (flow.py POLL_TIMEOUT_SEC=600, runner.py request_quit). A PC unpaired on the website retries uploads forever.
items.spec:
pairing/flow.py: loop until stop_event, with no deadline. A failed start emits PairingUiState(kind='unreachable', retry_in) with 2→60 s jittered backoff and a retry_now Event. Request a fresh code when expiresAt is less than 60 s away; expose request_new_code(). Remove every request_quit from the pairing path.
Pairing card (gui.py _build_pairing_card):
- big code with an 'Expires in 7:42' countdown
- 'Get a new code' link
- primary 'Link this PC in your browser' button that opens {dashboard}/devices?code=…&src=agent
- Copy button
- unreachable state with 'Retry now'
- 'Need help?' link
Unlink recovery: api_client raises DeviceUnauthorized on 401 for device-token calls. An AuthWatchdog fed by heartbeat and upload queue waits for 2 consecutive 401s, then confirms with GET /v1/me/profile. It then clears state.device_token (keeping cursor and settings), holds the upload workers without dropping jobs, and calls _Multiplexer.on_unlinked(). The dashboard shows 'This PC was unlinked from your account' with 'Link again', which re-runs ensure_paired and rebuilds ApiClient and SocketClient in _RuntimeCell. start() sends {hostname, os, version}.

items.title: Desktop app: plain-language sync errors, real backoff, and a calm offline banner
items.why: One outage floods Recent uploads with 40 raw 'http_503' rows per retry and hammers the server every 2 s. The fixed time.sleep(2.0) in queue.py adds load to the single API exactly when it is struggling.
items.spec:
New sc2tools_agent/errors.py: classify(exc) → UserError(kind, title, detail, action, transient). Kinds: offline (ConnectionError/Timeout), server_busy (5xx, ReplayIngestBusy), rate_limited (429), signed_out (401/403), rejected (TerminalUploadError and API codes mapped to sentences), file (unreadable or still writing), unknown.
UploadQueue: transient failures no longer call _on_failure. They update on_connection_state(kind, since, next_retry_at, waiting_count). Replace the 2 s sleep with capped exponential backoff (2 s → 5 min, with jitter) per consecutive batch failure, reset on success. A heartbeat success sets a ConnectivityProbe Event that wakes waiting workers immediately. Live rank-0 jobs keep their lane.
UI: an offline or busy banner, 'Offline: 312 replays waiting, retrying in 30 s [Retry now]'. Recent rows appear only for terminal outcomes, with a friendly title, the technical detail in a tooltip and 'Copy details'. Tray toasts: one after 10 minutes offline with a backlog, and 'Back online: 312 replays synced' when it clears.
ImportController keeps its terminal-only on_failure contract.
Tests: classify() table; no failure callback on transient errors; backoff resets; probe wake.

items.title: Desktop app: relaunch brings the window back, tray and window agree, and every replay folder is found and labelled
items.why: Double-clicking the shortcut while the app runs does nothing visible. The tray can show the opposite pause state from the window, and players with a moved Documents folder or localised OneDrive see an empty agent.
items.spec:
1) Single instance: GuiUI.run starts a QLocalServer named with the instance_lock mutex digest (removeServer first). A second launch connects with QLocalSocket, sends {cmd:'show'} and exits 0; the first instance shows its window. Headless mode keeps the stderr message.
2) The first hide-to-tray shows a one-time toast 'Still running in the tray' (state.tray_hint_shown). With no tray available, close offers Quit or Minimize.

4) Tray 'Re-sync from scratch' opens the GUI confirm dialog. 'Check for updates' toasts its result.
5) Folders: replay_finder first resolves FOLDERID_Documents via SHGetKnownFolderPath (ctypes, guarded on non-Windows), then HKCU User Shell Folders\Personal, then looks one level deep under ~/OneDrive* for 'StarCraft II/Accounts'. Existing candidates stay as fallback. describe_folder(path) → FolderInfo(region via region_from_toon_handle, toon, replay_count, newest_mtime, exists).
Folder list rows read 'EU · 2-S2-1-… · 1,204 replays · newest 2 h ago', with the raw path as tooltip. Missing folders show amber 'Not found (external drive?)'. With no SC2 folder, show the empty state 'We couldn't find StarCraft II replays' with a 'Locate folder…' button.

items.title: Trustworthy installer: one startup switch, an options page, a clean uninstall and signed builds
items.why: 'Run on Windows startup' shows unchecked while the app autostarts, because the installer always adds a Startup shortcut. Unsigned builds also make users click through 'Unknown publisher'.
items.spec:
installer.nsi: the HKCU Run value is the only startup mechanism. An nsDialogs options page offers 'Start SC2 Tools when Windows starts' (default on) and 'Create desktop shortcut' (default on). It writes or deletes Run SC2ToolsAgent = '"$INSTDIR\sc2tools-agent.exe" --start-minimized'. On every install, delete the legacy $SMSTARTUP shortcut, migrating to the Run value first if it existed. Silent /S installs keep the existing choice. MUI_FINISHPAGE_RUN adds 'Launch now'.
Uninstall deletes the Run value and offers an opt-in checkbox (default off) to delete settings, pairing and logs: agent.json, player_handle.json, logs, data, streaming, replay-observations. Never replay folders.
autostart.is_enabled() also detects the legacy shortcut, and set_enabled migrates it.
Signing: add SignPath Foundation (free for OSS) or Azure Trusted Signing to agent-installer.yml. Sign the inner exe before NSIS and the setup exe after.
Tests: tests/test_autostart.py (legacy detection and migration); packaging smoke assertions.
items.howto: Help article 'Install, start-up and uninstall' (slug desktop-app-install), plus a matching expander on /download (DownloadInteractive.tsx). Update apps/agent/README.md and packaging/README.md.

items.title: Match-aware background work: imports and updates never cost you FPS or interrupt a game
items.why: A large history import runs up to 12 normal-priority workers (about 1.8 GB) during ladder games, and auto-update can restart the overlay bridge mid-match.
items.spec:
1) A shared GameActivityGate, subscribed to the live EventBus, is 'busy' during MATCH_LOADING, MATCH_STARTED and MATCH_IN_PROGRESS and frees 20 s after MATCH_ENDED, MENU or IDLE. Safety valves release it after 45 minutes, or after 2 minutes without live events. With --no-live it is a no-op.
2) watcher.py _make_parse_executor gets initializer _lower_worker_priority: BELOW_NORMAL via SetPriorityClass on Windows, nice(10) on POSIX. While busy, the history drain submits no new parses and the archive lane holds; rank-0 live replays are unaffected. Automatic replay capture never starts mid-match.
3) Settings 'Performance': Background import speed Gentle / Balanced / Maximum (workers 2 / min(4,cpu) / max, IDLE priority in Gentle), 'Pause history import while I'm in a game' (on), and 'Pause on battery'.
4) Updates: UpdateScheduler installs only when the gate has been free at least 2 minutes, no OBS output is live and no capture is running. Otherwise the card reads 'Will install after this match'. The update card shows 'Version X is ready · What's new ▸ · [Install now] [Later]', with notes rendered by QTextBrowser.setMarkdown. Later snoozes 24 h; mandatory updates defer at most 24 h. On boot, when state.last_run_version differs from __version__, toast 'Updated to vX' and offer What's new. A tray item 'Install update vX' appears when one is pending.
Tests: gate decision table from synthetic lifecycle events; scheduler matrix (in match, streaming, mandatory, snoozed).

augments.text: (1) Replay-capture announcements currently go through gui.show_update_notice(message, sticky=False) (runner.py:1297-1302). _set_update_notice (gui.py:1348-1356) replaces whatever is shown and clears it after 8 s, which silently erases a sticky update notice. Give capture and other transient notices their own transient line or toast so they can never touch the update card. (2) Remove the copy 'automatic install is turned off… Enable it in Settings or run the installer manually' (runner.py:1636-1640). Install now works with auto-update off via install_release (runner.py:1650-1657). (3) When an install fails, the card shows 'Update failed: <reason>' with Retry and 'Download installer', which opens {dashboard}/download. (4) Replace the disabled tray status line for updates (tray.py:289-292) with the 'Install update vX' item at the top of the menu. (5) Add a short 'Updates' paragraph to the desktop-app-updates help article covering the banner buttons and where the release notes are.

items.title: Resumable welcome wizard that knows where you are and ends with 'You're set'
items.why: A refresh restarts the wizard at Welcome, already-paired users are walked through pairing again, and nobody is told whether the agent really connected.
items.spec:
- The step lives in ?step=(welcome|download|pair|import|done) via router.replace, so Back and refresh work.
- On mount, read /v1/me: agentPaired jumps to import, games.total>0 jumps to done, and earlier progress chips are marked complete.
- The Welcome step asks 'What do you want from SC2 Tools?' with two toggle cards, Improve my play and Upgrade my stream. Save to onboarding.goals through PUT /v1/me/preferences/onboarding, merging existing fields.
- Download step: 'Already installed? Pair it now'.
- Pair step reuses PairDeviceForm with live confirmation.
- New Done step shows the connected device, live import progress (useImportStatus) and 2–3 goal-specific next actions, each linking a help article. For improve: 'Open your latest game', 'Check your identity'. For stream: 'Copy your first overlay URL', 'Open the crash course'.
- One consistent time promise in the copy; fix the '3-step' docstring.
- Tests: step resolution from /v1/me fixtures; goals saved without clobbering other onboarding fields.

augments.text: In browser mode (no agent), Back from Import must return to Download, not to the skipped Pair step. Today OnboardingShell.tsx:154-157 uses index-1 (see also app/welcome/page.tsx:59-69). Keep a visited-steps stack (or derive the previous step from the active path) and use it for both the Back button and ?step=. Make completed step chips clickable buttons (aria-current on the active one) so users can revisit a step. When /v1/me says agentPaired, show the Pair chip with a check mark and let 'Continue' skip it. Don't just jump past it silently. Fix the stale '3-step' doc comments at OnboardingShell.tsx:121 and :126.

items.title: Notification center for everyone: useful system events, mark-all-read, muting, and replies to your reports
items.why: The bell is hidden unless Reviews are enabled (NotificationBell.tsx:37-40), so imports finishing, required agent updates and bug-report answers reach nobody. Other items in this roadmap need a delivery channel.
items.spec:
1) Always enable the notifications router and bell for signed-in users. Review kinds still come only from Reviews.
2) Event-driven producers, no cron:
- import.done ('Import finished: 1,243 games added')
- agent.update_required (groupKey per version) when a heartbeat reports a version below minSupportedVersion
- community.vote (groupKey per slug per day, render '{n} upvotes on {build}')
- support.status and support.reply
3) Support loop: admin Messages gets status (new | looking | fixed | wontfix) and a Reply action that stores the reply and notifies the user. GET /v1/messages/mine returns the user's last 20 reports. Settings > Help gets a 'My reports' section.
4) UI: kind→icon map, relative time (fmtAgo), 'Mark all as read' using the existing POST read {all:true}, a 'See all' link to a new /notifications page (kind filter, cursor pagination), per-kind empty states.
5) Preferences: new 'notifications' PREF_TYPE {muted: string[]}. notify() skips muted kinds via a projection findOne. Per-kind toggles in Settings > Misc.
The bell stays hidden on token surfaces.
Tests: producers fire once (idempotent groupKey); muted kinds skipped; reply round-trip.

Today they have identical classes and only aria-pressed (~L276-281). Use a segmented control whose active option is visibly styled (bg-accent/15 text-accent) and keep aria-pressed. (2) Add focus-visible rings to the toggles, retry buttons, row links and Load more, per docs/design-system.md ~L263-268. (3) Opening the panel still POSTs read for the visible rows. Rows that were unread when the panel opened go into a per-open Set and keep a 'New' dot and the bg-accent/10 tint until the panel closes. (4) A header row with the title 'Notifications' and a 'Mark all read' text button, disabled when nothing is unread. (5) 'Today' / 'Earlier' group headings. (6) On open, move focus to the first row (or the header when the list is empty). Return focus to the bell on close, by Esc or by outside click. (7) When the unread-count request fails, keep the bell rendered with a muted state and a 'Couldn't load notifications · Retry' row. Today the bell returns null and disappears (~L246). Tests in components/notifications/__tests__/NotificationBell.test.tsx: active-toggle styling; the New dot stays after the read POST while the panel is open; focus moves in on open and back to the bell on close; the error state keeps the bell.

(1) Add the coaching producers in this item, not only in push-notifications-calendar. Write coaching.booked, coaching.cancelled, coaching.assigned and coaching.practice_sharing_* notifications from the existing emit points in apps/api/src/services/coaching.js (~L1001 assigned, ~L1162/1740 cancelled, ~L1671 booked, ~L756/881 practice sharing), with href /coaching and a groupKey per booking or share id so retries don't duplicate. push-notifications-calendar (W6) then only adds the push fan-out and the reminder job. Both chips switch to the bell's compact chip style (h-8, the same badge), so the context bar uses one visual language. items.title: What's New drawer, public /changelog with RSS, readable agent release notes, and an incident banner
items.why: Features ship weekly but users never hear about them. During an outage there is no way to say 'uploads are delayed, nothing is lost'.
items.spec:
1) lib/whatsNew.ts holds curated entries {id, date, title, summary, audience, highlights[], helpSlug?, agentVersion?, major?}. A test checks unique ids, descending dates and that every helpSlug resolves.
2) A Sparkles icon in the AppChrome context bar shows a dot when the newest entry is later than onboarding.whatsNewSeenAt. It opens a right sheet filtered by onboarding.goals; opening it writes whatsNewSeenAt. Major entries send one whats_new notification.
3) Public static /changelog (an anchor per entry, filter chips Agent / Website / Stream Studio / Guides, in the sitemap) plus /changelog/rss.xml.
4) /download: replace the raw <pre> (DownloadCard.tsx:110) with a safe Markdown subset renderer, components/ui/MiniMarkdown.tsx.
5) Incident banner: a site_config doc {_id:'banner', severity, message ≤240, href, startsAt, endsAt (required), audience}. Edited on /admin/announcements with live preview and templates (upload outage, maintenance, agent update required). Public GET /v1/site/banner (public, max-age 60, ETag) plus a site:banner socket broadcast. AppChrome renders components/ui/Banner (role=status, dismissible per message hash; critical banners cannot be dismissed). /v1/agent/version adds `notice`, shown by the agent tray and window.
Tests: whatsNew lint; banner expiry; MiniMarkdown escapes HTML.
items.howto: /changelog is self-describing. Help article 'Stay up to date' (slug stay-up-to-date: What's New, agent updates, checking your version). Runbook section 'Posting an incident notice' in docs/runbooks/admin-operations.md.

items.title: Snapshots that work at any size, a restore preview that keeps build orders and replays, and self-serve repair
items.why: A snapshot is one Mongo document, so it throws beyond about 5k games and fills the shared 512 MB. Restore silently deletes every build order and archived replay (gdpr.js:1147-1167). Users email support to fix inflated opponent counts.
items.spec:
Storage:
- Snapshots stream as gzip NDJSON into R2 at user-backups/{userId}/{id}.ndjson.gz (header line per collection, then cursor rows).
- user_backups keeps metadata only {id, type manual|auto|pre_action, label, createdAt, sizeBytes, counts}.
- Retention: 5 manual, 2 weekly auto (created lazily on the first ingest of an ISO week), 3 pre_action; oldest pruned.
- A one-off script migrates existing payload docs to R2.
Endpoints:
- DELETE /v1/me/backups/:id
- GET /:id/download (signed URL)
- GET /:id/preview → {games:{kept, removed, added}, customBuilds, opponentNotes, overlayTokens}
- PATCH label
Restore: keep game_details and replay files for gameIds present in both the snapshot and current data. Purge only those for games the snapshot lacks, and re-stamp replayFile markers after a batched HeadObject. Restore, wipe and repair each take an automatic pre_action snapshot first.
UI (SettingsBackups.tsx):
- Rows show label, type badge, count chips, Download, Delete and Restore.
- Restore is two steps: preview diff ('Build orders and replay files for 11,842 games are kept'), then confirm.
- Remove the false 'Atlas' and 'queued' copy.
Repair card: 'Recount opponent records' (POST /v1/me/repair/opponents runs rebuildOpponentsAndHealForUser, at most once an hour through a CAS on users.repairs, 202 then a notification), 'Re-check replay archive' and 'Re-run custom-build matching'. All respect the GDPR mutation fence.
Tests: intersecting and non-intersecting gameIds, the 16 MB case, the repair rate limit.
items.howto: Help articles 'Backups, snapshots and export' (slug backups-and-export) and 'Fixing wrong opponent counts' (slug repair-my-data), plus an inline 'What does restore change?' disclosure.

items.title: Account deletion that really ends the account
items.why: After DELETE /v1/me the Clerk session survives, and ensureFromClerk silently re-creates the user as a new signup. The user.deleted webhook is ignored, and multichat sounds and token-keyed viewer data are never purged.
items.spec:
API:
1) A GDPR_CLASSIFICATION map in gdpr.js covers every COLLECTIONS key: user_scoped | purge_only | overlay_token_scoped | global | ttl_ephemeral. A Jest test fails on any unclassified collection.
2) Before deleting overlay_tokens, collect the user's tokens and deleteMany({token:{$in}}) on multichat_studio, multichat_viewers, multichat_predictions and multichat_clip_moments. Purge multichat_sounds and export its metadata.
3) After the purge succeeds, call Clerk Backend deleteUser via clerkClient. Failures are retried by a pending_identity_deletions sweep (jobLock pattern).
4) Handle the user.deleted webhook idempotently with the same deleteAll.
5) GET /v1/me/data-inventory returns counts.
Web: a 3-step dialog.
- 'Download my data first' (GDPR export).
- An itemized list of what is removed vs anonymized ('[deleted user]' on review comments), with live counts.
- Type DELETE.
Then Clerk signOut to /goodbye, a page that confirms deletion and states the backup retention window.
Agent: a 401 from a deleted token shows 'This PC was unlinked', reusing agent-pairing-recovery.
Tests: the classification coverage test; token-scoped purge never touches other tokens; webhook plus API double-fire is idempotent.
items.howto: Help article 'Deleting your account' (slug delete-account). app/legal/privacy 'Your rights' is rewritten to list what is deleted and the backup retention window.

items.title: One socket per tab, an accurate 'games synced' count, and coalesced dashboard refreshes
items.why: A /app tab opens up to 7 Socket.IO connections, each one verifying a Clerk JWT. Every upload batch during a re-sync refetches every chart, and the header pill counts reclassifications as new games.
items.spec:
Web:
- A RealtimeProvider in AppShell owns one ref-counted socket using useUserSocket's token-callback auth and capped backoff. useUserSocket keeps its signature but subscribes to the shared socket, so call sites are unchanged. SyncStatus moves onto it.
- games:changed handling: 2 s trailing debounce, 10 s max wait. When bulk:true, or more than 3 events arrive in 10 s, refresh every 30 s and show a small 'Syncing — charts refresh every 30 s' chip.
- SyncStatus adds `inserted` instead of `count`, ticks its relative time every 30 s and shows the absolute time in a tooltip.
API: the games:changed payload becomes {count, inserted, bulk, reason}. Ingest computes inserted from upsert results, and bulk follows pickFreshOverlayGame. Reclassify (app.js:600) and build-intent (buildIntentCommon.js:193) send inserted:0 with a reason. Overlay token sockets are untouched.
Tests: adapted useUserSocket tests; one connection per tab; debounce; counter ignores inserted:0.

augments.text: (1) SyncStatus's private io() (components/SyncStatus.tsx ~L44-53) pins the token as auth:{token}. On the shared socket, use the per-reconnect token callback from lib/useUserSocket.ts ~L48-55. (2) Derive 'connected' only from the namespace 'connect' event, and treat 'connect_error' as not connected. SyncStatus currently sets connected on the Manager 'reconnect' event (~L68-70), which fires before namespace auth, so it can show 'Live' while receiving nothing. (3) The provider exposes the connection state as {status:'connecting'|'connected'|'reconnecting'|'offline', attempts}. The agent pill pack (chrome-nav-polish-3) reads it. (4) Mount it for signed-in users in both shells (AppChrome and the marketing shell) and never on /overlay or /dock. useUserSocket falls back to its own socket when no provider exists (tests, token surfaces). (5) The 'one connection per tab' test must mount every current consumer: SyncStatus, NotificationBell, CoachingBookingAlert, BuildCheckInProvider, AnalyzerProvider, AnalyzerFrame and useImportStatus. (6) Record the root cause in a code comment: socket.io-client 4.8.1 creates a new Manager whenever the '/' namespace is already cached, so per-mount io(API_BASE) calls never share a connection.

Bring the admin socket under the one-socket rule. Today AdminShell (components/AdminShell.tsx:262-267), the Dashboard (app/admin/page.tsx:55-69) and Notifications (notifications/page.tsx:56-71) each call useAdminEventsSocket, and each call opens its own io(API_BASE) (useAdminEventsSocket.ts:37-53). An admin tab can therefore hold up to three extra websockets besides the user socket. The server already puts every Clerk-authenticated admin socket in the 'admin' room (apps/api/src/socket/auth.js:451), so the shared RealtimeProvider socket receives admin:event without server changes. Make useAdminEventsSocket(onEvent, onConnected) a thin subscriber of the shared socket with the same signature. Keep the onConnected-on-connect/reconnect callback, because pages refetch durable rows then; admin events are not replayed. Expose connection status from RealtimeProvider ('live' | 'reconnecting' | 'offline', plus lastConnectedAt). Add components/AdminLiveStatus.tsx with three states, each shown as text and not only as colour: '● Live'; '↻ Reconnecting…' with a 'Refresh' button that calls the page's mutate(); and 'Offline · updated 12s ago'. Show it in the Notifications header actions and in the header of the Dashboard's 'Recent activity' card. Notifications should only promise 'Updates in real time' while the status is live. Tests: with AdminShell, Dashboard and Notifications mounted, io() is called exactly once per tab; admin:event fans out to every subscriber; onConnected fires on reconnect; the pill renders all three states.

items.title: Retire the unused server-side ML endpoints and slim the API's Python image
items.why: Any signed-in user can start a CPU-heavy scikit-learn training run on the single instance (routes/ml.js, mounted in app.js), yet nothing calls it. The image installs sklearn, pandas, matplotlib and flask for nothing.
items.spec:
1) Delete services/ml.js, the mlTraining capacity snapshot and scripts/ml_cli.py. Replace routes/ml.js with a stub that returns 410 Gone for one release.
2) Move analytics/win_probability.py and clustering.py to apps/replay-engine/legacy/ (excluded from the image) or delete them.
3) Add a forward-only migration that drops ml_models and ml_jobs, and remove both from gdpr.js.
4) Split requirements-server.txt (sc2reader, numpy, scipy for spatial KDE) from requirements-desktop.txt; the API Dockerfile installs only server.
5) CI guard fails when sklearn, torch or transformers appear in the API image dependencies.
6) CHANGELOG 'Removed'.
The on-device multichat translation (lib/multichat/localTranslate.ts) is out of scope: keep, opt-in or remove is the owner's call.
Tests: 410 stub; the image build passes the spatial_cli smoke test.

items.title: Make widget Test safe while you're live
items.why: Test broadcasts 'TestOpponent' to sources that are on air, and Stop calls overlay:clear, which wipes the real opponent card and session HUD until the next push.
items.spec:
Client (OverlayClient.tsx, OverlayWidgetClient.tsx): payloads flagged isTest go into a separate testLive state rendered above the real state, expiring after TEST_DURATION_MS. Expiry or Stop restores real live/liveGame/session untouched. overlay:clear carries {scope:'test', widget}; clients treat a missing scope as test only.
Server (routes/overlayTokens.js test route): check LiveGameBroker.latest(userId). During match_loading or in progress, return 409 live_match unless {force:true}. Settings then confirms: 'You're in a game — viewers will see sample data for about 20 s' with 'Send anyway' and 'Preview here instead' (opens the widget page in a new tab with ?demo=1 until widget-playground ships).
Tests in components/overlay/__tests__: Stop during a live payload keeps opponent and session visible; the 409 path.
items.howto: Add a live-game note to step 3 of the help article 'OBS overlay setup' (slug obs-overlay-setup). Update the StuckWidgetHelp text and the LearnTroubleshooting item 'Test works, but a real game shows nothing' in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts.

items.title: Ops console: background-job history, admin audit log, per-user support view, activation funnel
items.why: About 15 setInterval jobs record no run history, so silent failures go unseen. Destructive admin actions leave no audit trail. Onboarding drop-off is visible only through consent-gated GA.
items.spec:
1) util/jobLedger.js instrumentJob(name, intervalMs, tick) writes best-effort to a capped job_runs collection (about 5k docs): {job, startedAt, durationMs, status ok|error|lock_held|disabled, summary, errorCode}. It never throws into the job. /admin/health 'Background jobs' table: last ok, last error, duration sparkline, next due, env flag, and 'Run now' for jobs that expose runOnce, respecting single-flight. A job overdue by 3 intervals raises an admin_events alert.
2) admin_audit collection (400-day TTL), written by audit(req, action, target, result) in every admin mutation. New /admin/audit page with filters. Add a revoke-admin endpoint that cannot revoke yourself or the last admin.
3) Admin user detail 'Support snapshot': devices (version, online), doctor output (move the builder from me.js into a service), replay-archive counts, last 5 import_jobs and recent audit rows.
4) /admin/analytics 'Activation' tab: GET /v1/admin/activation?weeks=8 (cohort cap 2k, 1 h cache) returns signups → download → paired → first game → 10 games → week-2 return per signup week, plus median hours to pair and to first game, and a stalled-users list.
5) Swap the hand-rolled admin tool buttons for Button and ConfirmDialog.
Tests: the ledger never throws; audit is written on wipe; activation math on fixtures.

augments.text: ops-console part 5 ('swap the hand-rolled admin tool buttons for Button and ConfirmDialog') reworks the same files, so it must also include the following. (1) New apps/web/app/admin/components/UserLookupField.tsx: a debounced (300 ms) combobox over GET /v1/admin/users?search= (role=combobox with a listbox; arrow keys, Enter and Esc) whose options show email, userId, games, opponents and last activity. Choosing an option resolves to a user chip, and pasting an exact userId auto-resolves. items.title: Accurate playback that just works: guided upgrade, prefetched segments, no blanking, ready notification
items.why: The best replay feature hides behind a plain button and a 60-word paragraph, then blanks the whole stage every game-minute while the next chunk downloads.
items.spec:
Guided flow:
- refreshControl becomes a PlaybackFidelityCard: a badge ('Standard' / 'Recorded playback') with an 'Upgrade' action.
- It shows agent presence and a stepper: Requested → Recording in StarCraft (mm:ss) → Uploading → Ready.
- useMapReplay exposes a typed `phase` alongside the existing messages.
- A 'What happens?' disclosure keeps the CPU note and links agent Settings → Map replay.
- When a website-requested artifact upload completes, the API emits notification kind 'playback_ready' ('Accurate playback ready: PvZ on Alcyone', groupKey gameId). It fires at upload completion, not from viewer polling.
Smooth:
- SegmentedReplayHost prefetches index+1 when t > end − max(8, 3×speed) s (and index−1 after a backward seek), each with its own AbortController.
- The cache becomes byte-budgeted (about 24 MB) instead of 3 entries.
- A cached switch shows no overlay. On a miss, keep the last frame and show a corner spinner (role=status). The full overlay is only for first load and errors.
- Accumulate a game-wide cast-marker index across decoded segments.
API: segment routes send 'private, max-age=604800, immutable' (content-addressed); manifests stay no-store.
Tests: no overlay on in-cache transitions; prefetch aborted on seek; the notification fires once.

items.title: Game story for every result: lead timeline, turning points and a fight ledger you can watch
items.why: Wins get a filler 'Result' card, and fights appear only as dashed lines, even though exact casualty_events are already on the page.
items.spec:
lib/gameStory.ts is pure, deterministic and unit-tested like lossAutopsy. It does not use win_probability.py, /v1/ml or any model. Inputs: stats_events, opp_stats_events, casualty_events, build events. Outputs:
- leadSeries (army, worker and income lead per sample)
- top 3 turningPoints (largest 30 s swings in combined lead)
- fights: casualty_events clustered by gaps of 10 s or less, each with per-side minerals/gas/supply lost, top units lost, trade ratio, an outcome label ('Won trade 2.1×' / 'Even' / 'Lost trade') and duration
- template recap sentences picked with fnv1a ('You led in workers from 4:10 and never gave it back')
GameStoryCard replaces the static Result card; on losses it sits in tabs next to LossAutopsyCard. It shows a diverging lead strip (tokens, not hex), turning-point chips, and a FightLedger table (time · duration · your losses · their losses · outcome · ▶ Watch through the game clock), as cards on mobile. Wins also show 'still cost you' (the top leak). Without casualty_events it falls back to detectBattles, labelled 'estimated'. Copy says 'largest swing', never claims causation.
Tests: golden fixtures; clustering edge cases (long fights, harass).

augments.text: The win recap must include the peak army lead and when it happened, the moment you overtook in workers, the count of fights won and lost, and supply-blocked time against the threshold, each as a chip that seeks the shared clock. Ties and draws, which today show a bare 'The loss autopsy only runs on defeats.', get the same card. If nothing stands out, drop the placeholder and let Mechanics take the full row width.

items.title: Alt-account-aware live scouting and an explainable, deterministic opening forecast
items.why: An opponent queuing on a linked alt reads as 'first meeting', and 'Likely next' shows a bare 100% from a single game.
items.spec:
Linked identity:
- After matching oppRow in the live path, resolve the group from an approved player_identities groupKey and the cached pulseCharacterLinks accountId (cache only, no upstream calls).
- Load siblings with {userId, pulseCharacterId:{$in}} capped at 20, sum H2H, and pass the merged ids into recentGames and tendencies.
- Add alsoPlaysAs[] and mergedAccounts to the payload, and include the group key in the enrichment cache key.
- Persist the groupByPlayer preference server-side (it is in localStorage today).
- ScoutingWidget and the brief show an 'also: Name2' chip.
Forecast (services/openingForecast.js, pure, no ML, does not reuse /v1/ml or win_probability.py):
- Matchup-scoped strategy pseudo-counts with exponential recency decay (half-life 8 games), ×1.5 for the current map.
- A Dirichlet prior from the ladderMeta distribution for the matchup and MMR band at α=3 pseudo-games, falling back to no prior.
- Normalised top 3 with effective n, a confidence label (Low <3, Medium 3–7, High ≥8) and count-only 'why' bullets ('3 of last 5 vs you', '2 of 2 on Alcyone', 'Ladder at ~4.2k: 18%').
- Used by the dossier's PredictedStrategiesList (confidence chip plus a 'How is this calculated?' popover), the live enrichment and the agent brief, so every surface agrees.
Tests: golden files for the forecast; alt merge via accountId; preference off.

items.title: Opponent dossier: a 10-second brief, section nav, opponent key timings, phases, and honest error states
items.why: Users scroll past identity panels to reach the answer. API-busy errors show as 'Opponent not found'. Key timings, phases and transitions are computed on every view, and up to 100 detail blobs are hydrated, but nothing renders them.
items.spec:
PR A, brief and layout:
- Pure lib/scoutingBrief.ts buildScoutingBrief(profile) returns at most 6 lines: last met, record and streak, likely opener with n, best build vs them (BuildMatrix cell with ≥2 games), best and worst maps, usual end phase, and the lib/grudge.ts storyline.
- ScoutingBriefCard at the top next to notes, with 'Copy brief'.
- Sticky chip nav: Brief · Tendencies · Timings · History · Ladder · Identity.
- The identity submission, candidates and diagnostics panels go into one collapsed 'Identity & data quality' card that auto-opens for unrevealed barcodes.
- States: 404 'Not in your history'; 503 opponent_profile_busy auto-retries with backoff ('Analyzing… retrying'); network errors get Retry.
- Show the community link only when the response's cached communityAvailable is true.
PR B, timings and phases:
- Split the endpoint. GET /v1/opponents/:id stays cheap with no detail hydration. New GET /:id/analysis returns timings, phases and transitions under the same admission gate, fetched when those sections scroll into view and SWR-cached. Drop gamesScouting from the default response.
- OpponentKeyTimings card: matchup pills; per token an icon, median, a p25–p75 bar on a 0–10:00 axis, n, last seen, trend arrow, and win rate when built; clicking a row filters the history.
- Reuse PhaseTrajectoryStrip, PhaseCompositionTabs and BuildTransitionSankey unchanged.

items.title: Your data, your rules: hide or delete one game, filter by your own account, and export CSV
items.why: One friend-played or bugged game pollutes stats, and the only fix is wiping a date range. A finished filter-aware CSV export (GET /v1/export.csv) has no button.
items.spec:
API:
- PATCH /v1/games/:id {excluded, reason} and DELETE /v1/games/:id. Delete reuses the gdpr.js wipe helpers for a single id (row, details, R2 replay, playback artifacts), closes active reviews and writes a tombstone {userId, gameId, deletedAt}.
- Ingest and /games/exists honour tombstones, so nothing re-imports the game.
- gamesMatchStage defaults to excluded != true (include_excluded=1 for the hidden list). The same guard goes into overlayLive, opponent counters and guide-sample corpora.
- After a change, recount only the affected opponent.
- `accounts=<toon,…>` maps to myToonHandle $in.
- CSV: Excel-safe cells (prefix ' before = + - @), UTF-8 BOM, added columns myMmr, matchup, region, effectiveBuild and gameUrl, an X-Export-Truncated header, and a rate limit of 1 per minute per user.
Web:
- Game header overflow menu and Replay Library bulk select offer 'Hide from stats' (reason chips: friend played, disconnect/bug, off-race practice, other) and 'Delete game…' (typed confirmation that lists what is removed).
- FilterBar 'Account' picker ('Main · EU · Master'), hidden when the user has one account.
- Replays toolbar 'Export CSV' uses the current filters (authenticated fetch to Blob) and states the 50k cap.
- Settings > Backups & data gets a 'Hidden games' list with Unhide.
Tests: a seeded excluded game is ignored by every endpoint; tombstone blocks re-ingest; the CSV injection guard.

items.title: Strength-adjusted win rates: actual vs expected wins, performance rating and confidence ranges
items.why: Raw win rate can't tell a good build from one that met weaker opponents. There are no expected-win or Wilson ranges anywhere in the personal analyzer.
items.spec:
A nightly job (leaguePercentiles pattern, jobLock, aggregate-only) bins corpus 1v1 games by (oppMmr − myMmr) into 25-MMR bins from −600 to +600, smooths monotonically (pool adjacent violators) with n≥200 per bin, and stores the result in mmr_expectation. Until then it falls back to the standard Elo logistic curve with a documented scale.
API helper expectedWin(diff). Builds, strategies, maps and matchup aggregations gain:
- expectedWins (Σp)
- winsAboveExpected
- perfRating: avg oppMmr plus the offset whose expected rate equals the observed rate, by inverse lookup
- a Wilson 95% range
- excludedNoMmr count
Web:
- A sortable 'vs expected' column with ± chips and a tooltip spelling out the arithmetic.
- A faint range bar in win-rate cells and a 'thin sample' badge under 10 games.
- A Trends 'Matchup rating' card with PvP/PvT/PvZ performance-rating sparklines over the last 50 games.
- Copy says 'given who you played', never 'prediction'.
Team and vs-AI games are excluded.
Tests: calibration fallback; inverse lookup; excluded counts.

'Update my scenes' only adds what is missing and never removes or reorders. Skip any item whose URL already exists with the same token, to avoid double voice audio.
Part B (web+api+agent): an 'Add to OBS' button on widget cards calls authed POST /v1/devices/obs/add-source {widget}. The cloud emits obs:add-source to the online agent, which asks for confirmation in the tray ('Add Opponent identity to scene X?'). On yes it creates the source at the recommended size in the current program scene and acks; the website shows a toast. The button is disabled with a reason when no agent is online.
Tests: plan_scenes invariants; skip existing; a remote add without local confirm is rejected.
items.howto: Update docs/obs-auto-scene-switching.md §5/§7, the help article 'OBS auto scene switching' (slug obs-auto-scene-switching), and the CrashCourse 'build-your-scene' step 'Let the app build it'.

items.title: Overlay health board: see which OBS sources are live, per widget, before going live
items.why: Streamers guess why a card never appeared, and duplicate sources (which double voice and alerts) can't be detected.
items.spec:
Every overlay client handshake adds auth.surface ('all-in-one'|'widget'|'scene'|'dock') and auth.widget, validated in socket/auth.js against KNOWN_WIDGETS/VALID_SCENES and stored on socket.data.
Authed GET /v1/overlay-tokens/:token/presence uses io.in('overlay:'+token).fetchSockets() (in memory, no DB, single instance). It returns counts per surface and widget with the oldest connectedAt, agent online state and the last overlay:live time, rate-limited to 1 request per 5 s per token. Only counts are returned, never socket ids.
Settings widget cards show 'In OBS ×N' (green), 'Not added' (grey) or 'Duplicate audio' (amber). A 'Ready to go live?' checklist (agent, game overlay, chat, dock) polls every 15 s while visible. The Dock header gets a counts-only status strip. Older cached pages show as 'unknown source'.
Tests: counts by surface; rate limit; duplicate detection.
items.howto: Help article 'Is my overlay ready?' (slug overlay-health). It becomes the first step of LearnTroubleshooting and of the CrashCourse 'test-with-purpose' lesson.

items.title: Widget playground: preview every widget, theme and scenario in the browser, never on air
items.why: Right now the only way to see most widgets is Test, which broadcasts to OBS, and the learn page shows static screenshots that can't reflect the 10 theme presets.
items.spec:
Shared <WidgetPlayground>: a grouped widget list and a 16:9 checkerboard stage (reusing CHECKERBOARD/PREVIEW_CSS). The side panel has theme presets plus scenario chips (Pre-game, Victory, Defeat, Cheese, Hot streak, Chat burst, Poll) and a 'Show all together' view.
Fixtures move to apps/web/lib/overlaySamples.json, read by both the API test route and the client so they never drift. Widgets that fetch for themselves (multichat, chat-oracle, supporter wall, build profile, stats ticker) get a `demo` prop that makes no network calls.
Mount points: a Preview button on each Settings widget card (Modal), a lazy-loaded section on /stream-studio, and WidgetExplorer rendering the live component with the webp kept as a no-JS fallback. 'Preview here instead' from safe-test-fire opens it.
Tests: demo mode never calls the API (mocked fetch asserts zero calls); fixture parity.
items.howto: CrashCourse lesson 'test-with-purpose' step 1 becomes 'Preview in the playground, then Test in OBS' (lib/streamStudioLearn.ts). A note in 'OBS overlay setup' (slug obs-overlay-setup).

items.title: Safe overlay token rotation and real multi-token management
items.why: A leaked overlay URL has no safe fix. Revoking orphans viewer XP, oracle scores, goals and b-roll, and extra tokens never show their URLs.
items.spec:
Authed POST /v1/overlay-tokens/:token/rotate:
1) Mint a new token with the same label, enabledWidgets and profile.
2) Copy the studio doc.
3) Re-key engagement rows idempotently with batched updateMany {token:old}→{token:new}. Audit multichat sound and alert-media references too.
4) Revoke the old token.
5) Emit overlay:config {replacedBy:true} to the old room. Open sources show 'This overlay URL was replaced — update it in OBS' instead of going blank.
The agent picks up the new token on its next config fetch and runs the existing non-destructive repair to rewrite generated source URLs.
Settings: a token switcher (which token's URLs are shown), inline rename, 'Rotate' as the primary action with a checklist of what moves, and 'Revoke' as a danger action warning that viewer XP is lost.
Tests: each step retryable; no data lost on partial failure.
items.howto: Help article 'My overlay URL leaked' (slug overlay-url-leaked). A rotation note in docs/CLOUD_SCHEMA.md.

items.title: Chat commands v2: richer SC2 stats commands plus streamer-defined custom commands
items.why: Viewers on Kick, YouTube and TikTok have no bot. Only 4 fixed commands exist, cooldowns are hard-coded, and nothing can be renamed or disabled.
items.spec:
One registry, api/src/services/chatCommands.js, is used by twitchChatBot, a generic GET /v1/chatbot/:token/:command (Nightbot), and a new /v1/multichat/:token/command behind useCommandAnswers.
New deterministic lines in ChatbotService: !record (today's W-L by matchup), !winrate [matchup|race] (30 days and season, with n), !streak, !lastgame, !h2h (current or last opponent, plus last 3 meetings), !peak (season, region-aware), !oracle (top 3), !uptime.
Custom commands in prefs {trigger, response, enabled, cooldownSec, platforms[], answerOnStream}, max 25. Whitelisted variables {user} {mmr} {record} {opponent} {streak}. Plain text only, clipped by clip(), with per-command and per-viewer cooldowns.
Settings 'Chat commands' table: toggle, alias, cooldown, 'Try it' (shows the exact reply) and 'Copy Nightbot snippet'. commandsGuide and the copy-for-bio text are generated from the registry.
Tests: registry parity across the three endpoints; cooldowns; no HTML.
items.howto: ChatCommandsCard and the help article 'Viewer engagement' (slug viewer-engagement) read the registry. New help article 'Custom chat commands' (slug custom-chat-commands) with a variable reference.

items.title: SC2 moment alerts: MMR milestones, new peak, promotion, revenge and giant-killer wins
items.why: Ladder achievements are the most clip-worthy moments on an SC2 stream, yet the alert system knows only platform events.
items.spec:
services/gameMoments.js runs from the existing post-ingest overlay emit in routes/games.js. Deterministic rules:
- crossedMmrMark (every 100 or 250, configurable)
- newSeasonPeak (region-aware, tickerFacts guard)
- leagueChange
- winStreak 5/10
- lossStreakBroken (after ≥4)
- revengeWin (beat the opponent who won the last meeting)
- giantKiller (opp − my MMR ≥ 200)
- marathonWin (≥25 min)
- streamerOpponentWin (approved player channel)
Every rule is a no-op on null values. Dedupe per gameId, skip isResumedFromReplay, never fire twice on reprocess.
Emits overlay:moment {kind, headline, detail, gameId}. ChatAlertsWidget renders moments through the existing presets under a new 'Ladder' category at lower priority than subs and raids. Optional bot post. DockClips logs each moment.
Settings 'Game moments' block in SettingsMultiChatAlerts: per-moment toggle, preset, sound and Test, stored in multichat prefs.
Tests: each rule on fixtures; dedupe; null MMR.
items.howto: Help article 'Game moment alerts' (slug game-moment-alerts) under Viewer engagement. A 'Game moments' paragraph and Test step in the lib/streamStudioLearn.ts chat-alerts guide.

items.title: Native Twitch Predictions and per-game stream markers, driven by the live game
items.why: Crystal Ball already has the right lifecycle (opens at loading, locks, settles on the verified replay), but Affiliates can't use Twitch's native channel-points Predictions or markers.
items.spec:
A 'Twitch automation' card in Settings → Overlay → Chat & alerts, enabled only for affiliate or partner broadcasters. Consent is incremental: a new scopesForPurpose purpose adds channel:manage:predictions. Markers reuse the already-granted channel:manage:broadcast.
Toggle 'Open a Prediction at the loading screen'. Window 30–300 s (default 120). Title template 'Will {me} beat {opp} ({oppRace} {oppMmr})?'. Outcomes Win/Loss. Ranked 1v1 only; skip rematches within 10 minutes.
Server: on a match_loading envelope, POST helix/predictions. On the verified result (the same ingest hook that settles Crystal Ball), PATCH RESOLVED. Games under 60 s, no result within 20 minutes, or a Dock cancel → CANCELED (refund). State is stored in a TTL collection {userId, gameKey, predictionId, status} for crash recovery, one per game. Offline channels and 403 get a clear status.
Toggle 'Add a stream marker at each game start' (POST helix/streams/markers, 'vs Opp · PvZ · Map').
The Dock shows the prediction state with Resolve and Cancel.
Tests: lifecycle state machine; refund paths; scope reconnect.
items.howto: New Stream Studio Learn guide id 'twitch-predictions' in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts. Help article 'Viewer engagement' (slug viewer-engagement) section #twitch-predictions.

items.title: Series mode for cups and showmatches: best-of scoreboard, map list, automatic scoring
items.why: Every widget is built for ladder sessions, so cup and showmatch streamers edit text sources by hand mid-series.
items.spec:
Dock 'Series' panel with:
- opponent (prefilled from live or last, or typed)
- format Bo1/3/5/7
- optional map list from /v1/seasons mapPool or free text
- Start/End
- manual +1/−1
A streamSeries doc per overlay token {format, opponentName, opponentToon?, maps[], score, games[], status, startedAt}. On ingest, a game counts when it started after startedAt and the opponent matches (toon handle first, then case-insensitive name), whatever the ladder/custom flag. The server emits overlay:series. Test-fire never mutates a series.
New 'series' widget: names, race icons, score pips, current and next map, lifetime H2H. Plus a 'Series won/lost' moment, a slot in the All-in-one layout, and a !series chat line ('Bo5 vs Clem: 2–1, next map Alcyone').
Tests: matching rules; manual correction; completion.
items.howto: Widget guide 'series' in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts (/stream-studio/learn), a Dock tooltip, and the help article 'Series mode' (slug series-mode).

items.title: Desktop app: stream titles with live stat tokens that refresh after each game
items.why: Titles are static today. 'GM grind | {mmr} MMR | {record} today' would stay accurate with no effort and draws directory clicks.
items.spec:
The Streams page title field accepts tokens {mmr} {league} {record} {wins} {losses} {streak} {peak} {wr:PvZ}, with a live preview line and an inline token reference.
Option 'Refresh after each game': default on for Twitch and Kick, off for YouTube (videos.update costs 50 quota units). It runs on the game-ended lifecycle at most every 10 minutes and only when the rendered text changes.
Values come from the cloud session endpoint the agent already authenticates against. Render, validate with shared_title (1–70 chars), and drop optional segments rather than cutting mid-word. Results show in the existing per-platform verified/accepted status. Runs on its own thread, so it never blocks uploads.
Tests: render and truncation; throttle; unchanged text skipped.
items.howto: Inline token reference on the agent Streams page, plus the help article 'Stream titles' (slug desktop-stream-titles). Agent CHANGELOG.

items.title: Synced practice targets and a 'Practice this' button on every build page
items.why: Ghost targets live only in one browser's localStorage and the widget URL fragment, so streamers must re-copy URLs after every change, and grades appear only in the browser that armed the target.
items.spec:
API:
- New 'ghost' PREF_TYPE. services/ghostConfig.js mirrors normalizeGhostBuildConfig (v2, ≤9 slots, ≤80 steps, name caps, ≤64 KiB), with a JSON fixture parity test against lib/ghostBuild.ts.
- resolveGhostPrefs in socket/auth.js adds `ghost` to overlay:config and re-emits it on preference change, to the owner's tokens only.
Web:
- lib/ghostBuild.ts read/writeSynced on SWR /v1/me/preferences/ghost; localStorage becomes an offline cache.
- A one-time 'Move this browser's assignments to your account' banner (GhostLegacyMigration pattern).
- GhostBuildWidget prefers the socket config and falls back to the #ghost fragment, so old URLs keep working. The Settings Ghost row presents the URL as permanent.
- components/practice/PracticeButton.tsx is a split button, 'Practice in PvZ', with a menu to assign a matchup slot or open settings. It goes in the BuildCard kebab, BuildDetailView header, BuildDossierModal, the community build aside, BuildHero/GuideCtas (replacing the localStorage-only arm) and definition cards that have a guide.
- Step source order: the reference build order, then the source game's log via fromBuildLog, then rule deadlines as checkpoints.
- App-chrome chip 'Practicing: <build> (PvZ)' with quick disarm.
Tests: parity fixtures; fragment fallback; socket wins only when present.
items.howto: Help article 'Practice a build with Ghost Build' (slug practice-ghost-build). Update the ghost-build entry in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts so setup and troubleshooting no longer say to re-copy the URL.

items.title: One build editor with a 'Start from…' chooser and a searchable unit, building and upgrade picker
items.why: 'New build' opens a legacy free-text sheet while 'Edit' opens the rich editor. Rule names are free text typed as internal tokens ('BuildStargate') with no validation.
items.spec:
'New build' opens a Start-from modal with four cards:
- From one of my games: GET /v1/games filtered by matchup and label, then /build-order, then BuildEditorModal seeded like 'Save as new build'.
- From a detected build: a catalog label with name, race and vs-race prefilled, then pick a game classified as it ('Make my own variant' from /definitions lands here).
- From a pasted build order: enabled once reference-build-order ships.
- Blank.
Every path lands in BuildEditorModal. Retire BuildEditorSheet for rule editing: signature builds open in the modal through EditCustomBuildLauncher.docToEvents, and BuildDetailView always uses the launcher.
New components/ui/Combobox.tsx (ARIA 1.2, keyboard, icons). TokenPicker reads a generated, race-aware lib/buildTokens.ts (Build*, Train*, Research*, Morph* from sc2-units, sc2-icons and an upgrade list) and shows friendly names while storing tokens. It filters by race, shows proxy eligibility, and treats unknown tokens as an inline error that blocks save. The rule row's text input becomes TokenPicker. Fix the empty-state copy to show the same four options.
Tests: docToEvents conversion of signature builds; catalog covers every token sanitiseRule accepts; Combobox ARIA.

augments.text: FirstRunEmptyState (BuildsLibrary.tsx:626-649) should show the Start-from options as cards, plus a fifth card, 'Copy a Community build', linking to /community builds (SaveToLibraryButton already saves them into the library). Add a footer link 'See the built-in labels' → /definitions. The 'From one of your games' card names the real entry point: 'Open any game and click Save as new build on its build order' (components/analyzer/charts/SaveAsBuildButton.tsx). The current copy points to opponent profiles. The copy fix itself lands in wave 1 via builds-correctness-fixes item 4; this item replaces the single 'Create your first build' CTA that opens BuildEditorSheet. items.title: Build dossier: key timings benchmark and plan survival
items.why: The API already returns p25, median, p75, trend and win-rate-when-built timing rows (buildDossier.js), but the web type doesn't even declare them. Check-ins store declared and detected builds, yet nobody compares the two.
items.spec:
Key timings:
- KeyTimingsCard between Performance and Phase. Matchup tabs come from matchupTimingsLegacy.
- Rows in medianTimingsOrder: icon, CiWhisker p25–median–p75, trend arrow, 'WR when built', n, and 'Based on your last 25 games' when truncated.
- Clicking a row sets filterGameIds.
- When the build maps to a published guide, a 'Community' column and delta chip ('12 s slower than community').
- dnaTimings adds winner and loser medians from existing samples (no extra reads), hidden when either side has fewer than 5.
- BuildOrderColumns on the game page gets delta chips against your median for that build (cached dossier SWR).
Plan survival:
- A `plan` facet in the custom-build matches aggregation and in BuildsService detail, over slim rows with buildIntent.status='confirmed': declared, held (detected empty or equal), knockedOff, heldWR, knockedOffWR, top 5 knockedInto labels, top 5 knockedBy opponent strategies, median knocked-off duration.
- /v1/builds rows gain planHeldRate.
- Plan survival card (held/knocked-off donut, two WR stats, two linked ranked lists), a BuildCard 'held 62%' chip, and a Builds-tab column. All shown only at 5 or more declared games.
Tests: facet on fixtures; small-sample hiding.
items.howto: Help articles 'Read your key timings' (slug custom-builds, section #key-timings) and the build-check-in article (slug build-check-in) section #plan-survival. '?' tooltips on both cards.

items.title: Private build execution scorecard: rule-by-rule check and timings vs your own median
items.why: evaluateRules returns only a pass count, so no screen says which rule failed or when. GhostGradeCard appears only when this browser armed a target.
items.spec:
API: GET /v1/games/:gameId/build-execution (owner only, never served to coach, review or public routes). Returns {build (effective: confirmed check-in, else detected), source, rules:[{index, sentence, pass, unavailable, got, need, evidenceSec}], timings:[{token, displayName, thisGameSec, medianSec, p25Sec, p75Sec, n, deltaSec}], matchPct}.
evaluateRulesDetailed sits next to evaluateRules, reusing evaluateRule per rule plus the earliest-match time; existing callers are unchanged. Timings come from builds.detail for that build and matchup. In-process LRU keyed by userId+gameId+buildKey+rulesHash.
Web: BuildExecutionCard above BuildOrderColumns.
- Header 'Stargate Oracle — 7/8 rules' with a ring.
- Rule rows with pass/fail/unknown icons and time chips that seek the shared clock ('needed ≥2 before 4:30 · had 1').
- Timing rows with a range bar.
- Pass matchPct to the replay rail as buildMatchPct.
- 'Practice this build' arms Ghost.
- Empty states: 'Check in a build to grade this game', 'This build has no rules yet', 'Timings appear after 3 games'.
- Catalog builds show timings only. 'Unavailable' renders as unknown, not failed. Wording describes evidence and never judges.
Tests: detailed evaluator parity with evaluateRules; owner-only access.
items.howto: Help article 'Build check-in' (slug build-check-in), section #grading-a-game. Cross-linked from the game-page article and the card's 'How is this checked?' popover. A note in BuildEditorRulesHelp.tsx.

items.title: Reference build orders: a timed step list on every build, with paste-import and text export
items.why: Custom builds store only classifier rules, and public pages show rule deadlines as a 'build order'. Players practise from supply/time/action lists, and Ghost targets lack supply.
items.spec:
Data: optional buildOrder {v:1, steps:[{t, supply|null, action ≤80, note? ≤140}] (≤120 steps), source:'game'|'paste'|'manual', sourceGameId?} added to BUILD_FIELDS/BUILD_SCHEMA and the community snapshot projection. The classifier ignores it.
Editor: a 'Build order' tab in BuildEditorModal with an editable table (m:ss, supply, action via TokenPicker, note), drag reorder, insert and delete, 'Trim to first 5:00', 'Collapse repeated army units' and 'Fill from source game'. Builds created from a game are auto-filled, with workers folded into supply.
Paste import: deterministic parsers in lib/buildOrderText.ts for '[m:ss] Name', Spawning Tool columns ('13  0:18  Pylon'), Liquipedia '14 - Pylon' and '0:18 Pylon'. A live preview shows per-line errors; names are normalised via normalizeBuildName and the sc2-icons aliases; unknown actions are kept with a warning chip and never block save.
Export reuses lib/gameExport.ts: Copy as text, Markdown table, .txt.
BuildDetailView and the community page render <BuildOrderSteps>. PracticeButton prefers these steps. Enables the 'From a pasted build order' start card.
Tests: parser fixtures per format; schema caps.
items.howto: Help article 'Write or paste a build order' (slug build-order-paste) with supported formats and examples. The paste dialog has an inline 'Supported formats' disclosure linking there.

items.title: Desktop dashboard shows games, not file names: last game, today, recent history, import progress, skipped replays
items.why: Recent uploads lists raw filenames for this session only. 'Queued' reads 0 during a 10k-replay import, and skipped replays (vs AI, unresolved player) are visible only in agent state.
items.spec:
1) on_game_synced(path, summary) sink event, with summary {gameId, dateIso, result, races, oppName, map, durationSec, mmr, isLadder} from CloudGame plus the accepted row. RecentGamesStore appends to recent_games.jsonl (trimmed to 200) and loads at start.
Recent table: When (relative, absolute in tooltip), Result chip, Matchup, Opponent, Map, Length, MMR, Status, with All / Problems filters. Double-click opens {dashboard}/app/game/{id}. Context menu: Reveal, Copy path, Re-analyze. History imports are grouped under one collapsed row.
Dashboard: a 'Last game' card, plus a 'Today' tile (W–L, games, net MMR across consecutive same-region ladder games in local time). 'Every game' notifications toast 'Victory vs X (Z) on Alcyone'.
2) Import: ImportController.snapshot() and on_change go to a GuiUI importProgress signal. Rate is an EWMA over 5 minutes, and the ETA is hidden until there are enough samples. Card 'Importing your replay history': bar, counts, rate, ETA, phase (Scanning / Importing / Paused / Waiting for connection / Done), with Pause, 'Only import this season' and 'View on website'. The stat 'Queued' becomes 'Waiting' (queue plus remaining inventory, counted off-thread).
3) Skipped view: state.uploaded 'skipped:<reason>' markers grouped with plain-English rows (for example 'We couldn't tell which player was you → Set player name'). Retryable reasons (player_unresolved, parse_failed, file_unstable, filtered) offer 'Retry these', which clears only that reason and re-queues.
Tests: summary builder; today math across midnight; ETA; retry clears one reason only.

augments.text: The GUI-thread performance half (incremental insertRow and stats refresh throttled to at most 4 per second) ships earlier in agent-gui-polish-2. Build on it rather than rebuilding the table. Additions: (1) On the first start of the new RecentGamesStore, seed it from the newest 100 dated entries in state.uploaded (state.py:40-41) so existing users don't see an empty table. (2) Back the table with a QAbstractTableModel that uses insertRows. (3) Add filter chips with counts: All / Uploaded / Problems / Skipped by date filter. (4) Context menu: 'Show in Explorer' using explorer /select,<path> (today double-click only opens the folder, gui.py:3162-3188), Copy path, Copy error and Retry. Multi-select failed rows and offer 'Retry failed'. (5) Failure text comes from agent-calm-sync's errors.classify: 401/403 'This PC was unlinked - Link again', 429 'Rate limited - retrying automatically', 5xx 'sc2tools is busy - will retry'. Update the README 'Recent uploads' row and add a help bullet: 'An upload failed - right-click the row, Retry or Copy error'.

(1) The Synced tile shows '+12 today' from state.uploaded timestamps in local time. (2) 'Last upload' is a relative time ('3 min ago') taken from the newest timestamp in state.uploaded, so it survives restarts. Today it is an in-memory HH:MM:SS that resets to '—' (gui.py:3297-3303). (3) Add a 'Failed (24 h)' tile that opens Recent filtered to Problems. (4) Show the determinate progress bar ('1,240 of 4,812 replays') for a manual Re-sync too, not only the history import. (5) Move 'Re-sync library' off the action row next to Pause (gui.py:1465-1490) into a danger-styled Maintenance group at the bottom of Settings; agent-settings-and-first-run folds it into Advanced. Move 'Check for updates' (gui.py:1505-1516) next to the version label in the sidebar footer. Pause and Open dashboard stay as the primary actions. items.howto: Help articles 'Your recent games in the desktop app' (slug desktop-app-recent-games) and 'Importing your replay history' (slug desktop-app-import, covering each skip reason and whether it can be retried).

items.title: Bring every visitor back to what they were doing after sign-in or sign-up, and finish their action
items.why: safeAuthRedirect allows only /try?resume=1, and every new account lands on /welcome or /app. The highest-intent moment on every public page (save, vote, compare, arm) loses its context.
items.spec:
1) Replace safeAuthRedirect with safeReturnPath(value). It accepts only same-origin relative paths under an allowlist (/community/, /guides/, /reviews/, /p/, /players/, /try, /stream-studio, /download, /donate, /help, and /settings?tab=overlay|profile) and rejects //host, absolute URLs, encoded tricks, whitespace and fragments, with a 512-char cap. Table-driven tests; keep the /try?resume=1 tests.
2) lib/authLinks.ts provides signInHref(returnTo), signUpHref(returnTo) and useReturnTo(), used in Header, MobileNav, AppChrome SignedOut, CommunityVotePanel, GuidePersonalComparison, GuideCtas, MyReviews, ReviewPage and ReviewReplayDownload.
3) Sign-up goes to /welcome?next=<safe path>; OnboardingShell shows 'Continue where you left off: <page>', and Skip and the final CTA route to `next`. Sign-in honours forceRedirectUrl with the safe path.
4) lib/pendingIntent.ts stores {kind:'save-build'|'vote'|'arm-ghost', payload, path, expiresAt +15 min} in sessionStorage. After auth, the page with a matching path runs the existing action and shows the success link. The Ghost CTA arms the target and opens /settings?tab=overlay#ghost with a toast.
5) GA events auth_intent_started and auth_intent_completed.
Tests: open-redirect suite; intent expiry and path binding.
items.howto: The help article 'Getting started' (slug getting-started) adds 'Signed up from a guide or build? You'll be taken back to it.' The wizard banner and the signed-out button copy explain the action inline.

items.title: Public pages: dynamic share cards, correct metadata, edge caching with on-demand purge
items.why: Community builds share as a generic banner and hit the API on every view and every crawl. SiteStats polls a no-store proxy every 30 s from every open tab, and sign-in pages are indexable with default titles.
items.spec:
PR A, metadata:
- app/community/builds/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx (satori, same palette as /p): title, matchup badge, author, votes, top rule icons; static fallback.
- alternates.canonical and absolute JSON-LD URLs via lib/seo/absoluteUrl.ts, shared with guideSeo.
- lib/seo/pageMetadata.ts gives coherent openGraph and twitter metadata for /try, /download, /donate, /community, the leaderboard, authors and /help.
- OG images for /try and /download.
- sign-in and sign-up layouts set robots noindex.
- robots.ts adds /app, /settings and sign-in sub-routes.
- Public SSR dates in PublicProfile and AuthorStatsStrip use a fixed en-US formatter (fixes hydration mismatches).
- A test: every sitemap route has a canonical and a non-default og:title.
PR B, cache:
- Community fetches use next:{revalidate:300, tags:['community', `community-build:${slug}`]}. Detail pages throw on API failure so the last good render is served.
- app/api/revalidate-community/route.ts reuses the guides HMAC verify with scope 'community'. The API pings it fire-and-forget after publish, update, unpublish and moderation removal (votes only when the rounded count changes).
- API Cache-Control 'public, s-maxage=60, stale-while-revalidate=600' on public community GETs.
- The site-stats proxy sends 'public, s-maxage=15, stale-while-revalidate=60'.
- The community opponent page uses revalidate 21600 plus a 1 h LRU in aggregateOpponent.
- Document the secret in docs/DEPLOYMENT_GUIDE.md.
Tests: signature verify; purge on publish.

augments.text: Also set alternates.canonical on app/community/authors/[userId]/page.tsx, not only on builds. Replace description.slice(0,200) with a word-boundary trim that appends '…' (shared helper lib/seo/trimDescription.ts, with a test). The build share card must include net votes and the first 5 key steps with times, taken from the signature or from positive rules (before / count_min / count_exact with time_lt).
