augments.text: public-player-page must also do the following. (1) Privacy works in both directions. The archive and detail payloads carry a profile link (profileHandle or a Profile tab) only when publicProfile.enabled, or the legacy published-build rule, is true. The profile/Overview payload carries replayArchive: { handle, total } only when replay sharing is on and showReplays is set. So an archive-only user's private profile is never revealed, nor is a profile-only user's archive. An archive-only user at /players/<slug> sees only the Replays tab. (2) One display name on every surface (profile hero, archive hero, analysis hero, OG images, metadata): the public profile/author name when the profile is public, otherwise users.displayName. Today the community author name and users.displayName (apps/api/src/services/users.js:398-411) can differ. (3) The tab bar is a <nav aria-label='Player sections'> under the hero, with aria-current='page' on the current tab. Tabs the player hasn't enabled are left out, not shown disabled. (4) The Overview has a 'Browse N replays' card linking to the Replays tab. The shared analysis page shows 'Back to {name}'s replays' and, when the profile is public, a '{name}'s profile' link. (5) The /players/<slug>/replays and /players/<slug>/replays/<gameId> URLs stay stable, because they are already shared. Legacy /p/<uuid> and /p/<uuid>/replays/** links must reach the final URL in one redirect hop. (6) Carry over the profiles-replays-polish-1 rules to the new /players/[player] page: notFound() only on a 404; 429, 5xx and unreachable errors throw to error.tsx so ISR keeps serving the last good render; fetch with revalidateSec 300; key the API limiter on `${req.ip}:${slug}`; use the segment not-found.tsx copy. (7) Tests: an archive-only user's archive and detail payloads contain no profile link, and a profile-only user's payload has replayArchive null. (8) The public-profile Help article (apps/web/lib/help/articles/account-data.ts, /help/public-profile and /settings?tab=help#public-profile) explains: how each surface is turned on (the Settings > Profile toggle, or publishing a build under a public name for legacy profiles, and the replay-sharing toggle); what visitors see on each; how they link to each other; and how to turn each off.

Build public-player-page's 'last-20 W/L' as follows. PublicProfileService (apps/api/src/services/publicProfile.js) maps aggregations summary.recent (aggregations.js:79-95) to an identity-free recentForm: Array<{ result: 'W'|'L'|'T', matchup: 'PvZ', date }>, dropping opponent name, pulse id, toon and map. It also derives currentStreak { kind: 'W'|'L', count }, where a tie ends a streak, and lastPlayedAt. UI: a 'Recent form' card with up to 20 pips, oldest to newest. Each pip has an accessible label such as 'Win, PvZ, Oct 20', and the list has the summary label 'Last 20: 12 wins, 8 losses'. Show streak copy ('4-win streak' / '2-loss streak') only when count >= 2. Show 'Last played 2 days ago' using the fixed en-US formatter so SSR and the client match. Hide the card when there are fewer than 3 recent games. Everything, including lastPlayedAt, sits behind showRecentForm. Update the profile loading skeleton (app/p/[handle]/loading.tsx or the new /players/[player]/loading.tsx). Extend the no-PII assertions in apps/api/__tests__/publicProfile.test.js so recentForm never contains opponent names, ids or maps. Test streak derivation, including a tie breaking a streak. Optional, only if cheap: an 'All time / Last 90 days' toggle via aggregations.summary(userId, { since }). items.title: WCAG AA colours with split fill/ink tokens, axe and keyboard gates in CI, an accessibility statement and a true design doc
items.why: --accent as link text is about 4:1 in dark, white on --danger is 2.78:1, and most light-theme semantic colours fail AA. Nothing in CI catches regressions, and docs/design-system.md describes a palette and fonts that no longer exist.
items.spec:
1) Tokens: --accent-ink (dark #1f9eaf, light #0a737a) and --danger-fill (dark #c9363c). tailwind.config.ts maps textColor.accent to the ink token and bg-danger to the fill token, which fixes 400+ call sites without a codemod. Retune light tokens: success #157a43, warning #8f5f0f, accent-cyan #0a737a, signal #8f5c0c, danger #b8333a, race-protoss #4a5ae6. The active nav label uses accent-cyan in dark.
2) The theme toggle gains 'System', which follows OS changes via a matchMedia listener, and updates <meta theme-color>.
3) lib/__tests__/contrastTokens.test.ts parses both :root blocks and asserts the pair matrix (text tokens on bg/surface/elevated at 4.5:1; white on accent and danger-fill at 4.5:1; borders at 3:1).
4) @axe-core/playwright in public-pages.spec.ts for every page and viewport in both themes (wcag2a/2aa/21aa; serious and critical fail), with a reviewed allowlist ratchet. Keyboard smoke: skip link; MobileNav traps focus and returns it.
5) eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y recommended as warnings.
6) app/legal/accessibility/page.tsx: AA target, keyboard support, known limits (replay canvas, OBS overlays), how to report a barrier. Linked from the footer and the Help menu.
7) Rewrite docs/design-system.md from the real tokens and fonts, with contrast tables generated from the test matrix.

(2) In app/layout.tsx (~L110), replace the static #06090e with viewport.themeColor as a media array: [{media:'(prefers-color-scheme: light)', color:'#f4f6fa'}, {media:'(prefers-color-scheme: dark)', color:'#06090e'}]. items.title: Find anything: grouped Settings with search, and a Ctrl/Cmd+K quick search across the app and public guides
items.why: Ten flat Settings tabs include one 1,225-line Overlay scroll. There is no global search or shortcut, and visitors can't search guides.
items.spec:
PR A, Settings IA:
- Grouped sidebar: Account (Account, renamed from Foundation; Profile; Backups & data), Gameplay (Build check-in, Randomizer, Import), Streaming (Overlay; a new Chat & alerts tab holding SettingsMultiChat and its sub-sections, the Dock URL, ChatBotCard and ChatCommandsCard, with the active token passed in; Voice), Preferences (renamed from Misc), Help. Old ids alias (foundation→account, misc→preferences).
- Every Section gets a stable id. Tabs with 3 or more sections get an 'On this page' rail (a select on mobile).
- lib/settingsIndex.ts (sections, field labels, synonyms) drives a search box above the tabs that navigates to ?tab=x#id with a flash. A test checks every entry's tab exists.
PR B, quick search:
- components/chrome/CommandPalette.tsx (lazy-loaded), opened by Ctrl/Cmd+K, '/' outside inputs, or the search icons. ARIA combobox and listbox.
- Static groups: NAV_ENTRIES (with the same gates), Settings index, help articles, glossary, build definitions, Stream widgets, Actions (Pair a device, Report a problem, What's new, Toggle theme).
- Dynamic: GET /v1/search/quick?q= (2+ chars, 200 ms debounce, limit 8 per type): an anchored, escaped, case-insensitive prefix on opponents.displayNameSample (sorted by lastSeen), customBuilds.name and maps, with maxTimeMS 300, private max-age=30 and 60/min per user. Recent games come via /v1/replays?search=.
- On public pages the palette searches guides (guideSlugTable plus matchup aliases like 'pvt'), counter guides ('beat 12 pool'), community builds (/v1/community/builds?q=) and maps, linking only published guides. app/search?q= is noindex, and WEBSITE_JSON_LD gets a SearchAction.
- A '?' shortcut sheet: g+t, g+o, g+r, g+s.
Tests: alias links; the scorer; inputs are never hijacked; overlay and dock never mount it.

items.title: 'Get more out of SC2 Tools' checklist after the first game
items.why: Onboarding guidance disappears exactly when value starts: the checklist hides once the first game lands, and nothing points to builds, check-in, the overlay or chat.
items.spec:
GET /v1/me/activation runs six projection findOne calls (SWR cached 60 s) and returns {identity (pulseIds or battleTag), firstGameViewed (onboarding.firstGameViewedAt), customBuild, checkIn (a confirmed buildIntent), overlayLive (any token lastSeenAt), chatOn (a multichat platform enabled)}. GameDetailPage writes firstGameViewedAt once.
Today card 'Get more out of SC2 Tools': a progress ring and 4–6 rows filtered by onboarding.goals (both when unset), each with a one-line why, a deep-link CTA and a HelpLink. Dismissible via onboarding.levelUpDismissedAt. It hides when everything is done; completion shows a toast, then the card collapses to 'You're all set — see What's new'. One card only, never on sub-pages.
Tests: activation flags from fixtures; goal filtering; dismissal.
items.howto: Help article 'Your first week' (slug your-first-week): what each checklist item unlocks. Linked from the card header.

items.title: Faster dashboards: per-user revision cache with ETags, lighter /v1/me, Trends charts that load as you scroll
items.why: Every aggregation reruns on every request. /v1/me writes users.touch and counts every game each minute through an unindexed $ne, and Trends fires about 13 aggregations at once on every filter change.
items.spec:
API:
1) util/userRevision.js keeps an in-memory userId→rev map, seeded from and $inc-persisted to users.dataRev. bumpUserRev is called inside services, next to every games:changed emit: GamesService upserts, gdpr wipe/restore, reclassify, buildIntent writes, notes, identities, game exclude/delete.
2) middleware/userCache.js wraps read-only per-user GETs (the aggregations router, the opponents list, /me/doctor, build stats) in an LRU (64 MB budget, 512 KB max entry, 10-minute TTL) keyed by userId+path+sorted query+rev. Responses carry a weak ETag and 'private, no-cache' (304 on revalidate). Hit, miss and byte gauges go on the prom registry. This subsumes the Trends completed-result memo.
3) /v1/me: touch only when more than 5 minutes stale. users.gameStats {total, latest} is maintained by ingest and wipe. latestAgent is cached 30 s.
4) Device auth caches tokenHash→userId for 60 s (evicted on revoke) and writes lastSeenAt at most once a minute.
Web: components/analyzer/DeferredSection.tsx (generalised from DeferredTrendsExplorer, with reserved min-height) wraps every Trends card below the first row. A sticky in-page nav (Overview · Performance & MMR · Time & activity · Explore · Fingerprint) uses scroll-spy. Measure aggregate calls per Trends visit before and after, targeting -50%.
Tests: a test enumerating mutating routes asserts a rev bump; 304 path; revoke evicts.
items.howto: A line in the 'Trends' help article (slug trends): 'Charts load as you scroll; use the section links to jump'. docs/engineeringexplanation.md section 'Per-user revision cache' (rule: every mutation calls bumpUserRev). An /admin/health cache tile.

items.title: Instant Daily Pulse, Season Recap and Arcade: keep game history on this device and sync only changes
items.why: Up to 20k games are re-downloaded after every synced game, through one site-wide lane (routes/games.js:22-23) that returns 503 to the 7th concurrent user.
items.spec:
API:
- Stamp updatedAt on every games write path (ingest upsert, check-in override, macro recompute, reclassify, exclude), with index {userId:1, updatedAt:1}. A contract test asserts that every writer stamps it.
- GET /v1/games/analysis-corpus?changed_since=<iso>&cursor= returns changed rows plus removed:[gameId] (from tombstones and exclusions), with a corpusVersion.
Web:
- lib/analysisCorpusStore.ts on IndexedDB (the /try store pattern), keyed by userId+corpusVersion, holding rows plus a watermark.
- AnalysisGamesProvider hydrates from IndexedDB, then pulls deltas, so a new game costs one small request. Cleared on sign-out, account switch, or Delete history. Falls back to today's behaviour without IndexedDB, with a size cap.
- The Daily Pulse gate becomes one-time ('Load your history once — kept on this device'). A footer reads 'Updated just now · 18,452 games on this device · Refresh'.
- Settings > Backups & data shows 'Games stored on this device: N (X MB) — Clear'.
Tests: delta merge; removal; account isolation.
items.howto: Help article 'Your history on this device' (slug history-on-this-device), linked from the Daily Pulse gate, the Arcade empty state and Backups & data.

items.title: Sync health everywhere: a health checklist and coloured tray in the app, health in the heartbeat, and fixes on the website
items.why: The window shows 'Active' while nothing uploads, silent failures (no folder, unknown player, analyzer failed) live only in the log, and the website can't tell why a game didn't arrive.
items.spec:
PR A (agent):
- sc2tools_agent/health.py: a Qt-free HealthMonitor that subsystems push facts into: pairing, cloud (last heartbeat, socket, last transport error class), folders, identity source, analyzer probe, sync (paused, filter, backlog), live (localhost:6119 last contact; grey when SC2 is closed), OBS, updates. It recomputes at most twice a second and emits healthChanged through _Multiplexer.
- The dashboard card becomes a headline ('Everything's working' / '1 thing needs attention') over rows with one sentence and an action (Link PC, Retry now, Add folder, Set player name, Resume, Open OBS settings, Install update). Off features collapse into a grey footer.
- Tray icon gets a PIL status dot (green, amber, red, grey for paused). Boot failures are classified, with 'Restart agent' and 'Copy details'.
PR B (agent+api+web):
- The heartbeat adds sync {pending, archivePending, paused, foldersWatched, missingFolders, lastUploadAt, lastErrorCode, skipped:{reason:n}, rejected, filtered, unresolvedNames:[{name, toonHandle, count}] (top 10, seen ≥3)}, capped under 2 KB. recordHeartbeat whitelists it.
- Ingest increments users.ingestStats.rejected.<code>.
- GET /v1/me/sync-health.
- Doctor warnings: agent_no_folders, agent_paused, agent_upload_failing, agent_outdated_required, replays_skipped_unresolved, uploads_rejected, each with a helpSlug.
- Web: the header pill reads 'Agent online · 12,431 games · 3 min ago', with a popover. A Settings 'Sync health' card shows one row per reason with fixes: 'Add as my account' saves the identity; 'Retry with latest agent' emits resync for those paths; 'Change sync window'; 'Report'. Devices cards show a health row.
Tests: HealthMonitor rule table; heartbeat size cap; old agents degrade gracefully.
items.howto: Help articles 'What the status lights mean' (slug desktop-app-status) and 'Why didn't my game show up?' (slug my-game-didnt-show-up). Linked from the agent headline '?', the header popover and every fix button.

items.title: Desktop app Help page: system check, copy diagnostics, redacted support bundle, secrets moved to DPAPI
items.why: Support today means 'send a screenshot'. agent.json stores device_token and obs_password in plaintext, so a user attaching it leaks both.
items.spec:
New ui/help_page.py sidebar page with quick links to the help articles and 'Run system check'.
The check runs on a worker thread: HealthMonitor results plus probes for /v1/agent/version latency, authenticated /v1/me/profile, state dir writable and free disk, each folder readable (count and newest), probe_analyzer(), an end-to-end parse of a tiny bundled fixture replay, the localhost:6119 client API, and the OBS websocket when enabled. Results show as a checklist with fix buttons.
'Copy support info' produces redacted text: version, OS, pool mode, workers, folder count and regions, filter, queue and backlog, last 10 classified errors, last 6 chars of the deviceId, live-metrics summary.
'Save support bundle…' writes a zip of diagnostics.txt, the last 3 agent logs plus worker logs (scrubbed with the crash_reporter path and BattleTag scrubbers) and a secrets-free state summary, showing the file list first.
'Email support' opens a mailto prefilled. Tray items 'Help & troubleshooting' and 'Copy support info'.
Hardening: device_token and obs_password move to streaming/secret_store (DPAPI) with transparent migration on load. Downgrading then needs a re-pair, which is documented.
Tests: redaction of sample logs; the bundle never contains the token or password; migration round-trip.

augments.text: (1) The checklist also shows the agent update channel and the API base host, which agent-gui-polish-3 removes from the status card. (2) 'Copy support info' adds a hashed user id (first 8 hex of sha256) next to the deviceId suffix, and never includes the device token. (3) Also put a 'Copy support info' button in the Activity log toolbar, since users already go there when something breaks. (4) Each failing row gets a one-click fix (Retry, Open Settings, Link again). Replace 'include a screenshot' in Help Troubleshooting (SettingsHelp.tsx:532-544, or its help-center article) with 'In SC2 Tools, open Help > Copy support info and paste it into your report'.

items.howto: Help article 'Something's not syncing? Run the system check, then send a support bundle' (slug desktop-app-support). It replaces the screenshot request in Troubleshooting; the agent Help page links it.

items.title: Export center: streamed full archive, build-order export, and bulk replay download as one zip
items.why: The GDPR export builds everything in memory and omits game_details (build orders, macro), and replays can only be downloaded one at a time.
items.spec:
In Settings > Backups & data, an 'Export' section with format cards, size estimates, progress and cancel:
1) Full archive: /v1/me/export becomes streamed NDJSON (collection headers, cursor rows; game_details with ?details=1), so memory stays flat on Starter.
2) Build orders: GET /v1/export/build-orders.csv|ndjson, one row per event (gameId, side, time, supply, name), read from GameDetailsService with concurrency 4, 2,000 games per request with a continuation cursor, and 3 per hour per user.
3) Replay packs: Replays multi-select ('Select all matching, max 100') plus 'Download pack'. POST /v1/replays/download-batch {gameIds ≤100} → signed URLs via prepareDownload. Add GET to the managed R2 CORS rule through replayFilesCors.js; ensureBrowserUploadCors merges rules, and browserUploadStatus verifies them. The browser fetches with concurrency 4 as URLs are signed (they expire), and zips client-side with fflate in store mode. The zip includes manifest.csv and README.txt; a filename template select ('{date} {matchup} {result} vs {opp} on {map}') renames files inside the zip. Uses showSaveFilePicker where available, otherwise 500-file chunks. Shows a partial-failure summary. R2 egress is free, and the server only signs URLs.
The replay disclosure copy (what a .SC2Replay reveals) is reused.
Tests: CORS merge keeps existing rules; NDJSON streaming; template sanitising.
items.howto: Help articles 'Download all your data' (slug backups-and-export, section #export) and 'Replay packs' (slug replay-packs).

items.title: Re-analysis center: bring games analyzed by an older engine up to date in managed batches
items.why: Label-changing engine releases (1.6.10, 1.6.11) leave old games with stale labels, and the only remedy is a blind 12k-replay Full Resync.
items.spec:
1) Keep engineVersion and agentVersion on agent uploads (stampIngestProvenance currently deletes them), semver-bounded.
2) config/analysisMilestones.json [{engine, date, summary, matchups[]}] is updated each release.
3) GET /v1/me/reanalysis returns cohorts with counts: older than each milestone (affected matchups only), missing macroScore, no engine stamp.
4) POST /v1/me/reanalysis {cohortId} creates a reanalysis_jobs row (one active per user). Batches of 100 go out via a reanalyze:batch socket emitWithAck; the next batch is sent only after acks and uploads, which the ingest admission gate also bounds. Progress arrives via reanalysis:progress. With no agent the job sits in 'waiting_for_agent'.
5) Agent: ids without a local path download the R2 original through a signed URL into a temp dir, parse, upload, then delete it.
6) UI: a 'Re-analyze games' card in Backups & data. Cohorts show a 'what changed' line and a note that historical stats will change. Start, Pause and Cancel; progress with ETA; an agent-offline state. Game pages show a chip 'Analyzed with engine 1.6.9 · Re-analyze'.
Tests: cohort counts; pacing; offline pause.
items.howto: Help article 'Re-analyze old games after an update' (slug reanalyze). CHANGELOG entries for label-changing releases link to it.

items.title: One session definition, then session history, session pages and a live 'This session' card on Today
items.why: Three session definitions already disagree: a 4 h overlay reset (games.js:1095), a 4 h gap in Arcade, and a 90-minute gap in Trends momentum. Ladder players think in nights.
items.spec:
PR A, core:
- services/sessions.js sessionize(games, {gapMinutes, tz}) mirrored in web lib/sessions.ts, with a shared JSON fixture parity test.
- One preference, 'A session ends after N minutes without a game' (Settings > Profile). Default 4 h for accounts with an overlay token, otherwise 90 minutes, shown wherever sessions appear.
- todaySession, ArcadeEngine and trendsInsights momentum all use it. The streamer default is unchanged, and the change is announced in What's New.
PR B, pages:
- GET /v1/sessions?before=&limit=20&tz= plus filters, bounded by a date window on {userId, date}. Each row: {id, start, end, playedMin, games, wins, losses, results 'WWLW', matchups, topBuilds, mmr per toon {start, end, delta, peak}, avgMacro, longestStreak}.
- GET /v1/sessions/:id adds games.
- GET /v1/sessions/current.
- /app/sessions shows session cards (pip strip, MMR delta per account, matchup mini-records with sample cues) with a ?day= filter.
- /app/sessions/[id] shows an MMR step line, AllGamesTable, breaks between games, and descriptive 'after a loss this session' counts (no tilt verdict).
- Today: a live 'This session' card replaces 'Games today' (fixing the 'Keep the streak alive' hint during a loss streak); otherwise 'Last session'.
- The Activity calendar day panel links to that day's sessions.
Tests: the parity fixture; multi-account sessions; tz labels.
items.howto: Help article 'Sessions: review a night of ladder' (slug sessions), including what counts as a session and the setting. Glossary entry 'session'.

items.title: Personal goals with automatic progress: games, win rate, MMR, macro and build practice
items.why: It turns the dashboard from a report into a training plan. The bucket and timezone math already exists in coaching.js, but only invited students get it.
items.spec:
Extract coaching's assignmentBuckets and zonedLocalToUtc into util/recurrenceBuckets.js, used by both features.
player_goals {userId, id, type, params, filters (matchup, build, map; ranked 1v1 default), window {recurrence once|daily|weekly|monthly|season, startsOn, endsOn, tz}, status, completedAt, metNotifiedAt}, max 8 active. Types: games_played, win_rate (minGames ≥20), mmr_reach (toon?), macro_avg, apm_avg, sq_avg, build_reps (effective build including check-ins via the buildIntentShape expressions).
GET /v1/goals computes progress lazily with one $facet per goal on {userId, date}, behind a 60 s per-user memo (rev-aware). POST, PUT and DELETE. After ingest, a cheap check sends notify('goal_met') once, guarded by an idempotent claim.
Web: a Today 'Goals' card with up to 3 pinned progress bars and sample guards ('9 more games before this rate counts'; 'no rated games yet' for MMR). /app/goals has templates in a New goal modal (BuildPicker, matchup, season picker), active and completed lists, and deep links to the filtered section.
Tests: bucket math across DST; minGames; notify once.
items.howto: Help article 'Goals: set a target and track it automatically' (slug goals), plus inline help in the New goal modal (windows, minimum games, what counts).

items.title: Next-league targets: where you stand vs your league and the next one, timing gaps, and a season goal estimate
items.why: This is what sc2replaystats Elite sells, and the league decile tables already exist. SQ tiers are still fixed cut-offs (lib/macro.ts tierFromSq).
items.spec:
A 'Targets' card at the top of /app/macro plus a compact Today strip. Decile bars for SQ, macro score, APM and duration profile, each showing your last-20 median dot, your league p50 and the next league p50 ('Diamond PvZ p38 → Master median needs +6 SQ'). League comes from current MMR or SC2Pulse with a manual override; matchup follows FilterBar. Uses /v1/benchmarks for the current and next league (SWR 1 h).
New nightly aggregate league_timing_percentiles, built from guide_samples only and never game_details (same k=50 floor), served at GET /v1/benchmarks/timings: natural, third, first upgrade and key tech.
Replace the tierFromSq label with 'pXX · League MU' when a table exists; otherwise fall back.
A 'Season goal' mini panel: target league or MMR (prefs), MMR to go, avg net MMR per game over the last 30, estimated games and games per week before season end (lib/seasonCatalog.ts). Plain arithmetic, labelled as an estimate.
Rows open the games below target in ReportGamesModal. States: below floor ('Not enough Master PvZ games yet', absolute values still shown); no MMR (prompt to set the league).
Tests: band selection; timing aggregate k-floor.
items.howto: Help article 'League targets' (slug league-targets): what the bars mean, the opponent-league proxy, the 50-game floor, the season estimate math.

items.title: One notes system: opponent notes v2 (tags, stream/private, alt-aware) and private timestamped game notes with a review queue
items.why: The note card says notes appear only privately, but ScoutingWidget broadcasts them. Notes don't follow alt accounts, and there is no way to mark a game to review or note a moment.
items.spec:
PR A, core and opponents:
- A notes collection {userId, target:{kind: opponent|game, id}, text ≤500, tags[] ≤8×24 (contentFilter), visibility:'stream'|'private', scope:'account'|'player', groupKey?, pinned, gameTimeSec?, x?, y?}, indexed {userId, target.kind, target.id} and {userId, groupKey}.
- NotesService plus a <NotesPanel target>. Migrate opponent_notes to target opponent, defaulting visibility to stream (current behaviour) with a one-time explainer banner.
- Player scope resolves exact toon first, then groupKey/Pulse accountId.
- The overlay gets only stream notes with non-private tags; the SSE stream and agent brief may include private notes.
- Preset tags (Cheeser, Proxy, All-in, Macro, Smurf, Off-race, Rival, and Toxic, which is always private) plus deterministic suggestions, never auto-applied ('Cheeser' when the early all-in share is ≥40% with n≥3).
- GET /v1/opponents attaches notesMeta.
- A quick-note popover on the game header and the live brief.
- GDPR export and delete.
PR B, games:
- Game notes at a time t: TransportDock 'Add note at 4:12' (B), 'Pin on map' via onWorldClick, rendered as commentMarkers and mapMarkers; a list with seek, edit, tags and undo delete. Max 200 per game, private, and never served by share or review routes (allowlist test).
- A small review subdoc on the game row {state todo|done, tags ≤5}: PUT /v1/games/:id/review, a header toggle, Replays filters 'To review' and tags, plus noteCount in GAME_SLIM_FIELDS for 'Has notes'. Search includes note text. Check-in notes stay separate and untouched.
Tests: visibility rules; migration; privacy allowlist.
items.howto: Help articles 'Opponent notes & tags' (slug opponent-notes) and 'Game notes & review queue' (slug game-page-notes). Update the 'scouting' entry in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts to say only 'Show on stream' notes appear.

items.title: Share one game by link, with the map replay, no account needed, revocable
items.why: Sharing is all-or-nothing for the whole library or a PNG. One game sent to a friend or Reddit is the strongest organic advert, and reviews already prove the scoped-grant pattern.
items.spec:
Data: game_shares {_id: 16-char token (reviews ID_RE), userId, gameId, createdAt, revokedAt, viewCount}, at most 200 active per user, included in GDPR export and delete.
API:
- Owner POST/GET /v1/games/:id/shares and DELETE /v1/shares/:token.
- Public GET /v1/shares/:token returns a redacted analysis using publicReplays.js's allowlist shapers.
- Public map-playback manifest and segments resolve the token to its owner, serving short-TTL presigned R2 URLs so bytes skip Render.
- Public /og image.
- Rate limits reuse the reviews heavyLimiter.
Web:
- A public /g/[token] route outside the auth matcher renders PublicReplayAnalysis plus an anonymous SegmentedReplayHost and the BenchmarkStrip (league only), with an opengraph-image (result, matchup, map art, builds, macro) and robots noindex.
- ShareGameButton becomes a menu: Copy share link (created on first use), Share as image, Manage links (list and revoke). The same menu goes on Replay Library rows.
Notes, review state and private data are never included.
Tests: redaction parity with the public allowlists; a revoked token returns 404; per-token rate limit.
items.howto: Help article 'Sharing a game' (slug game-page-sharing): link vs image vs public library, what viewers see (player names are inside replays), how to revoke. Linked from the share menu.

items.title: Replayer studio: vision modes, click-to-inspect units, and WebM/GIF clip export
items.why: 'What did my opponent see?' and 'share this fight' are the two most-asked replay jobs. Per-player fog is documented as unwired, and there is no clip export.
items.spec:
Vision:
- MapReplayer prop vision 'both'|'me'|'opp'|'off'. renderFrame filters pushFog by owner.
- In single-side mode, enemy units outside revealed fog are skipped (one sample per unit against the 0.4× fog buffer). Seen enemy buildings persist as dimmed 'last seen' ghosts.
- A 'Vision' segmented control in ReplaySettings, persisted with replay prefs. V cycles. Non-engine fidelity is labelled 'approximate vision'.
Inspector:
- A tap hit-tests live units in screen space (nearest within cell radius; repeated clicks cycle overlapping units).
- A glass popover shows icon, name, owner, born and died, lifetime and attacks, with Jump to birth, Jump to death and Follow (camera centres on the unit; Esc releases).
Clip:
- A 'Clip' button in ReplayTopBar. Range defaults to the nearest detectBattles marker ±10 s, max 60 s.
- Options: speed 1/2/4×, 1280×720 or 1080×1080, HUD on or off, watermark 'sc2tools.com' or the player page.
- Deterministic frame-by-frame render on an OffscreenCanvas reusing the draw functions, via captureStream + MediaRecorder (WebM VP9, MP4 where supported), or a worker GIF at 12 fps (gifenc). Progress and cancel.
- Zero server cost. Owner or analysis-enabled public pages only.
Tests: fog filtering; hit-test; clip frame count.
items.howto: Help article 'Game page & map replay' (slug game-page), sections #vision-and-inspector and #make-a-clip (browser support; Safari uses GIF).

items.title: Compare two games side by side: timelines, build diff and mechanics
items.why: 'Where did this loss diverge from my best win with the same build?' has no answer in any competitor, and every per-game endpoint already exists.
items.spec:
/app/compare?a=&b= (shareable). Entry points:
- A 'Compare…' button on the game page opens a picker with smart chips: Best win with this build, Previous game vs this opponent, Last game same matchup.
- A two-row multi-select in Replays.
Layout:
- Dual header.
- One synced chart overlaying A (solid) and B (dashed) for workers, army, income and supply via macro/timelineMetrics.ts, with a cursor readout of deltas.
- A build-order diff aligned by step name and occurrence index (the lib/ghostGrade.ts alignment) with coloured Δtime.
- Mechanics side by side: SQ, supply-blocked seconds, inject/chrono/MULE, APM.
Data: the existing endpoints fetched twice with SWR; no server changes. Each side has its own states, and metrics hide per side when data is missing. Charts stack on mobile.
Tests: alignment of repeated steps; missing data per side.
items.howto: Help article 'Compare two games' (slug compare-games), plus a one-time hint on the new Compare button.

items.title: Engine release: unit-by-unit trades, exact supply, full build logs, a game-wide cast index, and a Units card
items.why: Casualties record only which side killed, not which unit, so 'what each unit killed' (an sc2replaystats headline) is impossible. Supply is interpolated and cast markers cover only the loaded minute.
items.spec:
Engine and agent (one release):
- record_casualty resolves killing_unit_id to a canonical killerUnit and adds bornAt. Optional fields; the schema allows extras.
- build_log_lines emits an aligned buildLogSupply[] tracked from UnitInit/UnitBorn supply costs.
- A bounded buildLogFull (≤5000 lines, game_details only) includes depots, overlords and workers.
- playback_artifacts writes an optional manifest timeline:{casts:[…]}. sanitizePlaybackManifest accepts it additively.
- The '[m:ss] Name' wire format is unchanged.
API: prefer exact supply and drop ≈.
Web: a 'Units' card next to Mechanics, per side and unit type: Built, Lost, Kills, Resources killed and lost, Trade ratio, Median lifespan. Expand to 'Killed: 14 Marine…' and 'Died to: Baneling 62%'. Best and worst trader highlighted. A sticky unit column on mobile. An 'Unattributed' bucket for splash and spell deaths. Older games show side totals plus 'Update the app and re-analyze for unit detail', linking reanalysis-center.
Build dossier and Macro: 'Your Banelings trade 1.9:1 in ZvT (40 games)' via the bounded preview queue, cached per user, build and version.
Tests: engine fixtures; schema back-compat; card math.
items.howto: Help article 'Unit efficiency and trade ratio' (slug units): pricing in minerals+gas, what Unattributed means. Update 'Reading and exporting build orders' (slug build-orders-export) to say exact supply has no ≈. Agent CHANGELOG.

items.title: Map Intel (lean): opponent proxy, fight and unit-loss heatmaps from spatial data already uploaded
items.why: The agent still uploads game.spatial and /v1/spatial/* routes exist, but no UI has consumed them since MapIntelTab was removed.
items.spec:
API: add an `opponent` filter (pulseIds and character ids, merged identities allowed) to the spatial routes. Cap at the 300 most recent games and always use the pure-JS binning path, never spawning Python. A 10-minute in-process LRU keyed by user+map+layer+filters+rev.
Web: MapIntelPanel draws a canvas heat layer over MapArtwork using map_bounds (the same alignment as MapReplayer). Layer toggles: Their proxies, Fights, Where you lose units, Your buildings. Opacity slider, sample caption, and an accessible text list of the top 5 hot zones labelled by nearest base (main, natural, third).
Placement: a map detail drawer from each /app/maps row, and a 'Where they proxy / fight on this map' expansion per map in the dossier.
Empty state: 'No spatial data for this map yet — re-analyze in the desktop app'.
Tests: bounds alignment fixtures per map; the cap; the cache.
items.howto: Help article 'Map intel heatmaps' (slug map-intel): each layer, why some maps are empty, how to re-analyze. A mention on the /guides/maps hub intro.

items.title: Private practice log: every game in your practised matchup graded automatically, with your progress
items.why: lib/ghostGrade.ts grades only in the browser that armed the target and saves nothing, so there is no trend, no phone view and no history.
items.spec:
Private by design: never exposed to coaches or public, share or review routes, per the coaching no-automated-grading rule.
PR A, server grading:
- Port gradeExecution to services/practiceGrade.js with shared JSON fixtures against lib/ghostGrade.ts (the customRuleParity pattern).
- At ingest, after tagSingleGame, if a synced ghost slot for this matchup was armed before the game date, $set a slim ~300-byte `practice` subdoc: {targetHash, targetName, matchup, grade, matched, total, avgDrift, maxDrift, firstDivergence, worstSteps (top 5), checkpoints[], gradedAt}. This is a pure function with no extra I/O.
- Optional 'Grade my last 20 games' as a bounded job (at most 20 hydrations).
PR B, page:
- GET /v1/practice/summary?matchup=&targetHash= (grade distribution, rolling drift, divergence mode, checkpoint hit rate) and /v1/practice/games (paged).
- A /practice page linked under Custom builds: current target per matchup, a sparkline of the last 30 grades, a per-step drift bar, 'Where you fall off', a checkpoints editor (1–3 steps with ±s tolerance, stored in the ghost slot) and a weekly plan with a progress bar.
- GhostGradeCard prefers the stored grade.
- New daily quest 'Grade B or better on your practice build'.
Tests: TS/JS parity; grouping by targetHash; no regrading.

items.spec:

items.title: Build library safety and tools: undo, version history, recently deleted, duplicate, pin, tags, bulk actions, share codes
items.why: PUT overwrites in place with no revisions, soft-deleted builds have no restore (and block re-creating the name), and players with many variants can't organise them.
items.spec:
Safety:
- On each upsert, copy the prior doc to custom_build_revisions {userId, slug, rev, savedAt, doc} (cap 20 per build).
- GET /:slug/revisions and POST /:slug/revisions/:rev/restore, through upsert plus reclassify.
- GET /v1/custom-builds/trash (30 days) and POST /:slug/restore (no auto-republish; re-runs the ADR 0025 undelete logic).
- A nightly purge job.
- UI: the delete toast gets Undo for 10 s, a 'Recently deleted (n)' drawer, and a BuildDetailView 'History' sheet with a rules diff and 'Restore this version'.
Tools:
- Optional pinned and tags (≤8×24) on the schema with a multikey index; listPage filters tags=, perspective= and published=, pinned first.
- Kebab menu: Duplicate (create-only, '(copy)'), Practice, Add to randomizer pool, Copy share code, Pin.
- Filter bar: tag chips, Mine / Opponent, Published.
- A selection mode with a bulk bar (tags, randomizer, publish or unpublish through the per-build path, delete with one confirmation, export).
- Keys: '/' search, 'n' new.
Import/export:
- GET /v1/custom-builds/export (validated fields).
- An Import dialog for a .json, a share code or pasted JSON, with client validation and a preview of new / conflict (skip, copy, overwrite) / invalid.
- POST /import in batches of ≤100 with source 'import' and one reclassify at the end; cap 500 builds per user (409).
- Share codes are base64url ≤8 KB with hostile-input validation; /builds/import#code= keeps the code in the fragment.
Tests: revision cap; restore of a published build; import validation.

augments.text: Undo UI details: on BuildsLibrary (217-239) and BuildDetailView (69-87), show a 10 s toast 'Deleted “<name>” · Undo'. Toast description accepts ReactNode, so embed the Undo button there. On the detail page, a successful Undo navigates back to /builds/<slug>. When the deleted build was public, the post-undo toast reads 'Restored privately. Publish again to relist it.' Restore never auto-republishes, because delete removes the Community listing (routes/customBuilds.js:1085-1100). The ConfirmDialog warning 'Its Community listing will also be removed.' (when isPublic) ships earlier in builds-polish-4, so this item only needs the Undo/restore parts.

Filter UI details: in BuildFilterBar, add a compact segmented control 'All · Mine · Opponent captures' (perspective=you|opponent) and a 'Published' toggle chip. Add race-level pills (P / T / Z) that expand into that race's matchups, backed by a new `race` param in parseBuildPageOptions (apps/api/src/services/customBuildPages.js) matched against build.race. Persist these as ?src=mine|opp&pub=1&race=P in the URL scheme builds-polish-1 introduces (q, mu, sort, hide), and count them in its 'Clear filters (n)' button. Add perspective, published and race to pageScope so page cursors stay valid per filter set. Tests: API param validation (400 on bad values), cursor scope changes with each filter, URL round-trip.

items.title: Weekly report and post-stream report, delivered through the bell (and push when enabled)
items.why: There is no recurring summary to bring players back, and streamers have no recap after a stream. Both need sessions-core and a delivery channel, which the bell now provides.
items.spec:
Weekly:
- services/weeklyReport.js build(userId, isoWeek, tz) over slim rows for this week and last: totals, hours, W-L by matchup vs last week with n, MMR per account, best and worst map and build (≥3 decided, sample cues), top 3 opponent strategies faced with your record, avg macro and top leak vs last week, session count.
- GET /v1/reports/weekly?week=.
- jobs/weeklyReportJob.js on the reviewDigestJob hourly pattern: Monday about 09:00 user tz (misc tz pref), claim per user per week, ≥5 games, misc.weeklyReport=false opt-out, staggered and capped per tick. Sends notification 'Week 42: 23 games, 13–10, +86 MMR'.
- /app/reports/weekly/[week] with WinRateComparison rows, a week switcher, 'Open in Trends' and Share image (ShareCard deliverShareCard). Today shows a 'Last week' card Monday to Wednesday.
Stream:
- A stream session runs from the Dock Start new session to 'End stream' (or 4 h idle). On end, compute once and store a ≤5 kB doc in stream_sessions (cap 100): games, W-L by matchup and map, MMR start/end/peak plus sparkline, best win, builds, randomizer rolls, Crystal Ball accuracy, top 5 supporters and oracles (aggregates only unless opted in), and clip moments with VOD links.
- /app/streams and /app/streams/[id], with an opt-in Share to /players/<slug>/streams/[id] plus an OG image, and 'Copy Discord summary'.
Copy stays descriptive (no 'you lose because').
Tests: week boundaries in tz; claim idempotency; stream doc cap.

items.title: Post results, session summaries and milestones to Discord through channel webhooks
items.why: Clans, teams and streamer communities live in Discord. Webhook-only posting needs no bot process, so server cost stays flat.
items.spec:
A 'Post to Discord' card in Settings (Integrations). Paste up to 3 webhook URLs, validated against ^https://(canary\.|ptb\.)?discord(app)?\.com/api/webhooks/\d+/[\w-]+$, encrypted with platformCredentialVault and shown only as the last 4 characters. 'Send test'.
Events: each ranked result (embed coloured by result; matchup, map, opponent if allowed, builds, MMR delta, game link), session summary (sessions-core gap), weekly recap, new peak or promotion. Privacy: opponent names off by default, MMR on, replay link only when sharing allows.
Storage: discord_hooks {userId, label, enc, events, options, status, failureCount, lastPostAt} and discord_outbox {hookId, kind, embed, attempts, nextAttemptAt, status} with a 7-day TTL. Ingest only enqueues. A jobLock single-flight drain every 30 s takes ≤20 messages and honours 429 retry_after with exponential backoff. Three consecutive 401/404 responses disable the hook and send a notification. Nothing is posted for accounts in deletion. GDPR purge, with the URL redacted in exports.
Tests: URL validation; outbox backoff; disable after failures.
items.howto: Help article 'Post your games to Discord' (slug discord): creating a webhook (Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → Copy URL), what's posted, privacy toggles.

items.spec:

items.title: Classifier accuracy console: learn from every check-in correction which detector rules mislabel builds
items.why: Every confirmed check-in stores declared and detected labels, but nobody aggregates the disagreements. Rule fixes are guesswork.
items.spec:
A nightly jobLock job aggregates confirmed check-ins over the last N days into classifier_quality. Per (matchup, detected→declared): count, distinct users (k≥3 floor), engine version. Per label: agree vs disagree.
New /admin/classifier: pairs sorted by disagreement volume, a trend per engine version, and a drill-down with up to 20 sample games showing the first 6 minutes of the build order next to the declared rule's requirements. 'Copy as test fixture' exports the build log JSON for replay-engine tests.
/definitions shows a trust line, 'Matches N of M player corrections', framed as disagreement volume and never as accuracy. Rules stay human-edited and nothing auto-tunes.
Tests: the k-floor; bounded window.

items.title: Coaching: a 'Since last session' prep digest on each booking (facts only, no grading)
items.why: LOCKER_SITE_INTEGRATION.md plans this digest and it doesn't exist. Coaches currently rebuild the context by hand before every session.
items.spec:
On the React Sessions tab, each upcoming booking shows 'Since last session': games played and W-L by matchup, builds played (check-in labels), and new replays linking to /app/game/[id]. It is built from the existing coaching assignment and game endpoints, shows only when the student has accepted practice-sharing (PRACTICE_SHARING_POLICY_VERSION), and contains no grades, scores or practice-log data. Locker alerts also go through NotificationsService. The 283 KB Locker stays as is (its React port is deferred).
Tests: the consent gate; no grade fields in the payload.

items.title: Appearance & region preferences: reduce motion, text size, density, 12/24h, week start, locale-aware formatting
items.why: Text cannot be enlarged without zooming the whole page. Motion follows the OS only. 229 toLocale* calls format inconsistently, and EU players can't choose 24h or Monday weeks.
items.spec:
1) Motion system/reduce/full as data-motion on <html>. globals.css repeats the reduced-motion block under [data-motion=reduce]. One lib/a11y/useReducedMotion replaces the three separate hooks.
2) Text size 100/112.5/125%: convert tailwind fontSize and the .t-* classes from px to rem (pixel-identical at 100%, verified by the e2e overflow suite) and set html font-size; skip /overlay and /dock.
3) Density comfortable/compact as data-density for table and card padding.
4) lib/i18n/format.ts with cached Intl factories and useFormat() {date, time, number, percent, relative, duration}, driven by locale (auto or explicit), hourCycle and weekStart. Reimplement fmtAgo and fmtDate. Server components use a stable en-US formatter for SSR. An ESLint ratchet bans bare toLocale* outside lib/i18n against a baseline. weekStart feeds lib/datePresets.ts and lib/activityBuckets.ts, with tests.
5) Persist to localStorage (no-flash script) and sync through a new 'appearance' PREF_TYPE with a sanitiser. An 'Appearance & accessibility' card in Settings > Preferences.
Tests: rem parity; motion attribute honoured; week-start buckets.

items.title: Donate page: monthly coverage meter, recurring option and an opt-in supporter wall
items.why: /donate already publishes live infrastructure costs, but there is no goal or recurring option. 'Is this month covered?' turns goodwill into action and funds the flat-cost backend.

No payment API integration. An admin-entered ledger donation_months {month, receivedUsd, supporterCount, updatedAt} with PUT /v1/admin/donations/:month and public GET /v1/public/donations/current (s-maxage 600).
supporters {displayName, message ≤80 (contentFilter), month, approved}: entered by the admin, or self-serve 'Add me to the wall' for signed-in users, pending approval.

A third channel card for a recurring platform (Ko-fi monthly or GitHub Sponsors URL via env). FAQ updates with FAQPage JSON-LD. A SupporterWall (this month, plus collapsed all-time). DonateBanner shows the meter below 100%. A small /admin card for entering the month.

items.title: Backup status you can see: Atlas snapshot health on the admin page and honest backup copy
items.why: The cluster is M10 with Atlas Cloud Backup; make its health visible and the site copy accurate. No new secrets.
items.spec:
1) API: AtlasInfrastructureClient gets backupStatus(): GET /api/atlas/v2/groups/{projectId}/clusters/{clusterName}/backup/snapshots (and the backup schedule) with the existing service-account token; return only {lastSnapshotAt, status, retention summary, nextSnapshotAt} (no ids/hostnames). Cached 10 min, fail-soft when credentials are absent or lack Project Read Only.

3) Fix the SettingsBackups copy and app/legal/privacy to describe what really happens: Atlas daily snapshots of the whole database (retention as configured), plus the per-user snapshots in Settings > Backups, plus export.
4) Tests: client parsing with fixture JSON, 403/absent-credential paths, admin route auth, card colour thresholds.

items.title: Today: KPI cards that update live, today's W-L record, and a Default tab that stops redirecting away from Today
items.spec:
Two visible Today bugs plus some polish on the KPI strip. Files: apps/web/components/analyzer/DashboardKpiStrip.tsx, apps/web/app/app/loading.tsx, apps/web/app/app/layout.tsx, apps/web/components/dashboard/TodayView.tsx, apps/web/components/dashboard/AnalyzerFrame.tsx, apps/web/app/app/page.tsx.

A. KPI cards that update live (today-kpis-live-session-record)
1. Append `#${dbRev}` to the three keys that lack it: globalSeries `/v1/timeseries${globalSeriesQuery}` (~L158), streak `/v1/streak${streakQuery}` (~L200) and wrSeries `/v1/timeseries${wrQuery}` (~L204). This matches selectedRangeSeries (~L177), so all cards refresh on games:changed, as Ladder Pulse already does. Leave /v1/me/mmr unkeyed, because it calls SC2Pulse once per Pulse ID.
2. Error states: replace the placeholder logic (~L212-214). Loading shows '—'. An error with no data shows '—' as the value and a hint button, "Couldn't load · Retry", that calls that query's mutate() with aria-busy while it revalidates. A real zero still shows '0'. Use the compact RequestError from data-states-recovery if it has landed; otherwise use a local button.
3. Session record: rename the lead card from 'Games today' to "Today's session". The value reads '6 games' and the hint reads '4W 2L', taken from today's Period.wins/losses in the same globalSeries bucket (Period in apps/web/lib/timeseries.ts already has both fields). With zero games the value is '0 games' and the hint is 'No games yet today'. This replaces the 'Keep the streak alive' hint, which was wrong during a losing run. sessions (W6) later swaps this card for a real 'This session' card, so keep its data-testid stable.
4. Grid: five cards in grid-cols-2 leave an orphan card on phones. Give the lead card `col-span-2 lg:col-span-1` (phone rows become lead, then 2, then 2), drop the redundant `sm:grid-cols-2` (~L218), and copy the same classes into the skeletons in app/app/loading.tsx:10 and app/app/layout.tsx:72 so nothing shifts on load.
5. Turn the MMR empty hint (~L472) into a Link, 'Add a Pulse ID in Settings', pointing to /settings?tab=profile#pulse-id-help. The anchor already exists in SettingsProfile.tsx, and settings-quickwins makes #anchors scroll.
6. Win-rate timeframe menu (role=menu, ~L339-383): the trigger gets aria-haspopup='menu' and aria-expanded. On open, focus the selected menuitem, or the first one. ArrowUp/ArrowDown wrap, Home/End jump, and Enter/Space select. Escape and Tab close the menu, and Escape returns focus to the trigger. Keep global-filter-clarity's 'all time' labelling if it has landed.

B. Default tab only applies when the session starts on /app (default-tab-redirect-bounce)
1. AnalyzerFrame: on the first mount of any /app route, set a session cookie `sc2_app_session=1; Path=/; SameSite=Lax` with no Max-Age, so it ends with the browser session. Wrap the write in try/catch.
2. app/app/page.tsx (server), after the existing ?opponent and ?tab redirects: if the cookie is absent, read the preference with apiFetch('/v1/me/preferences/misc') using a short timeout, where any failure falls through to Today. When isTabId(pref) and pref is not Today, call redirect(hrefForTab(pref)). The default tab then applies only when /app is the first analyzer page of the browser session, and there is no flash because the redirect runs before render. Clicking Today later always shows Today, since the RSC request carries the cookie. Opening a bookmark such as /app/maps first and then clicking Today also shows Today.
3. Delete the client redirect in TodayView (the useEffect, its /v1/me/preferences/misc fetch, the redirected ref and DEFAULT_TAB_APPLIED_KEY, ~L20-58) and update the doc comment. This also removes one request from Today, and the 'storage blocked = bounce every visit' fallback goes with it.
4. settings-quickwins (W1) adds the 'Today (default)' option to the picker. If this pack lands first, add that option to SettingsMisc's select instead. A stored 'today' value means no redirect.
5. shareable-views (W3) later adds 'Set as default view'. It must plug into this server redirect, not reintroduce a client-side one.
Edge cases: a prefetch of /app from the rail runs page.tsx with the cookie already set. ?tab= and ?opponent= keep priority. If cookies are blocked the user cannot stay signed in anyway, so the cookie is safe to rely on.

Tests (vitest/RTL): a useApi mock records keys; the timeseries and streak keys end with #<dbRev> and change when dbRev bumps. A 500 on streak renders '—', and Retry calls mutate. The hint reads '4W 2L' from a fixture. The lead card has col-span-2. The MMR hint is a link with the right href. Menu keyboard: ArrowDown moves focus, and Escape closes the menu and focuses the trigger. page.tsx: no cookie with pref 'maps' calls redirect('/app/maps'); with the cookie present it renders TodayView; a throwing pref fetch renders TodayView; ?tab wins. AnalyzerFrame sets the cookie on mount. TodayView never calls router.replace.

Add one line saying 'Default tab' only applies when you first open the dashboard in a browser session, and clicking Today always shows Today. Add another line saying the session card shows today's games and W-L and updates as games land. Repeat the default-tab line in the Preferences entry of the settings-overview article.

items.title: Filter bar: one-line summary with an edit sheet, scoped per page, with plain labels and consistent copy

This pack reshapes the same FilterBar.tsx, so it lands after that item in W2 and reuses its sheet instead of building a second one. ui-primitives-and-dialogs (W5) later moves these popovers onto its Popover/Sheet. To make that a drop-in swap, this pack creates the focus-trap hook W5 plans to add.

A. Compact bar (compact-filter-bar). Files: apps/web/components/analyzer/FilterBar.tsx, FilterPill.tsx, GameLengthFilter.tsx, apps/web/components/dashboard/AnalyzerFrame.tsx, apps/web/lib/filterContext.ts, new apps/web/lib/a11y/useFocusTrap.ts, apps/web/components/ui/Modal.tsx.
1. Summary line: add summarizeFilters(filters) to lib/filterContext.ts. It returns plain labels in a fixed order: date preset, game type, game size, regions, length, and matchup when set. FilterBar renders one row, e.g. 'Current patch · Ranked ladder · 1v1 · All regions · Any length', followed by a 'Filters' button with a badge counting non-default facets (from describeActiveFilters). ActiveFilterChips stay below the row for removing filters.
2. Desktop (md and up): the date trigger, MatchupPicker and region pills stay inline. Map pool, game size, length (including GameLengthFilter's Custom) and too-short move into a 'More filters' popover anchored to the Filters button. Mobile (below md): show only the summary line and the Filters button. The button opens global-filter-clarity's bottom sheet, which now holds every facet and has a sticky footer with 'Reset' (DEFAULT_ANALYZER_FILTERS) and 'Done'.
3. Tap targets: FilterPill is min-h-[28px] (FilterPill.tsx:35; FilterBar.tsx:444). Make it min-h-11 (44px) inside the sheet and on coarse pointers (`@media (pointer: coarse)`); inline desktop pills can stay at 32px.
4. Plain labels, with stored values unchanged: 'Maps: Ladder/Custom' becomes a 'Game type' group with 'Ranked ladder', 'Custom games' and 'Both'. 'Players' becomes 'Game size'. 'Hide too-short' becomes 'Hide games under 45 s', built from TOO_SHORT_SECONDS. The length group keeps its bands and gains an 'Any length' option. Each group is a fieldset with a legend.
5. Focus: move Modal.tsx's focusableInside, Tab-wrap, Escape and focus-return logic into lib/a11y/useFocusTrap.ts, and have Modal use it with no behaviour change. Three popovers use the hook: the date popover (FilterBar.tsx ~L137-147, which sets aria-modal but neither moves focus into the dialog nor traps it), the new More filters popover, and GameLengthFilter's Custom popover. On open, focus moves to the first control. Tab wraps, and Escape closes the popover and returns focus to its trigger. An outside click also closes it.
6. Per-page scope in AnalyzerFrame (~L108-134): do not render FilterBar on /app/arcade. isArcade already exists there, and Arcade's corpus keys only on dbRev. On /app (Today), render a slim row instead: 'Filters shape the analysis sections. Today shows your live session.' It has a 'Show filters' toggle, remembered with useLocalStorageState('analyzer.today.showFilters'), that expands the full bar, because the 'Games in range' card does use filters. ActiveFilterChips still render on Today whenever a facet is non-default, and that card gets a small 'Uses filters' caption. /app/game stays without a bar.

B. Copy pass (copy-consistency)
1. Add `export const TOO_SHORT_SECONDS = 45` to lib/filterContext.ts, with a comment pointing to apps/replay-engine/core/strategy_detector_helpers.py:66. Use the constant in FilterBar's title (~L498), its aria-label (~L512; global-filter-clarity fixes that text, and this pack swaps it to the constant) and the new label. Fix two stale doc comments: filterContext.ts:30 says 'under 30 seconds', and FilterBar.tsx:472 says 'Default off' although the toggle defaults on.
2. Sentence-case placeholders and hints: BuildsTab 'search build…' (~L82) becomes 'Search builds'. The hint 'click a row to inspect or edit a build' (~L93) becomes 'Select a build to view or edit it'. StrategiesTab 'search strategy name…' (~L215) becomes 'Search strategies', and 'view games →' (~L275) becomes 'View games'. OpponentsTab 'search opponent name or ID…' (~L279) becomes 'Search by name or Pulse ID'. Give StrategiesTabBuildVs's hints the same pass.
3. ArcadeTab (~L15, 305-306): rename the sub-tab label from 'Today' to 'Daily' and keep the internal id 'today', so it no longer collides with the app's Today screen.

Tests: summarizeFilters for the defaults and for a mixed set; the Filters badge count; on mobile (matchMedia mock) only the summary and button render; useFocusTrap sets initial focus, wraps Tab, and returns focus on Escape, and the existing Modal tests still pass; no FilterBar on /app/arcade and the slim note on /app; the aria-label contains '45'; placeholder snapshots; the Arcade tab label reads 'Daily'.
items.howto: Help article 'analyzer-filters' (apps/web/lib/help/articles/analyzer.ts, created by global-filter-clarity / help-content-backfill). Add a 'Using filters' section covering: the summary line; what each facet means in plain words (ranked ladder vs custom games, game size, length bands, games under 45 s hidden by default); that the Filters button opens the full editor, a bottom sheet on phones; and that Today and Arcade show your live session and daily challenges, so most filters do not apply there. Rename 'Today' to 'Daily' wherever the 'arcade' article mentions the sub-tab.
