items.title: Creator loop: a Publish button that leads somewhere, and a 'Mine' view with your record
items.spec:
Goal: publishing is easy to find from /community, and authors can see and manage what they've published.

1) Publish CTA. In app/community/page.tsx, a new client island apps/web/components/community/PublishCta.tsx.
- It must be a client island: auth() in the server page would break the ISR that public-pages-seo-and-cache adds in wave 5.
- <SignedIn>: a LinkButton (from community-polish-3) 'Publish a build' → /builds?publish=1.
- <SignedOut>: 'Sign in to publish' → signInHref('/builds?publish=1') from lib/authLinks.ts.
- Next to it, a 'How publishing works' disclosure: a button with aria-expanded toggling an inline panel. Don't use a Popover; that primitive arrives in wave 5. The panel has three numbered steps:
  1. 'Save a build to your library — from any game's build order or the editor.'
  2. 'Publish it with your name or anonymously.'
  3. 'Collect votes and update it any time.'
  It ends with a HelpLink to publish-community-builds.

2) Publish picker (apps/web/components/builds/BuildsLibrary.tsx plus a new components/builds/PublishPickerModal.tsx).
- When signed in and the URL has publish=1, open 'Pick a build to publish'. It lists your library builds with a name filter, sorted by updatedAt desc.
- Each row shows name, matchup and a 'Published' badge. A build is published when its slug appears as sourceSlug in /v1/community/my-builds (see step 3).
- Choosing a row closes the picker and opens the existing BuildPublishModal for that build. It is an update when already published.
- publish=<sourceSlug> opens BuildPublishModal for that build directly, which the 'Publish update' links use.
- Either way, router.replace removes the param, so a refresh doesn't reopen the modal.
- Empty library: 'You don't have any saved builds yet.' with actions 'Create a build' and 'Learn how' (help custom-builds).
- Signed out: the visitor-dead-ends intro renders and the param is ignored.

3) Owner API (apps/api/src/services/community.js plus apps/api/src/routes/community.js).
- New GET /community/my-builds (deps.auth), Cache-Control 'private, no-store'.
- Returns the caller's own community rows, anonymous ones included, sorted by updatedAt desc, limit 200. Fields: slug, title, matchup, votes, upCount ($size upvotes), downCount, publishedAt, updatedAt, removed, publishAnonymously, sourceSlug, plus total/wins/losses merged from listOwnerReplayStats by public slug.
- sourceSlug is the caller's own private slug, so it is safe here. It must never appear in public list or detail responses; add a regression test for that.
- Never return voter arrays or other users' rows.

4) Owner record on cards (apps/web/components/community/CommunityOwnerReplayCount.tsx).
- Replace 'N classified replays' with '12 games · 8–4 · 67%'. The percentage is wins/(wins+losses), tinted with the analyzer's win-rate tone helper (the one WinRateCell uses), and hidden when wins+losses = 0.
- 0 games → 'No games with this build yet'.
- Loading becomes a small skeleton bar instead of 'Loading…'.
- Polling: refreshInterval becomes a function, (latest) => latest?.items?.length ? 15000 : 0. Signed-in viewers who own nothing stop polling every 15 s. Keep revalidateOnFocus.
- The owner kebab from community-polish-4 gains 'Edit in library' → /builds/<sourceSlug> and 'Publish update' → /builds?publish=<sourceSlug>, both from my-builds.

5) Mine view.
- CommunityFilterBar gets a 'Mine' toggle, shown in <SignedIn> only, which writes ?mine=1 and clears the other filters.
- In app/community/page.tsx, when mine=1, skip the public fetch and render a new client component, components/community/MyPublishedBuilds.tsx, using useApi('/v1/community/my-builds'). generateMetadata returns robots noindex for ?mine=1.
- Each row shows:
  - the title, linked to the public page
  - the matchup badge
  - VoteScore plus '7 up · 2 down'
  - the record line
  - Published and Updated (fmtDay)
  - an 'Anonymous' badge when publishAnonymously
  - a 'Removed by a moderator' badge when removed
  - the actions 'Edit in library' and 'Publish update'
- Empty: 'You haven't published any builds yet', with 'Publish a build' → /builds?publish=1.
- Signed out with ?mine=1: a sign-in panel using signInHref('/community?mine=1').
- Errors use the community-polish-2 or QueryState retry pattern.

Dependencies:
- Same wave, landing after community-polish-3 (filter bar and LinkButton) and community-polish-4 (owner kebab, VoteScore).
- visitor-dead-ends (wave 1) changes signed-out /builds.
- community-forks-and-trust (wave 6) later adds a saves column and the opt-in public record to these rows and to BuildPublishModal.
- auth-return-to-context (wave 5) hardens signInHref.

Tests:
- PublishCta: signed-in and signed-out hrefs; the disclosure toggles aria-expanded.
- BuildsLibrary:
  - ?publish=1 opens the picker
  - picking a build opens BuildPublishModal and removes the param
  - ?publish=<slug> opens the modal directly
  - empty-library state
- API (communityAndGdpr.test.js):
  - my-builds returns only the caller's rows, including anonymous ones
  - it includes sourceSlug
  - the public list and detail still omit sourceSlug and the vote arrays
  - auth is required
- CommunityOwnerReplayCount:
  - formats '12 games · 8–4 · 67%'
  - hides % with no decided games
  - the refreshInterval function returns 0 for empty items
- MyPublishedBuilds: rows, badges and links; empty state; signed-out panel.
items.howto:
Extend the publish-community-builds help article (apps/web/lib/help/articles/builds.ts, created by builds-correctness-fixes) with these sections:
- #publish-from-community: the Publish a build button opens a picker of your library builds.
- #named-vs-anonymous: anonymous builds never join your author profile.
- #my-published-builds: the Mine view; your record is visible only to you and comes from your classified replays.
- #update-or-remove: Publish update, and removing a build from Community keeps your private copy.

The 'How publishing works' disclosure next to the CTA links to this article.

items.title: Guide outage states with a real 'Try again', and CTAs that know you are signed in
items.spec:
Two problems show on every guide page: outage states give no working next step, and signed-in players are asked to sign up.

A) Outage states that can recover (unavailable-retry)
1. apps/web/components/guides/GuideRetryButton.tsx (new, 'use client') renders a primary 'Try again' button. On click it calls startTransition(() => router.refresh()). While the transition is pending, the button is disabled with aria-busy=true and a Loader2 icon spinning under motion-safe:animate-spin. Double clicks are ignored while pending.
2. apps/web/components/guides/GuideStates.tsx GuideUnavailable gains props {onRetry?: () => void; variant?: 'page' | 'hub'}.
- Description copy: 'The stats service didn't respond. This usually clears within a minute.'
- Action row: the primary is 'Try again', either GuideRetryButton or a plain button calling onRetry when it is passed.
- variant 'page' keeps the secondary 'All build guides' (/guides).
- variant 'hub' drops the self-link. Its secondaries are 'Open your dashboard' (/app) and 'Home' (/).
3. apps/web/app/guides/error.tsx accepts {error, reset}. It passes onRetry={() => startTransition(() => { router.refresh(); reset(); })} (the Next 15 recovery pattern). It keeps the noindex meta and the console.warn digest log.
4. apps/web/app/guides/page.tsx renders <GuideUnavailable variant='hub' title='Build guides are temporarily unavailable'/>. The maps outage (app/guides/maps/page.tsx) and the videos outage (app/guides/videos/page.tsx) get the same Try again.
5. Edge cases:
- ISR build, counter and map pages throw GuideUnavailableError into error.tsx, so reset plus refresh refetches the RSC payload. If the API is still down, the same state re-renders with no loop, because retry only runs on click.
- Keep the 200 + noindex semantics.
6. If help-and-feedback-menu (roadmap wave 1) has merged, add a tertiary 'Report a problem' link that opens its modal. If it hasn't, omit the link (no stub).

B) CTAs that know about sign-in (signed-in-aware-ctas)
1. apps/web/components/guides/GuideCtas.tsx is already a client component; it now reads useAuth().
- While !isLoaded, or when signed out, it renders today's markup unchanged: 'Track your win rate with this build — free' → /sign-up. ISR HTML and crawlers see the same thing, and the button classes are identical, so there is no layout shift.
- Signed in: the primary is 'See your record with this build', an in-page link to #your-record. That id already exists on the Section in BuildTimingsSection.tsx:132. Scroll smoothly only when prefers-reduced-motion is off. The secondary is 'Open my builds' → /app/builds.
- The GA event guide_cta_click gets cta values 'record' | 'my-builds' | 'upload' alongside the existing ones.
2. The GuideNotEnoughGames sign-up button (GuideStates.tsx:71) moves into a tiny client island, GuideAuthCta. Signed out, it keeps 'Sign up free and track your games' → /sign-up. Signed in, it shows 'Upload more games' → /download.
3. apps/web/components/guides/GuidePersonalComparison.tsx
- SignInPrompt links to guideSignInHref(usePathname()), which produces /sign-in?redirect_url=%2Fguides%2Fpvz%2Fx.
- The signed-in empty state's 'upload a few games' becomes a link to /download.
4. apps/web/components/guides/guideAuthLinks.ts (new) exports guideSignInHref(path).
- It accepts only ^/guides(/[a-z0-9-]+){0,3}$: no query, no fragment, no '//', no '..', no encoded characters. Anything else returns '/sign-in'.
- This relies on Clerk 6.9.5 SignIn's native redirect_url handling (same-origin only). That is the mechanism components/reviews/MyReviews.tsx:42 and ReviewPage.tsx:338 already use. app/sign-in only forces a redirect for the /try value.
- Do NOT widen safeAuthRedirect (lib/instant/authRedirect.ts): sign-up must keep routing new accounts through /welcome. Returning new sign-ups to the guide belongs to roadmap auth-return-to-context (wave 5, /welcome?next=). That item will replace guideSignInHref with lib/authLinks signInHref, so leave a comment pointing at it.
5. Conflicts: ghost-synced-practice (wave 4) later replaces the practice CTA in GuideCtas, and auth-return-to-context (wave 5) later reworks the sign-in links. Both build on this pack, so keep the CTA variants in one small function that is easy to extend.

Tests
- components/guides/__tests__/GuideCtas.test.tsx: signed out → /sign-up. Signed in → '#your-record' and /app/builds. Not loaded → the signed-out markup.
- GuidePersonalComparison.test.tsx: the sign-in href carries the encoded redirect_url, and 'upload a few games' links to /download.
- guideAuthLinks.test.ts is table-driven: it rejects '//evil.com', 'https://x', '/guides/../app', '/guides/pvz?x=1', '/guides/pvz#a' and '%2F%2Fevil'.
- A new GuideStates test (mocking next/navigation useRouter) checks that Try again calls router.refresh and that the hub variant has links to /app and /, and none to /guides.
- An error.tsx test checks that Try again calls reset and refresh, and that the noindex meta is still present.
- Update the app/guides/__tests__/hubPage.test.tsx outage case.
items.howto: None needed: the CTA copy explains itself. Roadmap data-states-recovery ships the general 'Something went wrong' article; link it from the outage description once it exists.

items.title: Matchup page: one clear opponent filter with loading feedback, a matchup switcher, and plain-language headers
items.spec:
These items share MatchupGuide.tsx, BuildHero.tsx and the counter pages, so they ship as one PR.

A) Filter clarity (matchup-filter-clarity), in apps/web/components/guides/matchup/BandSwitcher.tsx
1. Replace the three PillGroups with two clearly labelled rows inside <nav aria-label='Filter openers'>.
2. Row 'Starting workers': '12 workers' (current) and '8 workers (patch 5.0.16)'. Build the labels from eraShortLabel in lib/guides/guideCopy.ts, and delete the 'Game' label.
3. Row 'Opponents': the chip 'All opponents' (the unfiltered URL that keeps the era), then an axis switch 'By league | By MMR', then the band chips for the chosen axis.
- The server renders BOTH chip rows as plain crawlable links.
- A small client island, BandAxisToggle, hides the inactive axis row. Its default axis is the active band's type, otherwise league.
- Without JS both rows simply show.
- League and MMR are therefore visibly alternatives, and 'All' visibly clears either one.
4. Visible summary line above the table. guideCopy.ts filterSummaryText({count, band, era}) returns e.g. 'Showing 18 openers vs Diamond opponents · 12 starting workers' or 'Showing 9 openers vs 4500+ MMR opponents · 8 starting workers (patch 5.0.16)'.
- When band or era=before is set, a 'Clear filter' link follows it.
- The sr-only table caption (MatchupGuide.tsx:79) reuses the same string.
5. Pending feedback
- Each chip's label is a client child, FilterPillLabel, that uses useLinkStatus() from next/link (Next 15.5). While pending it shows a spinner (motion-safe) and sets data-pending.
- It reports into a GuideFilterPendingProvider context that wraps the switcher and the table.
- While pending, the table region gets aria-busy=true and opacity-60 (with a transition), and a polite live region reads 'Loading Diamond openers…'.
- Do NOT add app/guides/[matchup]/loading.tsx: it streams a 200 shell before notFound()/permanentRedirect() run, which breaks the 404 and 308 semantics pinned by app/guides/__tests__/segmentConfig.test.ts and matchupPage.test.tsx.
6. Empty filtered state (MatchupGuide.tsx:83-89)
- Copy: 'No opener has enough games vs Diamond opponents yet.'
- Action: a 'Show all opponents' button-link to the unfiltered URL with the same era.
- If era=before also yields nothing, add 'Back to 12-worker openers'.
7. Below sm, each chip row is one horizontally scrolling line (flex-nowrap overflow-x-auto snap-x) with a right fade mask that is shown only when the row overflows. There must be no page-level horizontal overflow at 360 or 375 px.

B) Matchup switcher (matchup-switcher-flip)
1. apps/web/components/guides/MatchupSwitcher.tsx is a new server component: <nav aria-label='Matchups'> with 9 pills grouped by race (Protoss: PvP PvT PvZ · Terran · Zerg).
- Each group shows the race icon (getIconPath(race,'race'), lib/sc2-icons.ts).
- Matchup letters are tinted with raceTint (lib/race.ts:195) through a shared components/guides/MatchupLabel.tsx. guides-polish-5 reuses this component, so create it here.
- The current matchup gets aria-current='page'.
- Links keep the era and drop the band. On the counter-list page they point to guidePaths.counters(slug).
- Below sm the switcher is one scrolling row.
2. Render it under the breadcrumbs on MatchupGuide (published and not-enough-games states alike) and on apps/web/components/guides/counter/CounterList.tsx.
3. In the matchup PageHeader, add 'See it from the Zerg side → ZvP'. Hide it for mirror matchups.
4. In apps/web/components/guides/build/BuildHero.tsx, add the quick links 'All PvZ openers' (guidePaths.matchup) and 'How to beat Zerg openers' (guidePaths.counters).

C) Copy (guide-copy-polish)
1. BuildHero.tsx:60 and CounterGuide.tsx:63/82 replace 'n = 1,203 games from 88 players' with 'Based on 1,203 games from 88 players · updated Oct 21'.
- Format the date with a fixed en-US, UTC formatter (fmtGuideDate).
- Omit the date when computedAt is null, and on pages that already show 'Stats updated'.
2. When BuildHero shows a league headline (lines 26-31), label the second line 'Overall: 55.0% over 1,203 games from 88 players'.
3. CounterGuide.tsx:77-83: drop the duplicate game count.
- Add a verdict chip (Badge) next to the headline. It uses rangeVerdict: win → 'Your race is favoured', even → 'Too close to call', loss → 'Your race is behind'.
- The text comes from a new verdictLabel() in apps/web/components/guides/guideUi.ts. guides-polish-4 extends this helper with glyphs; never duplicate it.
4. 8-worker view: one line above the table, from a guideCopy constant: 'Guide pages cover the 12-worker game, so openers aren't linked here.'

Tests
- matchupPage.test.tsx:
  - 'All opponents' links to the canonical URL, and the era is preserved.
  - There is no 'Game' label.
  - The summary text is right for league:4 and for mmr bands.
  - The empty state has a 'Show all opponents' link.
  - The 8-worker note is present.
  - The switcher has 9 links with aria-current on the current one.
  - The flip link goes to /guides/zvp, and mirrors have none.
- New FilterPillLabel.test.tsx mocks useLinkStatus to return pending and expects a spinner and aria-busy on the region.
- buildPage.test.tsx: no 'n =' text, plus the 'Overall:' label and the quick links.
- counterMapPages.test.tsx: one game count, and the verdict chip text for each verdict.

items.title: Build guide: 'On this page' nav, anchors that clear the sticky header, and one army growth table
items.spec:
This pack is a reading pass on the long build guide (up to 11 sections, BuildGuide.tsx:65-85).

A) Section nav (build-guide-section-nav)
1. apps/web/components/ui/SectionNav.tsx is new, generic and client-side. Props: items: {id,label}[] and an optional 'aria-label'.
- An IntersectionObserver with rootMargin '-120px 0px -60% 0px' sets aria-current='location' on the active link.
- Clicking a link scrolls smoothly only when prefers-reduced-motion is off (otherwise it jumps), and updates the hash with history.replaceState, so no history entries pile up.
- Mobile and below lg: a chip row that sticks under the header (top = header height 3.5rem/4rem + env(safe-area-inset-top)), scrolls horizontally with a fade edge, and auto-scrolls the active chip into view (block 'nearest', inline 'nearest').
- lg and up: a sticky right rail at top-24 inside a main + 14rem aside grid.
- print:hidden.
- Build it generic in components/ui because roadmap game-page-macro-workspace (wave 3) specifies the same sticky scroll-spy nav and should reuse it instead of building a second one.
2. apps/web/components/guides/build/buildGuideSections.ts (new, pure) returns the ordered list of sections that will actually render, using the same conditions BuildGuide uses: Video, By league, Timings, Army, Matchups, Game length, Maps, Leaks, Related, Coach's notes, 8-worker videos. BuildGuide.tsx renders from this list or asserts against it, so the two never drift.
3. apps/web/components/guides/GuideSectionNav.tsx wraps SectionNav and hides itself when fewer than 3 sections render. Place it under the hero in BuildGuide.tsx. Reuse it on CounterGuide.tsx and MapGuide.tsx when they have 3 or more sections.
4. Scroll margin: add GUIDE_SECTION_ANCHOR_CLASS = 'scroll-mt-28 lg:scroll-mt-24' to apps/web/components/guides/guideUi.ts. Apply it to every guide Section that has an id: BuildChartSections, BuildMatchupSections, BuildExtrasSections, BuildTimingsSection, BuildArmySection, and the counter and map pages. That way shared links like /guides/pvz/x#key-timings land with the heading below the sticky header (components/chrome/Header.tsx:70, h-14/sm:h-16) and the mobile chip row.
5. Copy link to section:
- Each guide Section heading gets a small icon button (Link2 icon, aria-label 'Copy link to Key timings', min 44 px target). It shows on hover or focus-within, and always on touch (pointer: coarse).
- It copies origin + pathname + '#id' via navigator.clipboard, and a toast says 'Link copied'.
- If the clipboard is blocked, fall back to a selected read-only input.
- Migrate it to CopyButton when ui-primitives-and-dialogs (wave 5) lands.

B) Army growth table (army-progression-table), in apps/web/components/guides/build/BuildArmySection.tsx
1. md and up: one server-rendered table.
- Rows are the union of units across the 6:00, 8:00 and 10:00 snapshots, ordered by 10:00 presence desc, then 8:00, then 6:00, then name.
- The first column is sticky and holds the unit icon and name.
- Columns are 6:00, 8:00 and 10:00. Each cell shows '×4', a thin presence bar (a decorative div whose width is the percentage) and the text '82%'.
- Absent cells show '—' with sr-only 'not built'.
- Hide a snapshot column that has no data, and note why: 'Not enough games reach 10:00'.
2. Below md: a segmented control (components/ui/Tabs.tsx) with 6:00, 8:00 and 10:00 that switches the existing card. It defaults to the first available snapshot. Without JS the cards stack, as they do today.
3. Caption: replace 'Median count when present' with 'Typical count in games that built it · how often it appears'.

Tests
- buildGuideSections.test.ts: a payload with no video, notes or leaks omits those entries, and the order is stable.

items.title: Readable, accessible stats: verdict glyphs, one Tab stop per chart, a 'How to read these numbers' legend and the guide stats help article
items.spec:
Colour-only verdicts fail WCAG 1.4.1, and first-time readers can't decode 'likely range', the floors or the arrows. This pack fixes both.

A) Accessibility (dataviz-a11y)
1. apps/web/components/guides/guideUi.ts: extend verdictLabel(), which guides-polish-2 created (create it here if that pack hasn't landed), into verdictMeta(verdict) → {glyph: '▲' | '●' | '▼', short: 'ahead' | 'even' | 'behind', phrase: 'clearly above 50%' | 'too close to call' | 'clearly below 50%'}. It is driven by the existing rangeVerdict (guideUi.ts:67-78). This is the one source for every guide surface.
2. apps/web/components/guides/WinRateCell.tsx: an aria-hidden glyph goes before the number, with the sr-only phrase after it. The tint is kept. Add a compact prop that hides the range text below sm and keeps it sr-only (guides-polish-5 and the expansion packs use it).
3. apps/web/components/guides/hub/MatchupGrid.tsx:37: the top-build win rates get the same glyph and sr-only phrase.
4. apps/web/components/guides/CiBarChart.tsx
- barTone (lines 49-53): add the glyph to the value label at the bar end ('56.7% ▲'), and give 'even' bars a hatched SVG <pattern> fill, so all three states differ without colour.
- The figcaption (line 210) adds the colour and glyph legend sentence.
- Roving tabindex: only the active row has tabIndex=0 and the rest have -1. Reuse the existing Arrow/Home/End handler (lines 128-134, 177-189), which moves focus and the active index. The chart becomes one Tab stop (today a build page has about 20).
- Enter, Space or a tap toggles a pinned tooltip (aria-expanded on the row). Escape or a pointerdown outside closes it. Hover still previews.
5. apps/web/components/guides/CiWhisker.tsx (lines 238-245): the same glyph and sr-only verdict next to the point label.

B) Legend (stats-legend-help)
1. apps/web/components/guides/GuideStatsLegend.tsx is a new server component: a collapsed <details> whose summary is 'How to read these numbers'. It contains:
- Swatch + glyph rows: '▲ green: the whole likely range is above 50%', '● too close to call', '▼ red: the whole likely range is below 50%'.
- 'Likely range': 'We're 95% sure the true win rate is inside this range. Fewer games means a wider range.'
- Ranking: 'Openers are ranked by the low end of the range, so a few lucky games can't top the table.'
- Floors: 'A number appears once at least 5 players have played 30 games in it; a guide page needs 100 games.'
- Trend arrows: 'Compared with a snapshot at least 7 days old; moves under 0.5 pp count as flat.'
- 'Updated nightly · last update Oct 21', from computedAt.
- A link 'More in Help: Reading guide stats' → /help/reading-guide-stats.
2. Every number in the legend comes from constants, never literals.
- Add GUIDE_CELL_MIN_USERS = 5 and GUIDE_CELL_MIN_GAMES = 30 next to GUIDE_PAGE_MIN_GAMES in apps/web/lib/guides/guideCopy.ts, with a comment mirroring apps/api/src/config/guides.js.
- Use GUIDE_TREND_FLAT_THRESHOLD from lib/guides/format.ts.
- All copy lives in guideCopy.ts.
3. Placement, once per page, beside the first data Section:
- the matchup openers Section (under the summary line),
- the build page 'By league' Section,
- the first counter Section (CounterGuide.tsx),
- the map matrix Section (MapGuide.tsx).
4. When glossary-and-infotip (roadmap wave 5) lands, wrap 'likely range' in <Term id='likely-range'> and add the glossary ids likely-range, publishing-floor and trend-arrow. Leave a TODO now.

Tests
- New WinRateCell.test.tsx: glyph and sr-only phrase for win, even and loss.
- CiBarChart.test.tsx (update):
  - Exactly one row has tabIndex 0.
  - ArrowDown, Home and End move it.
  - Enter pins the tooltip and Escape closes it.
  - The even bar uses the pattern fill.
- New GuideStatsLegend.test.tsx: the floors and threshold render from the constants, and the help link is right.
- hubPage.test.tsx: top-build glyphs.
- matchupPage.test.tsx, buildPage.test.tsx and counterMapPages.test.tsx: one legend per page.

Order: depends on help-center-foundation (roadmap wave 1) for the /help route. Land before guides-polish-5, which restructures MatchupGrid and must keep the glyph. contrast-tokens-and-a11y-gate and chart-kit (wave 5) later retune the colours. The glyphs stay.
items.howto:
New help article 'Build guides: reading the stats' (slug reading-guide-stats, category builds) in apps/web/lib/help/articles/builds.ts. It renders at /help/reading-guide-stats and in Settings > Help (apps/web/components/analyzer/settings/SettingsHelp.tsx, /settings?tab=help#reading-guide-stats). It covers:
- the data source (ranked 1v1 games uploaded to SC2 Tools; every number computed with fixed rules, no AI),
- the publishing floors,
- the likely range in plain words,
- why the ranking uses the low end,
- colours and glyphs,
- trend arrows,
- band filters (linking build-guides#filtering),
- the 8-worker archive,
- 'Practice it on stream' (linking practice-ghost-build).
The in-page GuideStatsLegend links to it.

items.title: Your own timings and record inside the Key timings table, with on-pace / early / late deltas
items.spec:

- Inside [p25, p75] inclusive is on pace (neutral). Later than p75 is late (warning tone). Earlier than p25 is early (info tone).

- Export it for reuse by roadmap build-dossier-insights (wave 4, community column and delta chip) and map-veto-planner (wave 3).
2. apps/web/lib/guides/useGuideMe.ts (new) wraps useApi(`/v1/guides/me/${matchup}/${build}`) and only fires when signed in. GuidePersonalComparison and the timings table share the SWR key, so there is one request.

items.title: Public profile and replay pages survive share traffic, return real 404s and never dead-end
items.spec:
Goal: a viral link to /p/<handle> or /players/<slug>/replays never 404s a real page, never caches an outage, and never leaves the visitor stuck. Lands in wave 1 alongside visitor-dead-ends. Coordinate with it: if it lands first, reuse its auth-aware not-found actions island and its CloudOff outage panel. Neither blocks the other. public-player-page (wave 5) later replaces /p/[handle] with /players/[player] and must keep every rule below (recorded in that item's augment).

1) Profile fetch and status codes (profile-404-under-load). In apps/web/app/p/[handle]/page.tsx, fetchProfile calls getJsonWithStatus(path, { revalidateSec: 300 }) so the documented ISR window actually caches. lib/serverApi.ts already supports this; only its doc comment changes. Wrap fetchProfile in React cache() so generateMetadata and the page share one request. Only status === 404 calls notFound(). For 429, any 5xx and null (unreachable), throw a PublicFetchError(status) from both generateMetadata and the page instead of rendering a 200 noindex page. Why throw: a thrown render is never stored in the ISR cache; Next keeps serving the last good page when a background revalidation throws; and a first-time visitor gets a 5xx, which crawlers treat as temporary, whereas a 200 noindex can de-index the profile. A rendered 'unavailable' page under revalidate=300 would be cached for 5 minutes. New app/p/[handle]/error.tsx ('use client') renders the unified unavailable state from step 3, with Try again calling reset() and then router.refresh(). Next 15 writes only 200 responses to the data cache, so a 429/5xx is never replayed. Rewrite the page's header comment to match. In apps/api/src/routes/publicProfile.js, add keyGenerator `${req.ip}:${String(req.params.handle || '').toLowerCase()}`, mirroring publicReplays.js:53-54, so one hot profile cannot exhaust every other profile's 60/min budget on the shared Next egress IP.

2) Archive cursor and busy states (archive-cursor-dead-end). In apps/web/app/players/[player]/replays/page.tsx, on status 400 with a cursor in the query, redirect to the same canonical URL with cursor (and page, once profiles-replays-polish-2 adds it) removed, keeping the filters and adding notice=page-expired. parseQuery accepts notice only as that literal value, and queryHref/replayListHref never re-emit it. PublicReplayLibrary renders an inline role=status notice above the list: 'That page link expired. Showing the newest replays.' (or 'oldest replays' when sort=date_asc), with a dismiss link to the URL without notice. A 400 without a cursor renders the unavailable state with no redirect, so it can never loop. A 429 renders the busy variant:
- Title 'Lots of visitors right now', body 'Try again in a few seconds.'
- An aria-live=polite countdown 'Retrying in 10…' that calls router.refresh().
- At most 3 automatic retries per URL. Keep the counter in sessionStorage inside try/catch; if storage is unavailable, retry once.
- Pause the countdown while document.hidden, show a manual Try again at all times, and use no animation under prefers-reduced-motion.
5xx and unreachable keep the outage copy and add 'Back to first page' (a link to the bare archive root) beside Try again whenever the URL has a cursor or filters. The detail page uses the same busy/outage split.

3) One unavailable component. Merge ProfileUnavailable.tsx and PublicReplayUnavailable.tsx into apps/web/components/public-profile/PublicUnavailable.tsx with props { surface: 'profile' | 'archive' | 'analysis', reason: 'busy' | 'outage', resetHref?: string }. Every variant has an sr-only h1, the CloudOff EmptyStatePanel and a Try again Button (router.refresh(), falling back to location.reload()). Titles: 'Profile temporarily unavailable', 'Replay archive temporarily unavailable', 'Replay analysis temporarily unavailable'. Update the imports and delete the two old files.

4) Shared analysis loading and a real 404 (public-states-skeleton-404). Move the analysis-shaped skeleton from app/p/[handle]/replays/[gameId]/loading.tsx to app/players/[player]/replays/[gameId]/loading.tsx, so opening a game no longer shows the list skeleton. Delete app/p/[handle]/replays/loading.tsx; the legacy routes only redirect and keep their redirect pages. In app/players/[player]/replays/[gameId]/page.tsx, wrap the apiFetch in a React cache() loader and call it from generateMetadata, raising notFound() there on a 404 so the status is a real 404, not a streamed 200. Middleware already requires sign-in, so the authenticated fetch works. The page reuses the cached result and keeps its canonical-handle redirect. Add app/p/[handle]/not-found.tsx and app/players/[player]/replays/not-found.tsx (which also covers [gameId]). Both render a new apps/web/components/public-profile/PublicNotFound.tsx:
- Title 'This page is private or no longer shared'.
- Body 'The player may have turned off their public profile or replay sharing, or the link is mistyped.'
- Actions 'Browse community builds' (/community), 'Leaderboard' (/community/leaderboard) and 'Get your own page' (/). No 'Open dashboard'.
- GlowHalo styling as in app/not-found.tsx, and robots noindex.

5) One API call per archive view (archive-metadata-double-fetch). The archive page's generateMetadata takes searchParams, parses them with the same parseQuery, and calls the same React cache()-wrapped fetchReplays(player, query), so metadata and page share one API call. app/players/[player]/replays/opengraph-image.tsx calls /v1/public/replays/:handle?limit=1&fields=profile. apps/api/src/routes/publicReplays.js accepts fields=profile (only that literal) and returns { profile, items: [], page: { hasMore: false } } without shaping rows or resolving VODs.

Edge cases: legacy opaque ids still redirect to the canonical slug, with notice and cursor handled as above. A profile 404 stays indistinguishable from a private profile. The cursor-expired redirect always targets the canonical handle.

Tests:
- components/public-profile/__tests__/PublicProfilePage.test.tsx: add 429 and 500 cases (they throw PublicFetchError, not notFound). Keep the 404 case. Update the unreachable case, which now throws. Assert next.revalidate is 300 and there is one fetch per render.
- PublicReplays.test.tsx: 400 with a cursor redirects without the cursor and with notice; 400 without a cursor renders unavailable; 429 renders the busy copy and countdown (fake timers); the notice is not carried into pager links; metadata and page share one fetch; the detail generateMetadata raises notFound on 404.
- apps/api/__tests__/publicProfile.test.js: the limiter is per handle (61 hits on A give 429 while B still returns 200).
- apps/api/__tests__/publicReplaysRoute.test.js: fields=profile skips the VOD resolver.
- apps/web/tests/e2e/public-pages.spec.ts: /players/<missing>/replays returns a 404 with the new copy and no 'Open dashboard' link.

items.title: Replay archive browsing: instant filters with chips, map and date filters, a filtered record, and a pager that points the right way
items.spec:
Depends on profiles-replays-polish-1, which changes the same page.tsx and PublicReplayLibrary.tsx. The filtered summary ships with the filter UX even though it is a feature expansion, because the matchup and map selects are fed by the same aggregation's facets. Reuse the chip look from global-filter-clarity (wave 1): extract its presentational chip to apps/web/components/ui/FilterChip.tsx if it isn't shared already. replay-library-control (wave 3) must apply its excluded-games guard through the same match builder, so the summary and facets below stay correct. public-player-page (wave 5) embeds this library unchanged as the Replays tab.

1) One query helper. New apps/web/components/public-profile/archiveQuery.ts owns PublicReplayQuery, parseArchiveQuery(raw) and archiveHref(root, query, overrides). Move parseQuery and replayListHref out of app/players/[player]/replays/page.tsx and queryHref out of PublicReplayLibrary.tsx into it. Allow-listed keys:
- search (≤100 chars)
- result (win|loss|tie)
- matchup (/^[PTZR]v[PTZR]$/)
- map (≤64 chars, trimmed)
- range (7d|30d|season)
- build (≤120 chars)
- sort (date_desc|date_asc)
- cursor (≤512 chars)
- page (integer 1–1000)
- notice (page-expired)
Unknown keys are dropped.

2) Filtered summary and facets (archive-filtered-summary).
API: replayLibrary.list() in apps/api/src/services/replayLibrary.js gains an option withSummary. When set, it runs one aggregation in parallel with the page query, using the same $match minus the cursor clause, sort and limit, and returns { total, wins, losses, ties, avgDurationSec }. It also returns facets { matchups: string[], maps: string[] }, with maps sorted by game count and capped at 30. Facets are computed over the player's whole public set, without filters, and cached per owner for 10 minutes in a small in-process LRU (max 500 entries), so the selects stay stable while filtering. apps/api/src/routes/publicReplays.js passes withSummary: true and shapes only those numeric and label fields. apps/web/components/analyzer/replays/types.ts adds summary? and facets?, and sets total? from summary.total.
Page: app/players/[player]/replays/page.tsx maps range to since/until for the API: 7d and 30d count back from the request time, and season comes from lib/datePresets.ts via resolvePreset(currentSeasonPresetId()). It also forwards map and build, which apps/api/src/util/parseQuery.js already accepts.
Web: replace '{n} replays on this page' (PublicReplayLibrary.tsx:123-126) with a summary strip:
- Unfiltered: '312 replays · 180–129 · 58% · avg 13:05'.
- Filtered: lead with the active filter labels, e.g. 'PvZ · Losses: 41 replays · avg 11:20'.
- Show W–L and % only when no result filter is set and there is at least 1 decided game. Colour the % with wrColor(rate, decided), W with text-success and L with text-danger.
- Add '· 2 ties' only when ties > 0.
- Show no strip when total is 0; the empty state already explains.
- Keep paging context on the right: 'Page 3 · Showing 51–75'.

3) Instant, visible filters (archive-filter-ux). A new 'use client' apps/web/components/public-profile/ArchiveFilterEnhancer.tsx wraps the existing GET form:
- A select change calls form.requestSubmit().
- Search submits 400 ms after typing stops when the value is empty or has 2+ characters. Enter submits immediately.
- The Apply button stays in the form for no-JS visitors and is hidden once the enhancer mounts.
- Submitting drops cursor and page.
- A clear (×) IconButton sits inside the search input while it has a value (aria-label 'Clear search').
Under the form, render a chip row server-side as plain links, so it works without JS. There is one chip per active key: 'PvZ ×', 'Losses ×', '“Alcyone” ×', 'Map: Alcyone ×', 'Last 30 days ×', 'Build: Glaive Adept ×', 'Oldest first ×'. Each chip links to archiveHref without that key, cursor or page, with aria-label 'Remove filter: Losses'. 'Clear all' appears when 2 or more chips are active and replaces the old Clear button.
Selects:
- Matchup lists facets.matchups, falling back to the full 12 when facets are missing, and always includes the current URL value so the select reflects state.
- A new Map select is fed by facets.maps, with 'All maps' first.
- A new Date select offers All time, Last 7 days, Last 30 days and This season. The URL keeps the range keyword, not raw dates, so a shared link rolls forward.

4) A pager that points the right way (pagination-direction-labels).
- Labels depend on sort. date_desc: '← Back to newest' and 'Older replays →'. date_asc: '← Back to oldest' and 'Newer replays →'.
- The next link carries page+1. Old links that have a cursor but no page show 'Showing more' without a number.
- Pager hrefs end in #replay-results. The results region (toolbar plus list) gets id='replay-results', tabIndex={-1} and scroll-mt-24, and the enhancer focuses it after navigation when the hash is #replay-results.
- No 'Previous page' link: browser Back covers it, and a cursor stack would bloat shareable URLs.

Edge cases: an unknown map or build gives the 'No replays match these filters' empty state, with the chips still removable. Removing a chip always drops cursor and page. notice is never re-emitted. Facet failures fall back to the full lists. The build key is what profile drilldowns link to later (profiles-replays-expansion-2).

Tests:
- components/public-profile/__tests__/PublicReplays.test.tsx: labels flip on date_asc; page increments and the hash is present; each chip removes exactly one key and drops cursor/page; Clear all; matchup options are limited to facets, with the fallback; the enhancer calls requestSubmit on select change and on debounced search (fake timers); summary strip formatting for unfiltered, filtered, ties and zero; range maps to since/until.
- apps/api/__tests__/replayLibraryService.test.js: the summary equals a manual count under filters and ignores the cursor; facets ignore filters and are cached.
- apps/api/__tests__/publicReplaysRoute.test.js: summary and facets are allow-listed.
- e2e: with JavaScript disabled, Apply still filters.

items.title: Shared analysis page: Back keeps your filters, older/newer game, section nav, one set of stream chips, clickable macro leaks
items.spec:
Wave 2, after profiles-replays-polish-2 (archiveQuery.ts) and profiles-replays-polish-3 (the single public Analysis action). The headline item is an impact-4 ease-of-use fix, so the pack goes in wave 2. The small macro-leak expansion rides along because it is in the same component. Nothing here reworks roadmap-owned files. This pack creates three shared pieces that wave-3 items should reuse rather than rebuild:
- apps/web/components/ui/SectionNav.tsx, for game-page-macro-workspace's Overview · Replay · Macro · Builds nav.
- The (date, _id) neighbor comparator in apps/api/src/services/replayLibrary.js, for game-nav-and-replay-controls' /v1/games/:id/neighbors.
- The from-param validator shape.
Recommend that game-nav-and-replay-controls use the same plain ←/→ keys outside the replay stage, because Alt+← is the browser's Back.

1) Back keeps your list, plus older/newer game (detail-return-and-prev-next).
- from param: PublicReplayLibrary passes listQuery to ReplayList. That is archiveHref's query string for the current view, including cursor and page. ReplayList appends ?from=<encodeURIComponent(listQuery)> to public Analysis links only.
- Validation: the detail page parses from with parseArchiveQuery (allowlist, ≤512 chars). It accepts a query string only, never a path, so the back link is always /players/<slug>/replays?<sanitised>. '//evil.com', 'javascript:' or junk fall back to the bare root.
- Back label: built from the active filter labels (matchup, result, map, date range, quoted search, build), e.g. 'Back to PvZ · Losses', with '· page 3' added when page > 1. Fallback: 'Back to {name}'s replays'.
- Neighbors API: GET /v1/public/replays/:handle/:gameId (apps/api/src/routes/publicReplays.js) accepts the same filter params, without cursor or page, and returns neighbors: { olderGameId: string|null, newerGameId: string|null }. A new replayLibrary.neighbors(ownerId, gameId, filters) makes two indexed findOne calls on the same public match as list(): detector-view labels, sharing eligibility, and later the excluded guard. It orders by (date, _id), with _id as the tie-break, and projects _id only.
- Buttons: '‹ Older game' and 'Newer game ›' LinkButtons in the analysis hero, both carrying the same from. At an end, the button renders aria-disabled (not a link) with title 'This is the oldest game in this list' (or newest). Without from, neighbors come from the unfiltered archive. If the game isn't in the filtered set, both are null and the buttons are hidden.
- Keyboard: plain ←/→ navigate. Ignore them when any modifier is held (Alt+← must stay browser Back), when focus is in input, textarea, select, contenteditable or [role=slider], or inside the InteractiveTimeline scrubber.
- Inline hint 'Tip: ← / → moves between games' next to the buttons, hidden under @media (hover: none). Keep the default next/link prefetch.
- Page: apps/web/app/players/[player]/replays/[gameId]/page.tsx reads searchParams.from, forwards the sanitised filters to the cached detail loader from profiles-replays-polish-1, and passes from and neighbors to PublicReplayAnalysis. Add neighbors to PublicReplayDetailResponse in apps/web/components/analyzer/replays/types.ts.

2) One set of stream chips and a section nav (detail-dedupe-section-nav).
- Hero (PublicReplayAnalysis.tsx:119): replace the full GameStreamLinks with one chip, 'Watch POV (2)' with the Radio icon, linking to #watch.
- The 'Watch the game' card gets id='watch' and scroll-mt-24, and keeps the full chips.
- apps/web/components/analyzer/GameStreamLinks.tsx gains an ariaLabel prop (default 'Game streams'). The Watch card passes 'Stream recordings of this game'; compact table cells pass 'Streams for {context}'.
- Add id='build-orders' and scroll-mt-24 to the build-order section (:189).
- Add a sticky SectionNav under the stat row: Timeline (#replay-analysis) · Macro (#macro-breakdown) · Build orders (#build-orders) · Watch (#watch, only when streams exist). IntersectionObserver scroll-spy sets aria-current='true' on the active pill. On mobile it becomes a horizontally scrollable pill bar. Smooth scrolling is off under prefers-reduced-motion.
- Component API: SectionNav takes { items: { id, label }[] }.

3) Macro leaks that seek, and a readable score (macro-leaks-expand-seek).
- In MacroLeakCard (PublicReplayAnalysis.tsx:211-235), each leak with a numeric time shows a timestamp button (mm:ss, e.g. '6:42', aria-label 'Jump timeline to 6:42'). It calls setScrubTime(time) and scrolls #replay-analysis into view. When timelineAvailable is false, the time is plain text.
- When all_leaks has more than 3 entries, add a 'Show all N leaks' disclosure (button with aria-expanded). It lists them all (the API caps at 50), sorted by penalty descending, with the total line '≈ 1,240 minerals lost across 14 leaks' (summing mineral_cost where present).
- Move macroTone from ReplayList.tsx:429-434 into apps/web/lib/format.ts as macroScoreTone(score): ≥80 success, 60–79 warning, <60 danger, null neutral. ReplayList imports it. The detail 'Macro score' StatCard (:129) uses it to colour the value and gets the hint 'out of 100'.

Tests:

items.title: Player page overview and sharing: clean hero and KPIs, drill into matching replays, one Share button, real per-game link previews
items.spec:
Wave 5. public-player-page reworks PublicProfile.tsx into the /players/[player] Overview tab, and ui-primitives-and-dialogs provides LinkButton and CopyButton/useCopy, so this pack lands after:
- public-player-page PR A (the Overview tab, with replayArchive in the payload).

It shares the OG card helpers and the fixed en-US SSR formatter with public-pages-seo-and-cache. try-conversion-pack changes GetYourOwnCTA's copy in the same wave, so rebase onto it. per-game-share-link (wave 6) reuses the per-game OG card drawn here for /g/[token].

1) Profile hero and KPIs without repeats (profile-hero-kpi-cleanup).
- In PublicProfile.tsx (now the Overview tab), the hero description becomes identity copy: 'Protoss player · Member since Mar 2024 · 4 published builds'.
- Omit the race when it is unknown or there are 0 games. Omit the builds part when there are 0. Use '1 published build' for one.
- This replaces 'Member {fmtAgo}' (:88-92, which renders as 'Member 3/14/2024') and the games/W–L/% sentence (:96-100) that repeats the KPI strip.

3) One Share button, and Button everywhere (consolidate-share-buttons).

It uses navigator.share when available (AbortError returns it to idle); otherwise it copies and shows a toast; otherwise it falls back to CopyButton's selected read-only input. No window.prompt.

(d) New app/players/[player]/replays/[gameId]/opengraph-image.tsx: a 1200×630 satori card in the archive OG palette, with a result colour bar, matchup badge, map name, length, both build labels and '{name}'s replay · SC2 Tools'. items.title: Reviews: no silent failures, and one map pin per composer
items.spec:
Bug sweep. Land after data-states-recovery (W1) and use its components/ui/RequestError (friendly copy + Retry + error id). If it has not merged yet, use an inline

with a ghost and the same copy, then swap. 1) Close request, which currently fails silently (ReviewPage.tsx RequestHeader.close, L243-252). Add catch(err) and setCloseError(err.message || "Couldn't close this request. Check your connection and try again."). Render it under the action row as role='alert' text-danger, with a 'Try again' button that re-runs the POST without asking for confirmation again. Clear it on retry and on success. Do not call onChanged on failure. Leave window.confirm in place: reviews-coaching-polish-4 replaces it with ConfirmDialog. 2) Leaderboard and digest toggles (ReviewBoardSidebar.tsx LeaderboardOptIn.toggle, L89-97). Make them optimistic. Keep prev = me.data, then me.mutate({...prev,[key]:value},{revalidate:false}). On success, store the PATCH response and call onChanged(). On failure, run me.mutate(prev,{revalidate:false}) so the checkbox snaps back, and show role='alert' "Couldn't save that setting. Try again." under the checkboxes, cleared on the next toggle. Extract this into a useReviewerPrefs() hook in the same file so reviews-coaching-expansion-2 can reuse it. When me.error is set (today it returns null), show "Your reviewer settings couldn't load · Try again" (me.mutate()). 3) ReviewBoardLoader.tsx (admin rollout stage). Branch on the error's HTTP status (ClientApiError.status): - 403 or 404: keep 'Reviews are in an admin-only preview.' - network, timeout or 5xx: EmptyStatePanel with the CloudOff icon, title "Couldn't load the review board", body "The review service didn't respond. Nothing was lost." and a 'Try again' button (req.mutate(), loading while req.isValidating). Replace the single h-40 pulse with 3 skeleton rows shaped like ReviewCard (h-24 rounded-xl border-2 border-line). 4) MyReviews.tsx, 'Reviews you've written' (L218 renders null). While !mine.data && !mine.error, show two h-20 skeleton rows (aria-busy). On mine.error, show the same error-with-Try-again (mine.mutate()) as the requests section. Upgrade the requests section's static 'Try again in a moment' (L199-200) to include a real Try again button. The 404 path is unchanged. 5) Map pin ownership (shared-draft-pin-bug). In ReviewPage, replace the shared draftPin and pinMode with draftPins: Record and pickingFor: owner | null, where owner is 'root' or the parent comment id. - onTogglePinMode(owner) sets or clears pickingFor. - onWorldClick writes draftPins[pickingFor] and clears pickingFor. - ThreadContext (ReviewThread.tsx) takes pinFor(owner), pickingFor, onTogglePinMode(owner) and onClearPin(owner). A reply composer uses owner = c.id. - Posting or cancelling a reply clears only its own pin (fixes L262 wiping the top-level pin). Top-level cancel and post clear only 'root'. - Map markers render each open draft's pin as '+'. - Pin chip copy (ReviewComposer.tsx L139): replace 'Pin at (123, 87)' with 'Pinned on map · becomes pin {pins.size+1}'. Keep the X button with aria-label 'Remove map pin'. - The pin-mode button reads 'Click the map to place the pin…' only in the composer that is picking. Tests (vitest + RTL in components/reviews/__tests__): - Close failure shows the alert, and Try again re-posts. - A toggle failure rolls the checkbox back and shows the alert. - The loader shows different copy for 404, 503 and a network error, and Retry calls mutate. - The written-reviews section shows its skeleton and error states. - With the root and a reply composer both open, a world click pins only the picking composer. - Posting the reply keeps the root pin. - The chip never shows coordinates.

items.title: Review board: filter chips and race filter, honest pagination, compact sidebar, and a game picker for Ask
items.spec:
Ordering:
- Lands after visitor-dead-ends (W1), which edits the same board page.tsx for the signed-out strip.
- Lands after global-filter-clarity (W1): reuse its chip look. If it exported a generic chip into components/ui, use that; otherwise create components/reviews/ActiveFilterChips.tsx with the same styling.
- Lands after reviews-coaching-polish-1 (loader and sidebar error states).
- Keep edits to AskForReviewButton.tsx to imports only. reviews-coaching-polish-3 owns the form internals in the same wave.

A) Filters (lib/reviews.ts, ReviewBoardFilters.tsx, page.tsx, apps/api/src/services/reviews.js)
1. Add race: 'P'|'T'|'Z'|null to BoardFilters. parseBoardFilters accepts ?race=P|T|Z and boardQuery writes it.
2. An exact matchup wins: if a matchup is set whose first letter differs from race, drop race. When race is set, the Matchup select lists only matchups that start with it.
3. API board(): accept query.race matching /^[PTZ]$/. When no exact matchup is given, set filter.matchup = {$regex: '^' + race + 'v'} (anchored prefix, so the index still applies). Make sure the route passes race through.
4. Replace the three raw <select>s with ui/Select (size sm) inside ui/Field labels: Race (asker race), Matchup, League, Focus. Keep the Hot/New/Top group and Unanswered.
5. generateMetadata adds the race to the title scope ('Protoss replay reviews…') and to the canonical URL.
6. New server component ActiveFilterChips under the bar. One chip per active filter (Race: Protoss, Matchup: PvZ, League: Diamond, Focus: Macro, Unanswered). Each chip is a <Link> to boardQuery without that key and without cursor, with aria-label 'Remove filter Matchup: PvZ'. Add a 'Clear all' link that keeps only sort. Render nothing when no filter is active. Links keep URLs canonical, so the server-rendered, cacheable board still works without JS.
7. Empty state (page.tsx L103-108):
- Filters active: title 'No requests match these filters', actions 'Clear filters' and AskAboutGameButton (signed in).
- No filters: 'No open requests yet' with the Ask button.
8. Pagination: when ?cursor is set, show a caption 'Showing older requests' and a '← Newest' link (boardQuery(filters)) next to 'Older requests →'. Both keep rel=nofollow.
9. Admin stage (page.tsx L77-84): also render ReviewBoardFilters, ActiveFilterChips and the aside. ReviewBoardLoader takes cursor and renders the same Newest/Older links from req.data.nextCursor.
10. loading.tsx mirrors the real layout: header block, a filter-bar row of 4 pill skeletons, then the lg:grid-cols-[minmax(0,1fr)_320px] grid with 4 card skeletons and an aside Card skeleton (title bar plus 5 rows), so nothing jumps.

B) Sidebar (ReviewCard.tsx, ReviewBoardSidebar.tsx)
1. ReviewCard gets variant 'full' | 'compact' (default full, unchanged).
- Compact: no MapArtwork thumbnail and no pr-14/pr-16 padding.
- One meta line: matchup badge · band · age · n reviews. The question uses line-clamp-2.
- The replay download (variant 'card', icon only) sits inline at the end of the meta line instead of absolutely positioned.
2. HelpWithList:
- Loading: 3 compact skeleton rows (aria-busy).
- Error: "Couldn't load requests for you · Try again" (mutate) instead of null.
- Items use variant='compact'.
- Footer link 'See all {Race} requests →' to /reviews?race=<letter>&unanswered=1, from data.verified race.
- reason=unverified keeps its copy and adds a /download link.
3. Mobile: extract a client HelpWithPanel with placement 'inline' | 'aside'. SWR dedupes /v1/reviews/for-me, so both placements share one fetch.
- Below lg, page.tsx renders <details className='lg:hidden'> above the main list, with summary 'Requests you can help with (n)', collapsed by default. Remember the open state in localStorage 'sc2tools:reviews:helpwith-open' (try/catch).

C) Ask picker (new components/reviews/AskGamePicker.tsx)
1. AskAboutGameButton (client) renders the primary 'Ask about one of your games' CTA. It is shown only when reviewsVisible(isAdmin), like AskForReviewButton, and replaces the /app/replays link in the board header.

4. MyReviews empty state (L203-208) uses AskAboutGameButton, plus a secondary 'Browse your replays' link.

Tests:

items.title: Writing reviews and requests: drafts that survive, Ctrl/Cmd+Enter, a real edit mode, and focus-range inputs that work on phones
items.spec:
Shares W2 with reviews-coaching-polish-2, which only imports AskForReviewDialog, and reviews-coaching-polish-4, which edits the comment header and menu in ReviewThread.tsx. This pack edits the edit-mode block and the Ask form internals.

1) Draft autosave. New lib/reviewDrafts.ts with loadDraft, saveDraft, clearDraft and pruneDrafts.
- Key: 'sc2tools:review-draft:v1:<requestId>:<parentId ?? root>'. Value: {body, start, end, savedAt}.
- Wrap every storage call in try/catch (private mode, quota, blocked storage). The composer must work without storage.
- Drafts expire after 14 days and are pruned on first use. Keep at most 20; drop the oldest.
- ReviewComposer saves, debounced 500 ms, whenever body.trim() is non-empty. It clears on a successful post and on discard.
- On mount, if a draft exists, restore body and range (range only if it still fits durationSec). Show a notice row: 'Draft restored (at 5:12) · Use current time · Discard'. Discard clears storage and resets the fields.

2) Discard confirmation. Cancel (L181) with a non-empty body opens ui/ConfirmDialog intent='danger': title 'Discard this comment?', description 'Your text will be removed from this browser.', confirm 'Discard', cancel 'Keep editing'. An empty body cancels immediately.

3) Keyboard submit. In the textarea's onKeyDown, (ctrlKey || metaKey) + Enter calls preventDefault() and submit(). Skip it while busy or while e.nativeEvent.isComposing (IME).
- Default help line: 'At least 10 characters · Ctrl+Enter to post', or '⌘+Enter' on Mac. Detect the platform after mount to avoid a hydration mismatch.
- The submit button gets aria-keyshortcuts='Control+Enter Meta+Enter'.

4) Edit mode (ReviewThread.tsx L186-194). Extract CommentEditor (next to ReviewComposer) and use it in CommentCard.
- Same textarea styling as the composer.
- Inline validation with validateComment({body, gameTimeSec: c.gameTimeSec, endTimeSec: c.endTimeSec}, durationSec), using aria-invalid and aria-describedby, plus the remaining-characters counter.
- Ctrl/Cmd+Enter saves.
- ui/Button size sm with loading={busy} for Save, and a ghost Cancel. Cancel with changed text uses the same ConfirmDialog.
- Countdown 'Editable for 12 more min' from createdAt + REVIEW_LIMITS.EDIT_WINDOW_MS, re-rendered every 30 s.
- At zero: 'The 15-minute edit window has closed. Copy your text before cancelling.' and Save is disabled.
- If createdAt is null, omit the countdown. API errors such as an expired window show inline.

5) Ask dialog guard (AskForReviewButton.tsx AskForReviewForm).
- The form is dirty when the question, tags or either range field is non-empty.
- While dirty, pass disableScrimClose to Modal.
- Route Esc (Modal onClose) and the Cancel button through a guard: when dirty and not submitting, open ConfirmDialog 'Discard this request?' (Keep editing / Discard).

6) Focus-range inputs (L236/L238).
- inputMode='text' (the iOS numeric keypad has no ':'), autoComplete='off'.
- Live echo under the inputs (aria-live='polite', referenced by aria-describedby): 'Focus 5:00–6:30 of 14:12' when valid.
- When a field is all digits, e.g. '500', echo '500 reads as 8:20 (seconds). Did you mean 5:00?' with a 'Use 5:00' button. New helper digitsToClock in lib/reviews.ts treats the last two digits as seconds when ≤59 ('500' → '5:00', '1230' → '12:30').
- parseClock is unchanged because markdown time links use it.
- Quick chips above the inputs: 'Early 0:00–5:00', 'Mid 5:00–10:00', 'Late 10:00–end' and 'Whole game' (clears both fields). Clamp to durationSec, hide chips that start after the game ends, and set aria-pressed when the current range matches a chip.

7) 'Who should review' and 'Visibility' (L245-257) use ui/Field + ui/Select with hints:
- "'My league or higher' is checked against each reviewer's league, verified from their own ranked games."
- 'Link only: not listed on the board and not indexed by search engines. Anyone with the link can open it.'

Tests:
- Draft save, restore and clear, with mocked localStorage; when storage throws, the composer still posts.
- Cancel with text opens the confirm.
- Ctrl+Enter submits and is ignored during composition.
- Edit: countdown text, expiry disables Save, validation messages, Save shows loading.
- Ask: a scrim click doesn't close a dirty form; Esc asks to confirm.
- digitsToClock and the echo suggestion; chips set and clamp ranges.

items.title: Review page chrome: one Share menu, asker tools, request reporting, comment times, accessible menus and ConfirmDialog
items.spec:
Relationship to ui-primitives-and-dialogs (W5): that item lists the window.confirm calls in ReviewThread and ReviewPage for migration. This pack removes them now, using the existing components/ui/ConfirmDialog. When W5 ships useConfirm, Popover and CopyButton, it may swap these call sites over and base ReviewMenu on useFocusTrap's helpers, but these files must not reappear in its uiLint baseline. Lands after reviews-coaching-polish-1 (close error state).

1) New components/reviews/ReviewMenu.tsx, a WAI-ARIA menu button.
- Trigger: aria-haspopup='menu', aria-expanded, aria-controls.
- Popup: role='menu' with role='menuitem' buttons or links.
- Open with click, Enter, Space or ArrowDown (focus the first item), or ArrowUp (focus the last).
- ArrowUp/ArrowDown/Home/End move focus with a roving tabindex.
- Esc and an outside pointerdown close the menu and return focus to the trigger. Tab closes it.
- Supports a second step, such as 'Report…' swapping the list for reasons and focusing the first reason.
- Right-aligned; flips upward near the bottom of the viewport; items are at least 40 px tall.

2) Request header (ReviewPage.tsx RequestHeader, L283-312). The action row becomes: [Download replay (when shared)] [Share ▾] [⋯].
- Share on a coarse pointer with navigator.share: one tap calls navigator.share({title: headline, url}). Ignore AbortError; on any other error, fall back to the menu.
- Share elsewhere: a ReviewMenu with 'Post to Reddit' as a real <a href={redditShareUrl(absolute)} target='_blank' rel='noopener noreferrer'> (absolute URL computed after mount), 'Copy for Discord' and 'Copy link'.
- Copy success shows toast.success('Link copied'). When the clipboard fails, show a selected read-only input with the text inside the menu. Remove window.prompt.

items.title: Review navigation: working #comment and ?t= links, copy links to a comment or moment, step through comments, filters and shortcuts
items.spec:

2) Reduced motion. scrollToComment (L104-107) uses behavior useReducedMotion() ? 'auto' : 'smooth'. Use the hook in lib/useChartTheme.ts until appearance-and-formats (W6) consolidates the hooks.

3) Copy links. Seeking never rewrites the URL; only these explicit actions produce links.

- The composer gets a 'Copy link at 5:12' text button beside its time chip: `${origin}${request.url}?t=5:12`.

4) Stepper in the thread header (ReviewThread.tsx): '‹ Prev · 3 of 12 · Next ›'.
- It walks visible comments with gameTimeSec, top-level and replies, sorted by time then createdAt.

- 'In focus range', shown only when request.timeRange exists: the comment's [start, end] overlaps the range.

7) Shortcuts. A document keydown handler, ignored when:
- the target is an input, textarea, select or contenteditable;
- any modifier is held;
- focus is inside [data-replay-stage];
- a dialog is open.
Keys: N / P go to the next or previous comment (the replayer's next/previous-marker keys). C opens the composer at the current time, when canComment. ? opens a 'Keyboard shortcuts' popover listing these keys and the replay keys. items.spec:

- Coaching rule (coaching/LOCKER_SITE_INTEGRATION.md): facts only, with no grades or scores. W-L, counts, streaks and schedule pace are facts.

1) Assign again. Every AssignmentCard (coach or admin, in any state including cancelled) gets a secondary 'Assign again' that opens AssignmentModal prefilled by a pure nextWindowDraft(assignment, todayKey) in coachingPracticeModel.ts.

- Recurring plans align to the next period boundary, as defaultCalendarRange does.

2) State filters. API GET /coaching/assignments accepts state=active|upcoming|ended|cancelled, filtered on stored fields only (startsAt and endsAt are stored UTC dates):
- active: status active && startsAt ≤ now < endsAt
- upcoming: status active && startsAt > now
- ended: status active && endsAt ≤ now
- cancelled: status cancelled
It also returns counts {active, upcoming, ended, cancelled, all} via countDocuments on the same role-scoped filter, with no progress computation.
UI chips above the grid: 'Active (n)', 'Upcoming (n)', 'Ended (n)', 'Cancelled (n)', 'All (n)'. Default to Active when n > 0, otherwise All. Ended cards keep their Met or Missed pill from progress.state. Changing a chip resets the page to 1.

It requests /v1/coaching/assignments?state=active&limit=100 without studentId; the API already returns every accepted student's plans (coaching.js L1036-1052). - student;
- active plans;
- behind schedule: currentBucket.playedGames < floor(requiredGames × elapsed fraction of the bucket), shown as 'Behind schedule · 2 of 5 games, 2 days left';

- met: success; missed: danger (past and !complete); current: accent ring; upcoming: dim.

- Show 'Streak: 3 weeks', counting consecutive met buckets up to the last finished one.

items.title: Stream tools fail safely: overlays reconnect, dead links explain themselves, and the Dock never overwrites or loses your work
items.spec:
One PR covering how every streamer surface fails. Today an API blip can blank an OBS source until it is refreshed by hand, a revoked link looks like a quiet scene, and the Dock can wipe saved goals or b-roll, or throw away what the streamer typed.

A. Shared overlay socket (overlay-handshake-retry)
- Add createOverlaySocket(token, {surface:'all-in-one'|'widget'|'scene'|'dock', widget?, onStatus, ...existing handshake auth fields}) to apps/web/components/overlay/overlayResilience.ts, modelled on lib/useUserSocket.ts:65-86.
- On connect_error with err.message==='invalid_overlay_token', set status 'invalid', close the socket and stop retrying.
- Any other connect_error (overlay_unsupported, or an exception thrown by the resolver, which apps/api/src/socket/auth.js:197-199 forwards) calls socket.connect() again with capped exponential backoff: 1, 2, 4 … 30 s, ±20% jitter, reset on 'connect'. It also retries immediately on window 'online'.
- Status sequence: 'connecting' → 'connected' → 'reconnecting' (only after the existing 5 s debounce) → 'invalid' (terminal). Clear all timers and listeners on unmount. The socket must survive StrictMode double-mount without connecting twice.
- Use the helper in OverlayClient.tsx:370-381, OverlayWidgetClient.tsx:590-601, overlay/scenes/OverlaySceneClient.tsx:139-148 and lib/multichat/useStudioUpdates.ts:29-36. useStudioUpdates now also returns {status}. ReconnectDot now shows during a refused handshake.
- OverlaySceneClient also calls attachOverlayResilience, for resync and heartbeat.
- surface and widget are passed now so that overlay-presence-health (wave 4) only has to add them to the handshake auth. realtime-one-connection leaves overlay sockets alone.

B. Dead-link states (dead-link-states)
- New apps/web/components/overlay/OverlaySetupCard.tsx with reason 'invalid-token'|'unknown-widget'|'unknown-scene'. token-rotation (wave 4) will add 'replaced', so build the card to accept new reasons.
- Layout: max 360 px wide, bottom-left, overlay font. It never prints the token.
- Copy: title 'This overlay link no longer works', body 'It was revoked or mistyped. Copy a fresh URL from sc2tools.com → Settings → Overlay.'
- After 60 s the card collapses to a small 'Overlay link invalid' pill. It stays noticeable in the OBS preview without dominating a live stream.
- The three overlay clients render the card when status is 'invalid'.
- app/overlay/[token]/widget/[name]/page.tsx:283-292 and scene/[name]/page.tsx:351-360 replace the raw red list of every id with the card, for example 'There's no widget called "opponnent". Did you mean "opponent"?'. The suggestion comes from a small pure helper (Levenshtein ≤3 against the known widget ids or VALID_SCENES). With no close match, the card only points to Settings.
- ?check=1 on any overlay URL shows a badge in the top-left for 10 s, then hides it. States: 'Connected · waiting for a game', 'Connected · live game', 'Reconnecting…', 'Link invalid'.
- Dock: DockClient.tsx:99 and :238 treat a 401 invalid_overlay_token as terminal. They stop the studio retry loop (:258-261) and the platform-config fetch, then render a full-panel 'This Dock link no longer works' state with an 'Open Overlay settings' link to /settings?tab=overlay. This replaces the endless 'Loading chat settings…' (DockChat.tsx:238-239). The same panel shows when the socket reports 'invalid'. A non-terminal outage shows a one-line role=status 'Reconnecting to SC2 Tools…' under the Dock tabs; the global ConnectionBanner from data-states-recovery never renders on /dock.

C. Wait for the real snapshot (dock-wait-for-snapshot)
- Pass studioReady (DockClient.tsx:200-203) to DockScenes (including the Timer), DockPoll, DockGoals, DockClips and BrollLibraryEditor. DockChat and BuildProfileEditor already receive it.
- Until it is ready, each card shows a skeleton with role=status 'Loading your saved controls…' instead of default-state copy such as 'No goals yet' or 'Stream is live — no scene overlay', and every write action is disabled.
- After 15 s, the skeleton reads 'Still loading your saved controls — retrying…'.
- The guards also go inside the functions, not just on the disabled buttons. DockGoals save (DockGoals.tsx:208-217, 254-257), BrollLibraryEditor's full-list save and DockClient.blockUser (:413-416, which posts [...studio.blockedUsers, user]) all return early while not ready.

D. Keep input on a failed save (dock-keep-input-on-failed-save)
- postStudioAction (DockClient.tsx:341-343) returns postStudio's Promise<StudioState|null>, and the panels' onPost type changes to match.
- Panels clear only on a non-null result. This applies to DockPoll.start (DockPoll.tsx:117-123), DockGoals clearDirty (:254-257), the DockClips VOD save (DockClips.tsx:130-133) and the DockScenes message and countdown inputs. Follow the BuildProfileEditor.tsx:66-85 pattern.
- Each panel shows a role=status confirmation inline for 3 s: 'Poll started', 'Poll closed', 'Goals saved', 'Scene set to BRB', 'VOD link saved'.
- The error banner (DockClient.tsx:451-455) gets role=alert, a Dismiss button and a Retry button. Retry re-runs the last failed action as a closure, so it re-reads the form as it is now instead of replaying a stale full list.

Edge cases:
- Switching token resets the status and snapshot.
- An 'invalid' socket never retries.
- A 401 must not loop.
- The card and badge never expose the token.

Tests:
- components/overlay/__tests__/overlayResilience.test.ts: backoff schedule; retry on 'online'; invalid → no retry.
- scenes/__tests__/OverlaySceneClient.test.tsx: resilience attached; card rendered on invalid.
- Unit test for the did-you-mean helper.
- dock/__tests__/DockClient.test.tsx: 401 → dead-link panel and no further fetches; writes disabled before the snapshot; full-list save refused before ready; Retry re-runs the action.
- DockPoll, DockGoals and DockClips tests: input kept when onPost resolves null, cleared on success.

items.spec:
These are features that are advertised or half-built but cannot be reached or undone. Depends on streamer-polish-1 (wave 1) for the studioReady gate and for onPost returning StudioState|null.

A. Build vote (mount-build-vote)

  - replace the 🗳 label with text (icons arrive in streamer-polish-4);

B. Scenes (dock-scene-modes)

  - API: apps/api/src/services/multichatStudio.js SCENE_MODES (:408) and sanitizeScene.

  - Fixtures: lib/multichat/testStudio.ts.
  - Headlines in StreamSceneWidget (StreamSceneCanvas) and SC2BackdropScene: STARTING SOON / BE RIGHT BACK / INTERMISSION / THANKS FOR WATCHING.
- Headline precedence in OverlaySceneClient.tsx:189-193: the Dock mode sets the headline and the URL variant only chooses the backdrop. With no Dock mode set, the variant's own headline shows, so /scene/intermission still reads INTERMISSION when the Dock is idle.
- DockScenes gets four buttons: Starting Soon, BRB, Intermission, Stream ending.
- 'Go live' becomes the primary/success style instead of danger (DockScenes.tsx:206-208). Going live from Starting Soon still stamps streamStartMs when it is unset (:215); 'ending' never stamps it.

  - DockClient passes the filtered messages to DockPoll (:559).

  - Matching is case-insensitive.

items.title: Dock UI pass: design-system controls, visible focus, icons, touch-size targets and collapsible, pinnable sections
items.spec:
Makes the Dock look and behave like the rest of the product.

Ordering:
- Land at the start of wave 4, before dock-game-desk, series-mode and twitch-predictions-markers add their Dock panels, so those panels are built on the new SectionCard and primitives.
- Migrate live-scouting-brief's Scout panel (wave 3) in this PR.
- This pack removes the Dock's entries from the outline-none baseline that ui-primitives-and-dialogs' uiLint ratchet (wave 5) will enforce.

A. Primitives and accessibility (dock-a11y-primitives)
- Rebuild Dock controls on components/ui Button (size sm), Input, Select and Toggle, all with focus-visible rings.
- Remove the 17 focus:outline-none inputs. DockButton (DockClient.tsx:658-671) becomes a thin wrapper over ui/Button, or is deleted.
- Replace emoji and glyphs with lucide icons plus text labels: 🔊 Read aloud→Volume2, ⏱→Timer, ⏭→SkipForward, 🔀→Shuffle, 🔇→VolumeX, ▶→Play, ⏸→Pause, ⏺→Circle, 🔥→Flame, ✕→X, and 🗳 in DockBuildVote→Vote.
- Target sizes: under @media (pointer: coarse), at least 40 px. On fine pointers (OBS custom docks are about 300 px wide and mouse-driven), a dense 28-32 px size is allowed.
- The per-message Highlight and Block buttons (DockChat.tsx:349-369) become proper targets with aria-labels such as 'Highlight message from <user>' and 'Block <user>'.
- Platform status becomes text, for example 'Twitch · connecting', instead of colour dots with only a title (DockChat.tsx:183-186).
- Robustness:
  - Wrap the localStorage read at DockClient.tsx:389 in try/catch.
  - Guard the clipboard writes (DockClient.tsx:424-429, DockClips.tsx:59). When the clipboard fails, fall back to a selected read-only input with 'Press Ctrl+C', as in WidgetExplorer.tsx:65-78. Swap to ui-primitives' CopyButton when it lands.

B. Collapsible sections (dock-collapsible-sections)
- New components/dock/SectionCard.tsx is a disclosure: a header <button aria-expanded aria-controls>.
- When collapsed, the header shows a one-line summary: 'Poll · open · 34 votes', 'Goals · 2 active', 'Scenes · BRB 3:12' or 'Scenes · Live', 'Timer · 4:59 left', 'Clips · 12 moments', 'Chat · 3 platforms', 'Highlight · pinned'.
- A collapsed section with active on-stream state (open poll, scene not live, running timer) shows a status dot.
- Each section has 'Pin to top', and there is a 'Reset layout' action.
- Open/closed state and pin order are saved per browser in lib/dockLayout.ts under localStorage key 'sc2t:dock-layout:v1' (try/catch; falls back to defaults). Default: everything expanded except the b-roll manager.
- Move the BrollLibraryEditor and JSON import behind a 'Manage b-roll' disclosure in DockScenes.
- The jump tabs (DockClient.tsx:438-449) get IntersectionObserver scroll-spy that sets aria-current on the visible section. Clicking a tab for a collapsed section expands it, then scrolls to it.
- Skeletons from streamer-polish-1 also appear in the collapsed summaries ('Loading…').

Tests:
- SectionCard toggles aria-expanded and persists the state.
- Throwing storage does not crash the Dock and uses the defaults.
- A missing clipboard shows the manual-copy fallback.
- Scroll-spy sets aria-current (mock IntersectionObserver).
- Pin reorders sections; Reset restores the defaults.
- Platform status is shown as text.
- Add an axe check of /dock in the e2e suite if one exists.

items.title: Dock live tools: timed polls with presets and one vote syntax, YouTube-chapter and CSV clip exports, and manual moment flags
items.spec:
Expands the Dock's Poll and Clips panels.

Ordering: land in wave 4 after these items, which change the same panels:
- streamer-polish-2 (filtered tally, Build vote)
- streamer-polish-4 (SectionCard, primitives)
- dock-game-desk ('Start new session' also sets studio.streamStartMs)
- sc2-moment-alerts (DockClips logs ladder moments)

A. Polls (poll-upgrades)
- Optional duration of 30 s, 1 m, 2 m or 5 m.
- API: multichatStudio.js poll sanitizing accepts durationSec from that allowlist and stamps openedAtMs and endsAtMs on the server when the poll opens. On read, a poll whose endsAtMs has passed is reported as closed, so a stream with no Dock open still closes it. The server is authoritative; clients tolerate about 2 s of clock skew.
- lib/multichat/useStudioState.ts mirrors the type and sanitizing.
- DockPoll shows a countdown and posts close at zero. The post is idempotent.
- ChatPollWidget shows '0:42 left' and switches to final results at zero.
- 'Run again' refills the form from the last poll {question, options, durationSec}, kept in state and in per-token localStorage (try/catch). It never auto-starts.
- Add POLL_PRESETS to lib/multichat/poll.ts:
  - 'Win or lose this game?' [Win, Lose]
  - 'Next opponent's race?' [Terran, Zerg, Protoss]
  - 'How long will the next game last?' [Under 10 min, 10–20 min, 20+ min]
  - 'Which build next?' switches to Build vote mode.
- Add a canonical POLL_VOTE_HINT to poll.ts ('Vote by typing the number (2) or !vote 2'). Use it in DockPoll (:85-87, :170), DockBuildVote, the ChatPollWidget footer, StreamStudioPage.tsx:58 and the chat-poll guide.

B. Clip log (clip-log-exports)
- Add pure helpers to lib/vodLinks.ts:
  - toYouTubeChapters(moments, streamStartMs) outputs '0:00 Stream start', then moments sorted by offset. It drops pre-start moments and any moment less than 10 s after the previous kept one. Times are M:SS, or H:MM:SS at one hour and above. Titles are single-line and capped at 100 characters.
  - If fewer than 3 entries remain, the button is disabled with 'YouTube needs at least 3 chapters'. With no stream-start mark it is disabled with 'Mark stream start first'.
- 'Copy timestamps' uses a single format: offsets when a mark exists, wall-clock HH:MM for everything otherwise. This fixes the mixed formats at DockClips.tsx:44-63.
- 'Download CSV': new lib/csv.ts with RFC 4180 escaping and a formula-injection guard that prefixes ' to cells starting with = + - @, because chat lines are viewer input. Reuse a CSV helper if a wave-3 item already added one. Columns: offset, wall_time_iso, kind, reason, sample_lines (joined with ' | ').
- Filter chips All / Chat / Game / Manual, plus any kinds sc2-moment-alerts adds, derived from the kinds present.
- Render the newest 100 moments with 'Show older'.
- 'Flag moment' button (lucide Flag) with an optional note of up to 80 characters:
  - New route POST /v1/multichat/:token/moment, using tokenAuth, the existing limiter and a 5 s per-token cooldown (429 'Too soon').
  - It calls recordMoment with kind 'manual'. Extend the kind allowlist at multichatEngagement.js:342-355, which today coerces every kind to game-event or chat-spike. The default reason is 'Flagged from Dock'.
  - The existing clip-moment emit updates the list live.
- 'Clear mark' (DockClips.tsx:79-84) shows an 8 s 'Stream start cleared · Undo' that restores the previous streamStartMs. Use the same Undo for dock-game-desk's reset if it overwrites a mark.

Tests:
- Chapter rules: 0:00 first, the 10 s gap, at least 3 entries, pre-start moments dropped.
- CSV escaping and the injection guard.
- Route auth, the cooldown and the 'manual' kind.
- Filters.
- Undo.
- Poll: sanitizer duration allowlist, expiry reported as closed, Run again refills without starting, presets.
- The parser accepts every syntax shown in POLL_VOTE_HINT.
- The widget countdown.
