items.title: Settings you can trust: wheel guard, honest Save message, resettable API address, remembered window
items.spec:
Scope: four small fixes to the existing desktop window. No roadmap item touches them before wave 6. agent-settings-and-first-run (wave 6) later moves these controls into ui/settings_page.py and an Advanced group, and must keep the helpers added here: _show_settings_toast, validate_api_base, install_wheel_guard/guard_value_widgets and _go_to_page. Merge before agent-gui-polish-2, because both edit gui.py.

1) Save message is accurate and survives (save-toast-overwrite)
- apps/agent/sc2tools_agent/ui/gui.py: add MainWindow._show_settings_toast(text, tone='info'|'success'|'error', ms=6000), backed by ONE QTimer (self._settings_toast_timer, single-shot, restarted on every call) that clears self._settings_status. Tone sets objectName settingsToastOk / settingsToastErr, coloured _SUCCESS / _DANGER in the global QSS.
- Route every direct self._settings_status.setText plus QTimer.singleShot clear through the helper (gui.py:2686, 2917-2922, 2927, 2969-2979, 3002-3015, 3150-3160), so an older timer can never wipe a newer message.
- _click_save_settings (gui.py ~2880-2928): set self._save_ack = False before ui._on_save_settings(payload); _on_settings_status sets it to True. If it is still False after the call, show the local baseline 'Saved.' in success tone. Delete the false 'Saved · changes apply on next start'. If log level, parse concurrency or API address differ from the loaded values, append e.g. ' Log level and API address change after you restart SC2 Tools.', naming only the fields that changed.
- runner.py:1544-1568: rephrase the apply summary for users. Plain save: 'Saved.' With a filter change: 'Saved. Syncing Season 67 only; 12 queued uploads skipped; 40 older replays will sync again.' Pluralise each part and leave out parts that are zero. The failure path (gui.py:2927) uses error tone: 'Couldn't save settings: <reason>'.
- Fix the upload-batch tooltip (gui.py:1904-1911). Replace 'Takes effect on next agent restart' with 'Applies to the next batch.' The runner hot-swaps the batch size (runner.py:1367-1378).
- Tests:
  - apps/agent/tests/test_gui.py (offscreen): a fake _on_save_settings that synchronously calls gui.show_settings_status('Saved. Syncing Season 67 only…') leaves that text visible after Save. A no-op handler gives 'Saved.'. A first toast's timer firing does not clear a second toast shown later.
  - tests/test_runner_save_settings.py: assert the new phrasing and pluralisation.

2) API address can be reset and is checked (api-base-reset)
- gui.py:2864: send self._api_input.text().strip().rstrip('/'), using an empty string rather than None when blank. runner.py:1324-1325 already maps '' to None (the default), so a blank field now resets it. Include api_base in the payload only when it differs from the loaded value.
- New ui/qt_helpers.py with a Qt-free validate_api_base(text) -> Optional[str]:
  - '' is OK.
  - https with a host is OK.
  - http is OK only for localhost, 127.0.0.1 or ::1.
  - Anything else returns 'Enter a full address starting with https://, or leave it blank to use sc2tools.com.'
- Show the error inline under the field (objectName fieldError) on editingFinished and on Save. Save aborts with the error toast 'Fix the API address before saving.' and focuses the field.
- Next to the field add:
  - 'Reset to default': clears the field; the placeholder shows the default URL.
  - 'Test': GET {url or default}/v1/health (apps/api/src/routes/health.js) on a QThreadPool runnable with a 5 s timeout. Shows 'Reachable · 142 ms', or 'Couldn't reach that address (timeout / HTTP 503 / name not found)'. The button is disabled while running, and a result is ignored if the text changed since the test started.
- Add a muted 'Needs restart' tag after the label. The 'Restart now' button comes with agent-settings-and-first-run, which owns the relaunch path.
- Tests: a validate_api_base table (blank, https host, http localhost, http remote host, 'sc2tools.com' with no scheme, ftp://). test_runner_save_settings.py: api_base='' clears state.api_base_override. GUI test: a blank field sends '' and an unchanged field sends None.

3) The mouse wheel never edits a setting by accident (settings-wheel-guard)
- Move _WheelGuard from ui/streams_page.py:18-26 into ui/qt_helpers.py as install_wheel_guard(widget, QtCore). It sets Qt.StrongFocus and installs one shared event filter that ignores Wheel events while the widget lacks focus, so the QScrollArea scrolls instead. streams_page.py imports it, with no behaviour change there.
- Add guard_value_widgets(root), called once after the Settings tab, Build check-in group and OBS card are built. It walks findChildren for QComboBox, QAbstractSpinBox and QAbstractSlider. That covers:
  - the sync range combo (gui.py:1958-1981) and its date edits (1968-1977)
  - the log level combo (2000-2002)
  - the six OBS scene combos (2318-2324)
  - both sliders (1708-1719, 1891-1900)
  - the debounce spinbox (2347-2352)
  - any future control
- Keep ObsPortSpinBox's always-ignore behaviour; tests/test_gui_obs_port.py must still pass.
- Edge cases: an open combo popup still scrolls its own list. Arrow keys still work on a focused control. Clicking a control and then wheeling changes it, which is intended.
- Tests: new apps/agent/tests/test_gui_settings_wheel.py, modelled on test_gui_obs_port.py. For each guarded widget: a QWheelEvent while unfocused leaves the value unchanged and moves the scroll area; after setFocus the wheel changes the value.

4) The window remembers its size, position and page (window-state-persist)
- state.py: add window_geometry: Optional[str] (base64 of saveGeometry) and window_page: Optional[str]. The page is a key ('dashboard', 'recent', 'log', 'settings', 'streams'), not an index, so reordering pages stays safe. from_dict/to_dict coerce junk values to None.
- gui.py: add _PAGE_KEYS and _go_to_page(key). It sets the stack index AND checks the matching nav button; today nav buttons call _stack.setCurrentIndex directly (gui.py:1215). Route nav clicks through it.
- moveEvent, resizeEvent and page changes restart a 1 s debounce timer that calls a new ui._on_window_state(geometry_b64, page_key). The runner persists it with the existing state save. Skip saving while the window is minimized or hidden.
- Restore in __init__ after resize(960, 640):
  - restoreGeometry, then clamp the frame rect with build_checkin_window.clamp_card_position(point, size, [each screen's availableGeometry], min_visible=120).
  - If that returns None, centre the window on the primary screen at 960×640. Shrink the size to the target screen's available area if needed.
  - Restore the last page, except that an unpaired agent always opens on Dashboard.
- Tests: new tests/test_gui_window_state.py: round trip; a saved x=5000 with one fake 1920×1080 screen ends up on-screen; unpaired gives dashboard; an unknown page key gives dashboard. test_state.py: junk values are coerced.

Compatibility: none of this changes upload behaviour, and agent.json files without the new keys load unchanged.
items.howto: Help center (apps/web/lib/help/articles/desktop-app.ts, rendered at /help/desktop-app-overview and in Settings > Help): add an 'API address (advanced)' callout to the desktop-app-overview article. It should say the field is only for self-hosted or development setups; leave it blank or click Reset to default to go back to sc2tools.com; Test checks the address; the change applies after restarting SC2 Tools. Inline help: helper text under the field ('Leave blank to use sc2tools.com') and the corrected upload-batch tooltip. The wheel guard, Save message and window memory need no doc.

Let a blank API base URL actually reset to the default, and guard the field

items.title: Help one click away and an Activity log you can copy errors from during a sync
items.spec:
Dependencies:
- Land after help-center-foundation and help-content-backfill (both wave 1), so /help/<slug> pages exist.
- Merge after agent-gui-polish-1, whose _go_to_page this reuses.
- agent-calm-sync (wave 2) changes which Recent rows appear and builds on the incremental insert below.
- agent-support-tools (wave 5) later adds an in-app Help page; the sidebar link added here becomes its entry point.

1) Activity log you can use during a sync (activity-log-usable). Code today: gui.py _build_logs_tab (1590-1628), _tail_log_now/_render_log (3429-3459), _matches_level (3491-3509).
- New Qt-free module apps/agent/sc2tools_agent/ui/log_records.py:
  - LogRecord(level, lines) and parse_chunk(carry, text) -> (records, new_carry).
  - A line matching ^\d{4}-\d\d-\d\dT\S+ (DEBUG|INFO|WARNING|ERROR|CRITICAL)\b starts a record. Any other line (traceback, wrapped JSON) belongs to the previous record.
  - A trailing partial line is carried to the next tick; today a half-written line is split in two.
  - matches(record, filter) replaces _matches_level, so 'Errors only' keeps the whole traceback.
- Keep records in deque(maxlen=3000); today the cap is MAX_LOG_LINES=800 lines.
- Render by appending only new matching records through a dedicated QTextCursor at the end of the document, with a QTextCharFormat per level: ERROR/CRITICAL _DANGER, WARNING amber, DEBUG _TEXT_MUTED, INFO default. Never call setPlainText on a tick, so the user's selection, caret and horizontal scroll stay put. Rebuild only when the filter changes. setMaximumBlockCount(6000).
- Seeding: the first tail seeks to max(0, size - 256 KB), skips to the next newline and shows a dim first line: '… older entries are in the log file - Open log folder'. Any later tick that finds more than 1 MB of new data does the same, so waking from sleep never freezes the GUI thread. Rotation (size < offset) keeps today's reset to 0.
- 'Follow new lines' toggle, on by default:
  - It turns off when the user scrolls up more than 4 px from the bottom or selects text.
  - While off, a pill shows '37 new lines - Jump to latest'; clicking it scrolls to the end and turns follow back on.
  - Reaching the bottom also turns it back on.
- Search: a 'Search log' box in the toolbar with a match count ('3 of 17').
  - A window-level Ctrl+F QShortcut calls _go_to_page('log') and focuses the box.
  - Enter or F3 goes to the next match, Shift+Enter or Shift+F3 to the previous one, Esc clears.
  - Case-insensitive QTextDocument.find; every hit is highlighted with ExtraSelections, and the current hit is scrolled into view, which also pauses follow.
- Copy tool-button menu: 'Copy selection' (disabled when nothing is selected) and 'Copy last 200 lines' (of the current filtered view). The button shows 'Copied ✓' for 2 s, like _copy_pairing_code. Ctrl+C keeps working.
- Filter labels become 'Everything', 'Info and above', 'Warnings and errors' and 'Errors only', with the same meaning as today.
- Public MainWindow.show_log(filter='errors', jump_to_last=True), used by agent-gui-polish-3 ('Open log' on the status card) and agent-pairing-recovery ('Open activity log' on the unreachable pairing state).
- Edge cases:
  - A missing or empty log shows the muted empty state 'Nothing logged yet'.
  - A file locked during rotation is retried on the next tick.
  - A search with no hits shows '0 matches'.

2) Recent uploads stays responsive during a bulk sync. This is the GUI-thread half of recent-uploads-history; the feature half is covered by agent-dashboard-games in wave 4.
- _on_upload_success and _on_upload_failed (gui.py:2601-2618) insert one row at index 0 with insertRow, and removeRow past MAX_RECENT. Today _refresh_recent rebuilds about 300 QTableWidgetItems on every event (gui.py:3305-3327). Full rebuilds happen only on first build.
- Coalesce _refresh_stats/_query_synced_count behind a 250 ms single-shot timer, at most 4 per second. Today count_synced scans all of state.uploaded on every upload (gui.py:2585-2606, 3290-3296). Between refreshes, the in-memory increment updates the label right away.

3) Help one click away (agent-help-entry)
- Sidebar footer (_build_sidebar, gui.py:1183-1233): a flat 'Help & support' link button above the version label. It opens {dashboard_url}/help/desktop-app-overview?src=agent through a _help_url(slug) helper built on ui._dashboard_url.
- Contextual '?' QToolButtons (20 px, round, objectName helpLink, accessible name 'Help: <topic>', tooltip 'Open help in your browser'):
  - Sync date range → desktop-app-sync-range
  - Replay folders → replay-folders
  - OBS card title → obs-auto-scene-switching
  - Build check-in title (ui/build_checkin_settings.py) → build-check-in
  - Activity log toolbar → desktop-app-activity-log
- New apps/agent/sc2tools_agent/ui/help_links.py with AGENT_HELP_SLUGS, the list of every slug the agent opens. A web test, apps/web/lib/help/__tests__/agentLinks.test.ts, holds the same list and asserts each slug resolves to an article. Comment both lists to say they must stay identical.

Tests:
- apps/agent/tests/test_log_records.py: a traceback attaches to its ERROR record; partial-line carry; the filter keeps continuation lines; text before the first record is handled.
- tests/test_gui.py:
  - A new tick leaves an existing selection unchanged.
  - Seeding a 3 MB fixture reads at most 300 KB.
  - Search count, next and previous work.
  - Follow pauses when the user scrolls up.
  - 500 synthetic upload successes in one event-loop turn call the synced-count provider at most twice before the timer fires; the table keeps 100 rows, newest first.
  - Each help button opens the expected URL (monkeypatch webbrowser.open), and every slug used is in AGENT_HELP_SLUGS.
items.howto:
This pack writes the desktop agent how-tos, in apps/web/lib/help/articles/desktop-app.ts (rendered at /help/<slug> and Settings > Help #<slug>):
- Extend 'desktop-app-overview' (created by help-content-backfill) with: the five window pages; closing the window keeps syncing in the tray, and how to quit; Pause vs Re-sync; where the logs are.
- New article 'desktop-app-sync-range' ('Choose what to sync'): pick Current season if you have years of replays; changing the range later skips queued uploads.
- New article 'desktop-app-activity-log' ('Find and copy an error'): Activity log > Errors only > Copy last 200 lines, then Report a problem. Link it from troubleshooting/my-game-didnt-show-up.
- Refresh the 'Main window - what is where' table in apps/agent/README.md: remove 'replay folder override… most apply on next start' and describe the new Activity log features and the Help link.

items.title: One honest status: the card, sidebar and tray icon say what the agent is really doing
items.spec:
Dependencies:
- Merge after these wave-2 items:
  - agent-pairing-recovery: pairing and unlinked states, pairing card.
  - agent-calm-sync: errors.classify, on_connection_state, and transient failures no longer calling on_upload_failed.
  - agent-window-tray-folders: tray.py pause broadcast and menu, describe_folder and the region helper.
- Uses show_log from agent-gui-polish-2.
- agent-calm-sync's offline/busy banner must render as this card's 'Needs attention' state, not as a second banner.
- agent-health-and-sync-health (wave 5) later feeds its HealthMonitor into derive_status and adds checklist rows under this headline. It must reuse AgentStatus, the card layout and the tray dot renderer from this pack rather than rebuild them.

1) Status model (truthful-status-card)
- New Qt-free apps/agent/sc2tools_agent/status_model.py:
  - enum AgentStatus {STARTING, CONNECTING, NEEDS_PAIRING, UNLINKED, WATCHING, SYNCING, PAUSED, NEEDS_ATTENTION, ERROR}.
  - dataclass StatusFacts: phase, boot_error, analyzer_ok, analyzer_diag, paired, unlinked, paused, connection (kind, waiting_count, next_retry_at), pending_count, terminal_failure_times, folders, filter_label, last_upload_at, update_pending.
  - derive_status(facts, now) -> StatusView(status, badge_text, tone, headline, cause, action, secondary_action). Actions are retry, resume, open_settings, open_log, pair_again, view_failed, copy_details or None.
  - Priority, highest first: boot error > analyzer failed > unlinked > needs pairing > paused > offline/busy > 3 or more terminal failures in 10 min > no folders > syncing (pending > 0) > watching > connecting > starting.
- Copy for each state (headline / cause / action):
  - Starting: 'Starting SC2 Tools…'.
  - Connecting: 'Connecting to sc2tools.com…'.
  - Needs pairing: 'Link this PC to your account' / 'Use the code below.'
  - Unlinked: 'This PC was unlinked from your account' / action: Link again.
  - Watching: 'Watching 3 folders (NA, EU)' / 'Last upload 3 min ago' (or 'Waiting for your next game') / link: Manage → Settings.
  - Syncing: 'Syncing 12 replays' / 'Uploads run in the background.'
  - Paused: 'Sync paused' / 'New replays wait until you resume.' / action: Resume.
  - Needs attention, offline or busy: 'Can't reach sc2tools.com' / '312 replays waiting · retrying in 30 s' / action: Retry now.
  - Needs attention, failures: '5 uploads failed in the last 10 minutes' / the newest failure's friendly title / action: View failed uploads (goes to Recent uploads).
  - Needs attention, no folders: 'No replay folder found' / 'Add your StarCraft II Replays folder.' / action: Open Settings.
  - Error, boot: 'SC2 Tools couldn't start syncing' / the first line of the exception, at most 140 chars / actions: Open log, then Copy details.
  - Error, analyzer: 'Replays can't be read right now' / 'The replay analyzer failed to load; new games wait until it does.' / actions: Open log, then Copy details.
- Badge tones: neutral for starting and connecting; ok green for watching; info cyan for syncing (add a badgeInfo QSS rule); warn amber for pairing, unlinked, paused and needs attention; err red for error. The filter chip ('· Season 67 only') stays on the headline.
- runner.py: keep ui.on_status(text) for console and tray text, and add structured _Multiplexer events:
  - on_phase(phase, detail=''): 'connecting' at runner.py:396/836, 'waiting_pairing' at 839, 'ready' at 1058, 'boot_error' with str(exc) at 1070.
  - on_analyzer_probe(ok, diag), after probe_analyzer (runner.py:858-864); today a failure is only logged.
  - GuiUI, TrayUI and ConsoleUI implement both (the console prints them).
- Delete the substring classifier _classify_status (gui.py:3214-3225).
- gui.py _refresh_status_card renders the StatusView:
  - badge, headline, cause;
  - one primary action button, hidden when the action is None;
  - an optional secondary 'Copy details', which copies the version, status, exception or probe diagnostic, and the last 20 ERROR log lines.
- Remove 'API: <host>' and the bullet list of folder paths from the secondary line (gui.py:3240-3261). Folders read 'Watching 3 folders (NA, EU) · Manage', with the full paths in the tooltip; the region comes from describe_folder, or '?' when unknown. The API host remains only in Settings and later in Diagnostics.
- The sidebar status (gui.py:1223-1226) shows '● <badge> · <headline>' elided to one line, with the full text as tooltip.
- Terminal upload failures: _on_upload_failed appends a timestamp. A 30 s timer prunes timestamps older than 10 min, so the state clears itself. A success does not reset the list.
- While NEEDS_PAIRING or UNLINKED, hide the stats row and disable Pause, Re-sync and Add folder (gui.py:1235-1252, 1444-1527); Open dashboard stays enabled. This is the early slice of first-run-setup.
- The update banner stays separate (agent-match-aware owns its content). Transient notices never replace the headline.

2) Tray icon (tray-icon-status). Code today: ui/tray.py _load_icon_image (142-150), gui.py:1088-1091.
- Replace ui/tray_icon.png (2 MB, 1347×1133) with a square 256×256 transparent PNG of the same logo, padded rather than stretched, under 80 KB.
- Keep a runtime guard, _square_pad(img), that centres any non-square image on a transparent square canvas before resizing.
- Window icon: a QIcon built from the same square PNG at 16/24/32/48/64/256 px. Confirm packaging/sc2tools_agent.spec still bundles the file (tests/test_packaging_smoke.py).
- render_tray_image(base, dot) draws a 20 px dot with a 3 px dark ring at the bottom-right of the 64 px image:
  - green: WATCHING
  - cyan: SYNCING
  - amber: PAUSED, NEEDS_PAIRING, UNLINKED, NEEDS_ATTENTION
  - red: ERROR
  - blue: an update is ready and the state is otherwise WATCHING
  - no dot: STARTING, CONNECTING
- Cache one image per colour and reassign icon.icon only when the colour changes. icon.title becomes 'SC2 Tools - <headline>'. TrayUI receives on_status_view(view) through _Multiplexer.
- Put the colours in a shared ui/palette.py constants module imported by gui.py and tray.py; tray stays Qt-free.

3) Tests
- New apps/agent/tests/test_status_model.py, a decision table:
  - boot error while the status text says 'watching' gives ERROR, not Active;
  - 'connecting...' gives CONNECTING;
  - 2 failures give WATCHING; 3 within 10 min give NEEDS_ATTENTION; failures older than 10 min expire;
  - paused beats offline;
  - analyzer failure gives ERROR;
  - no folders gives NEEDS_ATTENTION.
- test_gui.py: the card shows the exception text; the secondary line contains no 'API:'; while unpaired the stats are hidden and Re-sync is disabled; 'Open log' calls show_log('errors').
- test_tray.py:
  - a 1347×1133 fixture keeps its aspect ratio: the non-transparent bounding-box ratio is within 3% of the original;
  - the dot pixel colour matches each state;
  - icon.icon is reassigned only when the colour changes.
items.howto: New help article 'What the status lights mean' (slug desktop-app-status, in apps/web/lib/help/articles/desktop-app.ts, Settings > Help #desktop-app-status). It has a table of every badge (Starting, Connecting, Link this PC, Watching, Syncing, Paused, Needs attention, Error) with what it means and what to click, plus the tray dot colours. agent-health-and-sync-health later extends the same slug. Add the slug to AGENT_HELP_SLUGS and put a '?' link on the status card. Update the Dashboard row in apps/agent/README.md, which still lists 'Status badge (Active / Paused / Pairing / Error)'.

Fix the stretched tray icon and show status on it

items.title: Build check-in cards: preview them, reset their position, and type, Enter, Ctrl+Enter to check in
items.spec:
Dependencies:
- Lands in wave 3 after agent-private-scouting-card, which reworks LoadingCardModel and adds a 'Show scouting at loading' toggle to Settings > Build check-in. The preview reuses that model, so streamers also see the scouting strip.
- agent-practice-hud (wave 6) reuses the placement helpers, so keep the position reset generic over card kinds.
- build_checkin/controller.py business logic is not changed.

1) Preview mode (ui/build_checkin_settings.py, ui/build_checkin_window.py, ui/build_checkin_cards.py)
- New apps/agent/sc2tools_agent/build_checkin/preview.py:
  - sample_loading_model(race) and sample_postgame_model() build LoadingCardModel and PostgameCardModel from fixed sample data.
  - Sample data: three featured builds for the matchup (for ZvP: '12 Pool', 'Hatch First', 'Roach-Ravager'), opponent 'PreviewOpponent', map 'Alcyone', and a sample scouting strip once that model exists.
  - The race is the player's last known race from state, else ZvP.
- BuildCheckinHost.show_preview(kind) shows the card with preview=True:
  - A header chip reads 'Preview - nothing is saved'.
  - Every action (pick, confirm, later, add build, not now) goes to a local handler that only closes the card. The controller and the API are never called.
  - Dragging works, and the position is remembered exactly as for a real card; that is the point of the preview.
  - The preview closes after 90 s or on Esc.
  - A real loading or post-game card replaces the preview immediately.
- Settings > Build check-in gets a 'Cards' row:
  - 'Preview loading card' and 'Preview after-game card';
  - 'Reset card positions';
  - a link 'Open check-in queue on sc2tools.com' using web_queue_url(dashboard_url), as the tray already does (runner.py:1852-1859).
  - The preview buttons work even when check-ins are off, with the hint 'Check-ins are off; this is only a preview'.
- Reset card positions:
  - Clears AgentState.build_checkin_card_positions (state.py:266) and BuildCheckinHost._positions, and persists.
  - Moves any visible card to its default spot.
  - Shows 'Positions reset' next to the button for 3 s.

2) Search keyboard flow (ui/build_checkin_widgets.py:536-543, BuildList)
- search.returnPressed checks the first visible build row in display order (featured, then more) and moves focus to it. With no match, Enter does nothing and the existing empty hint stays.
- Down in the search box focuses the first visible row; Up on the first row returns to the search box.
- Ctrl+Enter still confirms from anywhere in the card, so type, Enter, Ctrl+Enter completes a check-in. Esc is unchanged.
- Edge case: the cards still never take focus from the game on their own; these keys apply only after the user clicks into a card.

3) Tests
- test_build_checkin_ui_settings.py: the preview buttons call host.show_preview with the right kind; Reset clears and persists positions; the queue link URL is correct.
- test_build_checkin_ui_cards.py:
  - preview card actions never call the controller (a fake controller records zero calls);
  - a real card replaces an open preview;
  - after filtering, Enter checks the first visible match; Enter with no matches does nothing; Down focuses the first row.

items.title: Guided tours that can't go stale: Today, your first game breakdown, and Overlay settings
items.why: Owner request: short tours help first-time players, as long as they never point at a screen that has moved.
items.spec:
1) components/ui/Tour.tsx: steps target [data-tour='id'] elements, a spotlight cut-out plus an InfoTip-style card with Next, Back, Skip and a 'Step n of N' counter. It has a focus trap, Esc to close, scrollIntoView, and falls back to a bottom sheet under 640px. Under reduced motion it skips animation, and when a target is missing it skips that step instead of breaking. 2) lib/tours.ts holds the definitions (3 tours, 4-5 steps each, every final step linking to a help article). 3) Triggers: Today tour when games.total > 0 and 'today' is not in onboarding.toursDone; Game tour on the first GameDetailPage visit; Overlay tour on the first visit to the Overlay tab. 4) Completion and skips are written to onboarding.toursDone (merge PUT). 5) The Help center gets a 'Take a tour' list with replay buttons that navigate and start the tour. 6) No tours on mobile analyzer tables, where the help drawer is used instead.

Keeping tours from going stale (the reason this was set aside):
- Every step targets a stable data-tour id, and lib/tours.ts is the only registry. Each tour step names the component that renders its target.
- A vitest per tour renders each target component with fixture data and fails if any step's data-tour id is missing, so a layout change that removes a target fails CI instead of shipping a broken tour.
- At runtime a missing target skips its step. If more than half the steps are missing the tour does not start at all, and the 'Take a tour' list hides it.
- Each tour has a version; bumping it after a redesign re-offers the tour once, otherwise tours never re-trigger on their own.
- Tours never cover the build check-in card or modals, and never start while a dialog is open.
- Ships with or after glossary-and-infotip and level-up-checklist (wave 5), reusing their InfoTip card style; the checklist links 'Take the Today tour'.
items.howto: Help article /help/take-a-tour (lists the tours with replay buttons). Each tour's last step links to /help/reading-your-stats, /help/your-first-game or the Stream Studio crash course. Help articles live under apps/web/lib/help/articles (one file per article); add 'take-a-tour' in getting-started.

items.title: Channel-point reward actions: map a Twitch reward to a stream action
items.why: Owner request: the follow-up to native Twitch Predictions (twitch-predictions-markers, wave 4).
items.spec:
Builds on twitch-predictions-markers (wave 4), which ships native Predictions. This item adds only the channel-point reward half of the original proposal:
 a table mapping reward title to one action from a fixed allowlist (re-roll randomizer for next game, start build vote, pin the redeemer's message, fire session recap, play b-roll, read input via TTS). Actions run server-side through existing studio actions on the EventSub redemption, with optional auto-fulfil or refund.

Consent and safety:
- Ask for the extra Twitch permission (channel:manage:redemptions) only when the streamer turns on reward actions, in its own connect step after Predictions.
- Actions come from a fixed allowlist and run through existing studio actions server-side; each mapping has an on/off switch, a per-viewer cooldown and an optional auto-refund when the action can't run (offline, game not live).
- A small activity log in Settings shows the last 20 redemptions and what they triggered.
- Tests: scope request only on opt-in, allowlist enforcement, cooldown, refund on failure, EventSub signature checks reuse the existing verifier.
items.howto: Add a Settings > Help 'Viewer engagement' subsection 'Twitch Predictions & channel points'. Note the Twitch mirror in the lib/streamStudioLearn.ts chat-oracle guide. Update the OfficialPlatformConnections Twitch coverage copy.

items.title: Visual layout editor for the All-in-one overlay (landscape and vertical)
items.why: Owner request: arrange every widget on one canvas instead of placing OBS sources by hand; vertical layouts for TikTok/Shorts streams.
items.spec:
Add Settings → Overlay → Look → Layout: a scaled 1920×1080 canvas (toggle to 1080×1920) with a translucent SC2 HUD safe-zone mask (minimap bottom-left, command card bottom-right, resources and supply top-right) and draggable widget ghosts rendered with playground fixtures. Support snap-to-8 px grid, per-widget scale, z-order and 'Reset to default'. Keyboard: focus a widget, use arrows (Shift for 10 px). Save profile.layout {[widgetId]: {anchor:'top'|'bottom', xPct, yPct, scale}} through the overlay profile endpoint. WidgetShell accepts a placement override from config and falls back to SLOT_STYLE. The All-in-one URL supports ?canvas=vertical, which selects profile.layoutVertical.

Built after overlay-profile-sync, widget-playground and widget-manager-redesign (wave 4): it saves through the live overlay profile (no URL re-copy), previews with the playground fixtures, and the per-widget drag-into-OBS cards stay available for streamers who prefer separate sources. Vertical layout ships in the same item (profile.layoutVertical, ?canvas=vertical).

items.title: Build randomizer for everyone (no OBS needed), plus a randomizer challenge scoreboard
items.why: Owner request: players who do not stream want the randomizer and a challenge to work through their build pool.
items.spec:
API:
- In buildIntentLive, when the pool for the matchup is enabled and no overlay randomizer widget is connected, roll on the server.
- Port lib/randomizer/engine.ts (weighted pick plus mulberry32 seeded by seedFromString(gameKey)) to JS, with parity fixtures.
- Record the roll on the build_intent_live document and send it to the agent as the pending roll. The overlay path is unchanged, and the first roll wins.

Agent:
- The loading card's randomizer strip shows the rolled build with 'Play it' (declares it), 'Reroll' (one per game, recorded) and 'Not now'.
- New setting: 'Roll on the desktop card when I'm not streaming', stored in the randomizer prefs.

Web:
- A 'Challenge' panel in Settings → Randomizer and a section on /practice.
- Per-pool table: times rolled, played as rolled, W-L, last played.
- Pool-completion progress.
- A 'Reset challenge' button that stores challengeStartedAt in the prefs.
- Data comes from a new GET /v1/build-intents/randomizer-stats, aggregated over slim rows where buildIntent.randomizer is set.

Keeping the live build-intent path safe (the reason this was set aside):
- Server-side rolling happens only when the player turned on 'Roll on the desktop card when I'm not streaming' AND no overlay randomizer is connected for the game; otherwise the existing overlay path is untouched.
- The roll is written through the existing roll write on build_intent_live (verified pool, ROLL_MAX_WRITES, first roll wins), so check-in, the OBS hold and binding behave exactly as today; add regression tests for the hold, declare-before-roll and roll-then-declare paths.
- JS engine parity with lib/randomizer/engine.ts is pinned by shared fixtures.
- The agent change ships in a normal agent release with the controller tests extended.
items.howto: Extend the 'Build randomizer' paragraph in Settings > Help #build-check-in, add a /builds/learn section 'Randomize your practice', and update the randomizer entry in lib/streamStudioLearn.ts so its 'needs' list makes OBS optional. Use the help center article build-check-in (apps/web/lib/help/articles/builds/build-check-in.ts) and add a 'randomizer' article.

items.title: Real-data social proof on the landing page: live counts, what's winning, fresh community builds, latest answered review
items.why: Owner request: show visitors the product is alive, using only real data.
items.spec:
Add a server section <LiveFromTheLadder /> between OutcomeRail and the Analyze chapter. Each part is wrapped in Suspense with a null fallback so a slow API never blocks the page, and it is ISR revalidate 3600. It has (a) a stat row from a new cheap aggregate GET /v1/site/totals: estimatedDocumentCount of games, count of published community builds, count of answered reviews, and the guides corpus size from the latest guide_stats run doc. It is cached in-process for 1 h and sent as 'public, s-maxage=3600'. (b) "Climbing this week": the top 3 guide builds with the largest positive week-over-week trend (TrendBadge already exists), linking to their guides. (c) "Fresh from the community": 3 CommunityBuildCards from the top-this-week sort. (d) "Latest answered review": one ReviewCard when the reviews rollout is on. Each block hides when its data is missing (the "ALL DATA IS REAL" rule). Numbers are rounded down to friendly thresholds ("12,400+ games analyzed") with a footnote link explaining how they're counted.

Avoiding weak-looking numbers (the reason this was set aside):
- Each block renders only above a minimum (e.g. games analyzed >= 10,000, published community builds >= 25, answered reviews >= 10); thresholds live in one config and the block hides below them, so early numbers never read as weak.
- Served from the edge cache built by public-pages-seo-and-cache (wave 5) with on-demand purge, so it adds no load to the single API instance.
items.howto: A "How we count these" footnote on the landing section links to /help/how-we-count (public Help Center), or to a short explanation on /donate until /help ships.

items.title: Follow a player's camera and see where their attention went
items.why: Owner request: camera follow in the replay and an attention breakdown before each fight.
items.spec:
Engine (core/map_playback_data.py): read sc2reader CameraEvent per player (load game events during playback extraction if not already loaded), downsample to 1 Hz with a ≥2-world-unit change threshold, and emit camera:{me:[t,x,y…flat], opp:[…]} (~10 KB for a 20-minute game).

Agent: _compact_map_playback passes it through and slice_playback windows it.

Web:
- The sanitizer accepts optional `camera` (additive).
- ReplaySettings 'Camera: Free / Follow you / Follow opponent': the view centre lerps to the camera at POV zoom, and the other player's screen is drawn as a faint rectangle.
- An AttentionCard computes % time near own army centroid vs own townhalls, 'looked away' before each fight (camera not within 20 units of the fight in the prior 5 s), and a 64×64 heatmap over the map art.

Release plan (the reason this was set aside):
- Ships in ONE engine + agent release together with unit-trades-and-exact-supply and hotkey-habits, so players update once.
- Older games: the reanalysis-center (wave 5) gets a 'Add camera data' batch so players can backfill past games from the desktop app; games without camera data show the replay normally with a one-line note and a link to that action.
- Built after replayer-studio so the Camera control sits in its vision-mode toolbar.
items.howto: Help article 'Follow camera and attention' (slug game-page-camera, category game-page), including the note that older games need a re-sync with the updated desktop app.

items.title: Hotkey and camera habits: control groups, camera saves and screen switching
items.why: Owner request: show control-group and camera-hotkey habits with clear, rule-based callouts.
items.spec:
Agent:
- Also run extract_behavior_signature and extract_camera_signature for my_pid over the whole game.
- Emit a compact `myMechanics` into macroBreakdown (game_details): per group slot sets, recalls and recalls/min; camera saves per slot and returns/min; selection changes/min; queued-command share; all per phase.
- Stamp `groupsUsed` and `cameraReturnsPerMin` on the slim row so leaguePercentiles can benchmark them later.

Web, a 'Hotkeys' sub-tab in MechanicsPanel:
- A 0-9 key strip heat-shaded by recalls/min, with unused groups dimmed.
- A camera-slot strip and a screen-switch rate.
- Rule-based callouts with fixed thresholds, e.g. 'No camera locations saved' or 'Group 4 never recalled after 6:00'.

Macro tab: a trend card for groups used and camera returns over time.

Copy always says 'logical actions recorded in the replay', never key presses.

Ships in the same engine + agent release as unit-trades-and-exact-supply and camera-follow-and-attention, so the new my-side payload is added once. Older games backfill through the reanalysis-center batch.
items.howto: Help article 'Hotkey and camera habits' (slug hotkey-habits, category game-page), explaining that replays record logical actions, not physical keys (matching the play_signature.py docstring). Also a Settings > Help 'Dashboard & analyzer' subsection.

items.title: Coaching Locker on the main app stack, one view at a time, with no data loss
items.why: Owner request: bring the Locker onto the same React components as the rest of the coaching workspace.
items.spec:
Phase 2 of coaching-one-stack (phase 1 is coaching-prep-digest).

- Port the Locker views one at a time (Roster/Students, then Shelf library, then Worksheets, then Content studio) to React with components/ui (Card, Modal, Tabs, Toast, ConfirmDialog).
- Keep the same /v1/coaching/state compare-and-set document and backup format.
- Put each ported view behind a flag and remove its HTML from the template.
- Delete LockerHost when nothing is left.

Phase 3: move Locker alerts into the shared NotificationsService.

Data safety (the reason this was set aside):
- One view per PR, in order: Roster/Students, Shelf library, Worksheets, Content studio. Each sits behind its own flag with the HTML view kept until the React view has been used for a week.
- Same /v1/coaching/state compare-and-set document and the same backup format; no schema change.
- Before the first write from a ported view, the app takes an automatic Locker backup; a 'Restore previous version' action exists in each ported view.
- Round-trip tests load fixture exports of real Locker state shapes, edit through the React view, and assert nothing else in the document changed.
- Flags can be flipped back per view without a deploy.

items.title: Battle report for every game: a 1-4 paragraph story of the match with captioned map snapshots
items.why: Owner request: an old-school battle report for each replay, entertaining to read and accurate to what happened.
items.spec:
Built without AI: a deterministic, rules-based story engine (no LLM, no model API). Every sentence is filled only from facts in this game's data, so nothing is invented, and the same game always reads the same way.

1) Facts (apps/web/lib/battleReport/facts.ts): one pure function turns the game page's existing data into a typed StoryFacts object. It uses no new server endpoint and adds no server cost. Inputs:
- result, length, map, matchup and both players' names, races and MMR;
- the planned build from build check-in versus what the replay was classified as, and the opponent's classified opener;
- key timings: expansions, first tech, first attack and upgrades;
- the fight ledger and lead timeline from game-story-fight-ledger: each engagement's time, place, army value traded and supply swing, the biggest lead swing (the turning point), and comebacks;
- macro moments from the macro report: supply blocks, idle production and worker counts;
- base trades and the end condition (GG, all buildings lost).
Every fact carries its game time so the text can link to it.

2) Story plan (lib/battleReport/plan.ts): picks 1 to 4 paragraphs by game length and how eventful the game was. A short all-in gets 1 paragraph; a long macro game with swings gets 4.
- Setting: map, matchup, the players, and what each went for. The check-in plan versus the classified build gives lines like "planned a 2-gate blink but the scouting said otherwise".
- The middle game: timings, the first clash, expansions and tech.
- The turning point: the biggest swing from the fight ledger, told as the climax, with comeback framing when the lead flipped.
- Aftermath: result and duration, a 'man of the match' stat, and one rule-based lesson from the macro leaks ("three supply blocks before 6:00 cost about 40 seconds of production").

3) Writing (lib/battleReport/phrasebank/*.ts): large template banks per beat and per tone, with typed slots. Race and unit flavour comes from data (Zerg "the swarm", Protoss "the Golden Armada", Terran "the bio ball"). Variety comes from a seeded pick (seed = gameId) without repeats inside one report, plus synonym sets for verbs and adjectives. A generated headline ("The Siege of Alcyone", "Twelve Pool at Dawn") is drawn from map, matchup and story-shape templates.
Tones:
- Battle report (default): classic war-correspondent style, dateline, past tense.
- Caster: excited esports play-by-play.
- Tactical: dry, staff-officer summary.
Copy follows the site's voice: no slurs, no mocking the opponent by name, and the opponent's name only as it appears in the replay.

4) Snapshots (components/battleReport/BattleSnapshot.tsx): render 2 to 4 still frames from the existing map playback data at the story's key moments (first clash, turning point, decisive fight, the end). Each frame shows map art, both sides' units as dots in race colours, a fight marker and a timestamp caption. Clicking a frame seeks the replay to that moment, using one-game-clock where it has shipped. Frames use the replay stage's canvas renderer.
For games without playback data, the frame is the army-value chart cropped around that moment, with a note that map snapshots need the desktop app's map data.

5) UI on /app/game/[id]: a 'Battle report' section near the top.
- Headline, a dateline (map · date · length), the paragraphs set in the editorial display face with a drop cap, and snapshot figures placed between paragraphs. Every timestamp in the text is a link that seeks the replay.
- Controls: a tone switcher, 'Copy text' (plain text or Markdown with timestamps), and a 'How this is written' note: generated from the replay's events with fixed rules, never AI.
- Works at phone width, in light and dark, and with screen readers (snapshots have text alternatives describing the moment).

6) Quality gates (vitest):
- A fixture corpus of at least 12 real game shapes: all-in, cheese loss, macro win, comeback, base trade, short GG, each matchup.
- Snapshot tests of the generated text for each fixture and tone.
- A template lint that fails on any slot a fact can't fill and on any banned word.
- A variety test over 200 seeded synthetic games: no sentence appears in more than a set share of reports, and no report repeats a template.
- A truthfulness test: every number in the text matches a fact.
items.howto: Help article 'Battle reports' (slug battle-reports, category game-page, one file under apps/web/lib/help/articles/game-page/). It explains what the report covers, that it is written by fixed rules from the replay's events and never by AI, the three tones, what the snapshots show and why some games show a chart instead, and how to copy it. Linked from the 'How this is written' note with <HelpLink>.

items.title: Share a battle report: public report page, link preview card with headline and snapshot, and image export
items.why: Owner request: battle reports are made to be shared with friends, on Discord and on stream.
items.spec:
Builds on battle-report (wave 3) and per-game-share-link (wave 6).
- The public shared-game page (per-game-share-link) shows the battle report when the owner shares the game. It is revocable along with the link.
- A dynamic Open Graph image (app/.../opengraph-image.tsx, edge-cached via public-pages-seo-and-cache) shows the headline, matchup, result and the turning-point snapshot, so links unfurl nicely on Discord and Twitter.
- 'Save as image': renders the report (headline, first paragraph, 2 snapshots) to a PNG in the browser with canvas and hands it over through the browser's normal save.
- discord-posts (wave 6) can include the headline and first paragraph when posting a result.
- No server-side generation: text and frames are produced in the browser from data the share page already loads.
items.howto: Extend the 'Battle reports' help article with a 'Share a report' section (link, preview card, image) and how to revoke.

dropped.why: Renaming files breaks the agent's path-keyed state (state.py path_by_game_id, which accurate-playback requests use). A copy-only version adds little, because server downloads already have descriptive names (replayDownloadFilename) and export-center's replay packs apply a filename template.

Each lookup costs upstream SC2Pulse calls from the single Render instance, and it is L effort for impact 3. dossier-upgrade, live-scouting-v2 and the pre-game note path cover repeat opponents, which are the common case.

Deferred. XL scope: invites, per-member consent, moderation and cross-user queries, with real privacy risk. Cheaper social loops (discord-posts, public-player-page, per-game-share-link) ship first; revisit when there is demand.
Deferred. It needs ongoing volunteer human translators and an extracted string catalog first. appearance-and-formats lays the locale groundwork, and machine translation is off the table.
Deferred. There is no Mac hardware to test on, notarisation needs a paid Apple account, and Mac players already have browser Folder Sync and /try. Revisit if Mac demand shows up in support reports.

deferred.why: Bot Lab (/bot-lab) drives locally trained bot models, which is AI. It is also an admin-only, env-gated developer page. The roadmap's critic (discovery.json critic notes) explicitly ruled 'It is AI, so propose nothing for it', and no roadmap item touches it. Only the owner ever sees it, and the audit rates it impact 2, so a design-system rebuild with a W-L tally and Play again is not worth a PR. Revisit only if Bot Lab becomes user-facing.
